- Yorùbá Question: Irú ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ wo ni wọ́n ń bèèrè fún?
- English Question: What kind of State practice is required?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Títàn káàkiri, ìṣesí àṣetẹ̀léra àti ìkan náà, tó ní àpapọ̀ àwọn ìṣesí àti àwọn àyọkúrò. | B) Àwọn ìṣesí tó tàn káàkiri, àṣetẹ̀léra àti ìṣọ̀kan nìkan tí kìí ṣe àyọkúrò àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀  | C) Ìṣesí tó tàn káàkiri àti àyọkúrò àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ṣùgbọ́n kò pan dandan kó jẹ́ àṣetẹ̀léra tàbí ìkan náà  | D) Ìṣesí àṣetẹ̀léra àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ díẹ̀, tó fi mọ́ àpapọ ìṣesí àti àyọkúrò, tí wọ́n pàdé rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ìfẹ̀hónúhàn láti àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ mìíràn 
- Options (English): A) Widespread, consistent and uniform practice, consisting both of acts and omissions. | B) Only widespread, consistent and uniform acts and not omissions of States | C) Widespread acts and omissions of States but not necessarily consistent or uniform | D) Consistent practice of few States, including both acts and omissions, which is met with protestation by the other States
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Títàn káàkiri, ìṣesí àṣetẹ̀léra àti ìkan náà, tó ní àpapọ̀ àwọn ìṣesí àti àwọn àyọkúrò.
- Verified Answer (English): A) Widespread, consistent and uniform practice, consisting both of acts and omissions.

search_context: Àwọn àdéhùn wo ni wọ́n ń rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi 'orísun òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè' lábẹ́ abala ìwé òfin Àjọ ICJ 38? | Which treaties are considered as 'source of international law' under article 38 ICJ Statute? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Àwọn àdéhùn wo ni wọ́n ń rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi 'orísun òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè' lábẹ́ abala ìwé òfin Àjọ ICJ 38?
- English Question: Which treaties are considered as 'source of international law' under article 38 ICJ Statute?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Gbogbo àdéhùn tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ ní àsìkò àríyànjiyàn náà  | B) Àwọn àdéhùn tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ tó sì wà lórí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ tó wà nínú àríyànjiyàn náà nìkan  | C) Gbogbo àdéhùn tí wọ́n ti parí láàrín àwọn ẹgbẹ́ tí wọ́n wà nínú àríyànjiyàn, tí kò níṣe pẹ̀lú bóyá wọ́n ń ṣiṣẹ́  | D) Àwọn àdéhùn tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọlọ́pọ̀ ènìyàn tí wọ́n sì ní àpẹẹrẹ pàtàkì jùlọ 
- Options (English): A) All treaties that are in force at the time of the dispute | B) Only the treaties that are in force and binding upon the parties to the dispute | C) All treaties that have been concluded between the parties to the dispute, regardless whether they are in force | D) Only treaties that are multilateral and of paramount significance
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Àwọn àdéhùn tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ tó sì wà lórí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ tó wà nínú àríyànjiyàn náà nìkan 
- Verified Answer (English): B) Only the treaties that are in force and binding upon the parties to the dispute

search_context: Kínni 'gbólóhùn; wọ̀fún' nínú Ìwe òfin Àjọ ICJ? | What is the 'optional; clause' in the ICJ Statute? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni 'gbólóhùn; wọ̀fún' nínú Ìwe òfin Àjọ ICJ?
- English Question: What is the 'optional; clause' in the ICJ Statute?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Gbólóhùn wọ̀fún jẹ́ gbólóhùn nínú ìwé òfin Àjọ ICJ, tó ń ṣe ìpèsè fún òfin aṣeélò, gẹ́gẹ́ bíi èrò àwọn ẹgbẹ́ náà  | B) Gbólóhùn wọ̀fún máa ń sọ èro àwọn ẹgbẹ́ láti gbà pé ìpinnu Ilé ẹjọ́ ni yóò jẹ́ òpin tí yóò sì wà lórí wọn  | C) Gbólóhùn wọ̀fún jẹ́ ìkéde tí Ìpínlẹ̀ kan fi pamọ́, tó ṣe wí pé ó gbà ìdájọ́ ilé ẹjọ́ ní èyí tí níṣe pẹ̀lú òfin àríyànjiyàn ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ní àjọṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú Ìpínlẹ̀ mìíràn tí ó gba irú ojúṣe yìí kan náà. | D) Gbólóhùn wọ̀fún jẹ́ gbólóhùn tí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ náà ń fi pamọ́, tí ó ń ṣe àlàkalẹ̀ ìlànà àwọn ìjírẹ̀bẹ̀ kíkọ àti ti ẹnu 
- Options (English): A) Optional clause is the clause in the ICJ Statute, which provides for the applicable law, according to the intention of the parties | B) Optional clause determines the intention of the parties to accept that the decision of the Court will be final and binding | C) Optional clause is the declaration deposited by a State, whereby it accepts the jurisdiction of the Court in respect of international legal disputes in relation to any other State accepting the same obligation. | D) Optional clause is the clause that the parties deposit, which sets out the procedure of the written and oral pleadings
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Gbólóhùn wọ̀fún jẹ́ ìkéde tí Ìpínlẹ̀ kan fi pamọ́, tó ṣe wí pé ó gbà ìdájọ́ ilé ẹjọ́ ní èyí tí níṣe pẹ̀lú òfin àríyànjiyàn ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ní àjọṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú Ìpínlẹ̀ mìíràn tí ó gba irú ojúṣe yìí kan náà.
- Verified Answer (English): C) Optional clause is the declaration deposited by a State, whereby it accepts the jurisdiction of the Court in respect of international legal disputes in relation to any other State accepting the same obligation.

search_context: Ṣé ìwa ipá tí àwọn tí wọn ò kì ń ṣe òṣìṣẹ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ ṣe lè di ìdigun kọlù lábẹ́ Abala ìwé òfin 51 ti UN Charter? | Can armed violence perpetrated by non-State actors ever amount to an armed attack under Article 51 UN Charter? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ṣé ìwa ipá tí àwọn tí wọn ò kì ń ṣe òṣìṣẹ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ ṣe lè di ìdigun kọlù lábẹ́ Abala ìwé òfin 51 ti UN Charter?
- English Question: Can armed violence perpetrated by non-State actors ever amount to an armed attack under Article 51 UN Charter?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìṣesí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ tí kìí ṣe ti ìpínlẹ̀ ò lè yọrí sí ìdigun kọlù láéláé  | B) Ìpẹ̀jọ́ Caroline dúró gẹ́gẹ́ bí ohun ìṣáájú pé àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ tí kìí ṣe ti ìpínlẹ̀ lè dáràn ìdigun kọlù lábẹ́ àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan | C) Kò sí ohun ìṣáájú nínú òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè fún ìdábàá wí pé àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ tí kìí ṣe ti ìpínlẹ̀ lè dáràn ìdigun kọlù  | D) Àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ tí kìí ṣe ti ìpínlẹ̀ lè dáràn ìdigun kọlù wọ́n sì ní ẹ̀tọ́ fún ìdáàbòbò ara ẹni lábẹ́ òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè 
- Options (English): A) The conduct of non-State actors can never amount to an armed attack | B) The Caroline case serves as precedent that non-State actors can under particular circumstances commit an armed attack | C) There is no precedent in international law for the proposition that non-State actors can commit an armed attack | D) Non-State can both commit an armed attack and possess a right of self-defence under international law
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Ìpẹ̀jọ́ Caroline dúró gẹ́gẹ́ bí ohun ìṣáájú pé àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ tí kìí ṣe ti ìpínlẹ̀ lè dáràn ìdigun kọlù lábẹ́ àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan
- Verified Answer (English): B) The Caroline case serves as precedent that non-State actors can under particular circumstances commit an armed attack

search_context: Èwo nínú àwọn gbólóhùn wọ̀nyìí ni kò péye? | Which of the following statements is inaccurate? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Èwo nínú àwọn gbólóhùn wọ̀nyìí ni kò péye?
- English Question: Which of the following statements is inaccurate?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì jẹ́ ọ̀na kan láti ṣe ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì ẹ̀tọ́ àwọn ènìyàn tako ìdáàbòbò àwùjọ lápapọ̀  | B) Fún ìṣesí kan láti wà ní ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì, wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ so ó pọ̀ mọ́ èròngbà àìbófinmu ìpínlẹ̀ náà àwọn òdiwọ̀n tí wọ́n ṣàròyé rẹ̀ | C) Ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì jẹ́ ìkan náà pẹ̀lú ìfòyebánilò | D) Ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì gbọ́dọ̀ túmọ̀ sí pé ìpínlẹ̀ mú ìṣesí ìfíràn tó kéré jùlọ tó sì ṣe pàtàkì jùlọ.
- Options (English): A) Proportionality is a means of balancing the rights of an individual against the protection of the community as a whole | B) For an act to be proportionate, it should be linked to the legitimate aim of the state measure complained of | C) Proportionality is the same as reasonableness | D) Proportionality should mean the state takes the least intrusive action that is necessary
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Ìwọ̀ntún-wọ̀nsì jẹ́ ìkan náà pẹ̀lú ìfòyebánilò
- Verified Answer (English): C) Proportionality is the same as reasonableness

search_context: Nínú ìpẹ̀jọ́ Grootboom ní South Africa Ilé Ẹjọ́ Gíga  | In the Grootboom case in South Africa the Supreme Court | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Nínú ìpẹ̀jọ́ Grootboom ní South Africa Ilé Ẹjọ́ Gíga 
- English Question: In the Grootboom case in South Africa the Supreme Court
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Wọ́n rí i wí pé ìpínlẹ̀ náà ni ó jẹ̀bi fún àìnílélórí olùpẹ̀jọ́ náà àti wí pé wọ́n ní láti pèsè irúfẹ́ ilégbèé kan fún olùpẹ̀jọ́ náà láì pẹ́ láì jìnnà  | B) Wọ́n rí i wí pé ìpínlẹ̀ náà ni ó jẹ̀bi fún àìnílélórí olùpẹ̀jọ́ ṣùgbọ́n pé ìlẹ́tọ̀ọ́ sí ilégbèé ò sí nínú àṣẹ Ilé ẹjọ́ náà  | C) Wọ́n rí i wí pé ìpínlẹ̀ náà ní láti gbé ìgbésẹ̀ tó yẹ láti ṣe ojúṣe rẹ̀ sí olùpẹ̀jọ́ náà lábẹ́ ìlẹ́tọ̀ọ́ sí ilégbèé nínú Ìwé Òfin | D) Wọ́n rí i pé ìpínlẹ̀ náà kọ́ ni ó jẹ̀bi fún àìnílélórí olùpẹ̀jọ́ náà 
- Options (English): A) Found the state was responsible for the homelessness of the appellants and that they had to provide the appellants with a certain type of housing as soon as possible | B) Found the state was responsible for the homelessness of the appellants but that the right to housing was not enforceable by the Court | C) Found that the state had to take reasonable steps to fulfil its obligation to the appellants under the right to housing in the Constitution | D) Found the state was not responsible for the appellants' homelessness
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Wọ́n rí i wí pé ìpínlẹ̀ náà ní láti gbé ìgbésẹ̀ tó yẹ láti ṣe ojúṣe rẹ̀ sí olùpẹ̀jọ́ náà lábẹ́ ìlẹ́tọ̀ọ́ sí ilégbèé nínú Ìwé Òfin
- Verified Answer (English): C) Found that the state had to take reasonable steps to fulfil its obligation to the appellants under the right to housing in the Constitution

- English Question: Which rule of jus cogens was the first to be accepted explicitly as such by the ICJ?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ṣíṣe ipá lílò lééwọ̀ | B) Ṣíṣe ìfìyàjẹni lééwọ̀ | C) Ṣíṣe ìpànìyànrun lééwọ̀ | D) Májẹ̀mú ìpinnu ara ẹni

search_context: Nínú ìpẹ̀jọ́ wo ni Ìpínlẹ̀ aláì-farapa ti lè pè fún ojúṣe Ìpínlẹ̀ tó ṣẹ̀? | In which cases may a non-injured State invoke the responsibility of the culprit State? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Nínú ìpẹ̀jọ́ wo ni Ìpínlẹ̀ aláì-farapa ti lè pè fún ojúṣe Ìpínlẹ̀ tó ṣẹ̀?
- English Question: In which cases may a non-injured State invoke the responsibility of the culprit State?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Nínú àwọn ìpẹ̀jọ́ tí Ìpínlẹ̀ tó farapa bá fún aláì-farapa ní àṣẹ láti pè fún ojúṣe ní ipò rẹ̀  | B) Nínú àwọn ìpẹ̀jọ́ rírú òfin àwọn ojúṣe pàtó tó ń dáábò bo ìpinnu àjọni àgbáríjọpọ̀ àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ kan (obligations erga omnes partes) tàbí ìpinnu àwùjọ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè lápapọ̀ (obligations erga omnes) | C) Nínú àwọn ìpẹ̀jọ́ tó tako àwọn ìṣesí ilé iṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè, bíi Ìpinnu Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ | D) Nínú àwọn ìpẹ̀jọ́ tí kò tẹ̀lé ìpinnu ilé ẹjọ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè tàbí ilé ẹjọ́ kòtẹ́milọ́rùn 
- Options (English): A) Only in cases that the injured State has authorized a non-injured one to invoke the responsibility on its behalf | B) In cases of breaches of specific obligations protecting the collective interests of a group of States (obligations erga omnes partes) or the interests of the international community as a whole (obligations erga omnes) | C) In cases of violation of acts of international organizations, such as General Assembly Resolutions | D) In cases of non-compliance with a decision of an international court or tribunal
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Nínú àwọn ìpẹ̀jọ́ rírú òfin àwọn ojúṣe pàtó tó ń dáábò bo ìpinnu àjọni àgbáríjọpọ̀ àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ kan (obligations erga omnes partes) tàbí ìpinnu àwùjọ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè lápapọ̀ (obligations erga omnes)
- Verified Answer (English): B) In cases of breaches of specific obligations protecting the collective interests of a group of States (obligations erga omnes partes) or the interests of the international community as a whole (obligations erga omnes)

search_context: Ṣé àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ lè jẹ gbèsè fún àwọn gbèsè àti aṣemáṣe tí wọ́n so pọ̀ mọ́ ilé iṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀?  | May States incur liability for the debts and wrongdoings attributable to an international organisation to which they are parties? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ṣé àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ lè jẹ gbèsè fún àwọn gbèsè àti aṣemáṣe tí wọ́n so pọ̀ mọ́ ilé iṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀? 
- English Question: May States incur liability for the debts and wrongdoings attributable to an international organisation to which they are parties?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ò lè sá sẹ́yìn gàgá ilé iṣẹ́ ìjọba  | B) Ẹni tí òfin dámọ̀ nínú ilé iṣẹ́ náà yàtọ̀ sí ti àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀. | C) Àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ àti Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn náà jẹ̀bi fún aṣemáṣe tí wọ́n bá so pọ̀ mọ́ ilé iṣẹ́ náà  | D) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ nìkan ni wọ́n jẹ̀bi fún àwọn gbèsè àti aṣemáṣe tí wọ́n so pọ̀ mọ́ ilé iṣẹ́ náà 
- Options (English): A) Member States cannot hide behind an organisation's corporate veil | B) The legal person of the organisation is distinct from that of its member States | C) Organisations and their member States are equally liable for any wrongdoings attributable to the organisation | D) Member States are alone liable for debts and wrongdoings attributable to the organisation
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Ẹni tí òfin dámọ̀ nínú ilé iṣẹ́ náà yàtọ̀ sí ti àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀.
- Verified Answer (English): B) The legal person of the organisation is distinct from that of its member States

search_context: Kínni ó ṣe pàtàkì fún òfin gbogbogbò ti òfin àṣà láti di ṣíṣe?  | What is required for a general rule of customary law to be formed? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni ó ṣe pàtàkì fún òfin gbogbogbò ti òfin àṣà láti di ṣíṣe? 
- English Question: What is required for a general rule of customary law to be formed?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìṣesí gbogbogbò, títàn káàkiri àti àṣetẹ̀léra láti ọ̀dọ Ìpínlẹ̀ ni ó ṣe pàtàkì  | B) Ìṣesí àṣetẹ̀léra àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ díẹ̀ ti tó  | C) Gbígbà lọ́nà òfin pé ìṣesí kọ̀ọ̀kan ní Ìpínlẹ̀ kan wà ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ni nǹkan tó ṣe pàtàkì jùlọ | D) Àpapọ èròjà títàn káàkiri àti àṣetẹ̀léra ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ àti èrò àwọn adájọ́ ló ṣe pàtàkì 
- Options (English): A) Only general, widespread and consistent practice on the part of States is required | B) The consistent practice of few States is sufficient | C) The legal conviction that a certain practice of a State is in accordance with international law is the most significant requirement | D) Both the elements of widespread and consistent State practice and of the opinio juris are required
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): D) Àpapọ èròjà títàn káàkiri àti àṣetẹ̀léra ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ àti èrò àwọn adájọ́ ló ṣe pàtàkì 
- Verified Answer (English): D) Both the elements of widespread and consistent State practice and of the opinio juris are required

search_context: Kínni 'ìrúfin ohun èlò' nínú àdéhùn náà? | What is 'material breach' of the treaty? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:

search_context: Ṣé lọ́gàlọ́mọṣẹ́ kankan tàbí ṣíṣe pàtàkì wà láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ lábẹ́ òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè?  | Is there any hierarchy or priority among States under international law? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:

- English Question: Is there any hierarchy or priority among States under international law?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Bẹ́ẹ̀ni, àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé láti ìgbà ìwáṣẹ̀ ní wọ́n fún ní agbára tó pọ̀ àti aṣẹ  | B) Bẹ́ẹ̀ni, Àwọn Ọmọ Ẹgbẹ́ Láéláé Márùn-ún ti Àjọ Aláàbò UN (UK, USA, France, Russia, China) wà ní ipò alágbára ju àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ mìíràn lọ  | C) Rárá, gbogbo àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ní wọ́n rí bí ìkan náà gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìpínlẹ̀ Olómìnira (ìpìlẹ̀ òye ìbádọ́gba òmìnira, tó wà nínú abala òfin 2, ìpínrọ̀ 1 UN Charter) | D) Yálà lọ́gàlọ́mọṣẹ́ kankan yóò wà láàrin àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn àjọ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè kọ̀ọ̀kan láti ṣe 
- Options (English): A) Yes, the States that were the founding members of the United Nations are vested with more powers and authority | B) Yes, the Permanent Five Members of the UN Security Council (UK, USA, France, Russia, China) are in a superior position than the other States | C) No, all States are considered equal as sovereign States (the principle of sovereign equality, enshrined in article 2, para 1 UN Charter) | D) Whether there will be any hierarchy among States is a matter of each international organization to decide
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Rárá, gbogbo àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ní wọ́n rí bí ìkan náà gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìpínlẹ̀ Olómìnira (ìpìlẹ̀ òye ìbádọ́gba òmìnira, tó wà nínú abala òfin 2, ìpínrọ̀ 1 UN Charter)
- Verified Answer (English): C) No, all States are considered equal as sovereign States (the principle of sovereign equality, enshrined in article 2, para 1 UN Charter)

search_context: Ǹjẹ́ lọ́gàlọ́mọṣẹ́ tàbí ṣíṣe pàtàkì kankan wà láàrín àwọn oríṣiríṣi ọ̀nà yíyanjú àríyànjiyàn pẹ̀lú àlàáfíà?  | Is there any hierarchy or priority among the various methods of peaceful settlement of disputes? | international_law

- English Question: Is there any hierarchy or priority among the various methods of peaceful settlement of disputes?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Bẹ́ẹ̀ni, gbogbo àwọn ìlànà òfin (b.a. ìfọ̀rọ̀wérò, ìlàjà, ìbéèrè, ìparí ìja) gbọ́dọ̀ di lílò ṣíwájú lílo àwọn ìlànà òfin  | B) Àwọn ìlànà òfin máa ń borí àwọn ìlànà òṣèlú, nígbà tó jẹ́ wí pé wọ́n máa ń wà lórí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ náà  | C) Kò sí lọ́gàlọ́mọṣẹ́ láàrín àwọn ìlànà wọ̀nyìí bẹ́ẹ̀ ìpinnu sì wà lọ́wọ́ àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n ní àríyànjiyàn  | D) Ó jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ alàgàta aláìṣègbè láti pinnu irú ìlànà wo ló ṣe pàtàkì lórí àwọn tókù

- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Kò sí lọ́gàlọ́mọṣẹ́ láàrín àwọn ìlànà wọ̀nyìí bẹ́ẹ̀ ìpinnu sì wà lọ́wọ́ àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n ní àríyànjiyàn 
- Verified Answer (English): C) There is no hierarchy among these methods and the choice belongs to the disputing States

pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:

- English Question: What is the meaning of proportionality in relation to the options available to the victim State?

- Options (English): A) The victim State may use the same means and intensity of force as the aggressor | B) The victim State may use any means to defeat and incapacitate the aggressor | C) The victim State may only use such means and force as it is necessary to defeat the aggressor | D) The victim State can do nothing without Security Council approval
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Ìpínlẹ̀ olùfaragbà lè lo irú ìlànà àti agbára bẹ́ẹ̀ bó bá ṣe yẹ láti ṣẹ́gun olùfíràn rẹ̀ nìkan

pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni ànfàní ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ lábẹ́ òfin orí omi òkun? 
- English Question: What is the purpose of baselines under the law of the sea?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìpinnu ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ ni wọ́n ń lò fún wíwọn àwọn omi abẹ́lé àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ etí omi  | B) Ìpinnu ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì fún ìdásílẹ̀ àwọn ẹkùn etí omi, nígbà tó ṣe wí pé wọ́n jẹ́ ọ̀gangan ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ fún wíwọn fífẹ̀ ẹkùn kọ̀ọ̀kan  | C) Ìpinnu ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì fún ìdarí àwọn ọkọ̀ lórí ìpele gíga omi láì sí ewu | D) A máa ń ya àwọn ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ ààlà orí omi láàrín Ìpínlẹ̀ alátakò níwájú ilé ẹjọ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè tàbí ilé ẹjọ́ kòtẹ́milọ́rùn 
- Options (English): A) The determination of baselines is used for the measuring of the internal waters of coastal States | B) The determination of baselines is instrumental to the establishment of all maritime zones, since they constitute the starting point for measuring the breadth of each zone | C) The determination of baselines is instrumental to the safe navigation of vessels on the high seas | D) Baselines are drawn only in cases of maritime delimitation between opposing State before an international court or tribunal
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Ìpinnu ipẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì fún ìdásílẹ̀ àwọn ẹkùn etí omi, nígbà tó ṣe wí pé wọ́n jẹ́ ọ̀gangan ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ fún wíwọn fífẹ̀ ẹkùn kọ̀ọ̀kan 
- Verified Answer (English): B) The determination of baselines is instrumental to the establishment of all maritime zones, since they constitute the starting point for measuring the breadth of each zone

search_context: Kínni ìyàtọ̀ láàrín ìparí ìjà àti ìlàjà?  | What is the difference between conciliation and mediation? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:

- Yorùbá Question: Kínni ìyàtọ̀ láàrín ìparí ìjà àti ìlàjà? 
- English Question: What is the difference between conciliation and mediation?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìparí ìjà ni ìtẹ̀síwájú ìlàjà pẹ̀lú ìyàtọ̀ pé ìparí ìja máa pèsè èsì àsopọ̀, nígbà tí ìlàjà ò rí bẹ́ẹ̀ | B) Àwọn aṣojú Akọ̀wé-Àpapọ̀ UN ni wọ́n máa ń parí ìjà ní àdáṣe, nígbà tí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ alàgàta náà tún lè làjà | C) Ẹni tí wọ́n bá yàn ló máa ń làjà ní gbogbo ìgbà pẹ̀lú ìgbàlááyè àwọn ẹgbẹ́ náà, nígbà tí ìparí ìjà níṣe pẹ̀lú àjọ kan, tó ṣíwájú àyẹ̀wò aláìṣègbè àríyànjiyàn náà tí yóò sì dábàá àwọn àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ ìparí ìjà  | D) Ìparí ìjà ni ìlànà ìparí àríyànjiyàn tí wọ́n ń ṣe nítorí àdéhùn, nígbà tí ìlàjà tún lè wà lórí ìpìlẹ alátagbà 
- Options (English): A) Conciliation is the continuation of mediation with the difference that conciliation produces a binding result, while mediation not | B) Conciliation is conducted exclusively by representatives of the UN Secretary-General, while mediation may also be conducted by third States' officials | C) Mediation is usually conducted by a person appointed with the consent of the parties, while conciliation involves a commission, which proceeds to an impartial examination of the dispute and proposes settlement terms | D) Conciliation is a method of dispute settlement pursued only by virtue of a treaty, while mediation may also be on an ad hoc basis
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Ẹni tí wọ́n bá yàn ló máa ń làjà ní gbogbo ìgbà pẹ̀lú ìgbàlááyè àwọn ẹgbẹ́ náà, nígbà tí ìparí ìjà níṣe pẹ̀lú àjọ kan, tó ṣíwájú àyẹ̀wò aláìṣègbè àríyànjiyàn náà tí yóò sì dábàá àwọn àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ ìparí ìjà 
- Verified Answer (English): C) Mediation is usually conducted by a person appointed with the consent of the parties, while conciliation involves a commission, which proceeds to an impartial examination of the dispute and proposes settlement terms

Which of the following statements is not part of the Osman test? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Nínú Osman v UK (1998), Ilé Ẹjọ́ Yúrópù ṣe àgbékalẹ̀ àyẹ̀wò, tí ó ṣe é lò láti ṣe ojúṣe tó dára lápapọ̀ lórí àwọn ìpínlẹ̀. Èwo nínú àwọn gbólóhùn wọ̀nyìí ni kò sí lára àyẹ̀wo Osman?

- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ewu náà gbọ́dọ̀ wá láti ọ̀dọ aṣojú ìpínlẹ̀ | B) Tí ó bá jẹ́ ewu gidi tó sì ti súnmọ́ (ti ikú/ìpalára) | C) Ìpínlẹ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ gbé àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ láti dèna ìṣẹ̀lẹ ikú/ìpalára  | D) Ìpínlẹ̀ náà mọ̀ tàbí yẹ kí ó ti mọ̀
- Options (English): A) The risk must emanate from a state agent | B) If a real and imminent risk (of death/harm) | C) A state should take reasonable steps to prevent death/harm occurring | D) A state knows or ought to have known

search_context: Ta ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti bèèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn ICJ? | Who is entitled to request an advisory opinion of the ICJ? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ta ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti bèèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn ICJ?
- English Question: Who is entitled to request an advisory opinion of the ICJ?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn olórí ẹ̀ka UN nìkan ni wọ́n lè bèrè ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn (Àjọ tó ń rí sí Ètò Ààbò, Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀, ECOSOC, Àjọ Aṣeégbẹ́kẹ̀lé, Ilé Iṣẹ́ Ìjọba) | B) Gbogbo ilé iṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn  | C) Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ àti Àjọ tó ń rí sí Ètò Ààbò lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn lórí èyíkéyìí ìbéèrè òfin, bẹ́ẹ̀ náà ni 'àwọn ẹ̀ka Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé mìíràn àti àwọn àjọ oníṣe àkànṣe, tí ó lè gbà àṣẹ bẹ́ẹ̀ nígbàkígbà ní Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀, lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn Ilé Ẹjọ́ lórí àwọn ìbéèrè òfin tó ń ṣúyọ láàrín agbègbè iṣẹ́ wọn  | D) Àwọn olórí ẹ̀ka UN lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn bẹ́ẹ̀ náà sì ni àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n ti gba àṣẹ lọ́dọ̀ Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ 
- Options (English): A) Only the principal organs of the UN may request an advisory opinion (Security Council, General Assembly, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, Secretariat) | B) All international organizations may request an advisory opinion | C) The General Assembly and the Security Council may request advisory opinions on any legal question, as well as 'other organs of the United Nations and specialized agencies, which may at any time be so authorized by the General Assembly, may also request advisory opinions of the Court on legal questions arising within the scope of their activities' | D) The principal organs of the UN may request an advisory opinion as well as the State that have been authorized by the General Assembly
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ àti Àjọ tó ń rí sí Ètò Ààbò lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn lórí èyíkéyìí ìbéèrè òfin, bẹ́ẹ̀ náà ni 'àwọn ẹ̀ka Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé mìíràn àti àwọn àjọ oníṣe àkànṣe, tí ó lè gbà àṣẹ bẹ́ẹ̀ nígbàkígbà ní Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀, lè bèrè fún ìpinnu ìmọ̀ràn Ilé Ẹjọ́ lórí àwọn ìbéèrè òfin tó ń ṣúyọ láàrín agbègbè iṣẹ́ wọn 
- Verified Answer (English): C) The General Assembly and the Security Council may request advisory opinions on any legal question, as well as 'other organs of the United Nations and specialized agencies, which may at any time be so authorized by the General Assembly, may also request advisory opinions of the Court on legal questions arising within the scope of their activities'

search_context: Kínni ànfàní ìdájọ́ gbogbo àgbáyé?  | What is the purpose of universal jurisdiction? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni ànfàní ìdájọ́ gbogbo àgbáyé? 
- English Question: What is the purpose of universal jurisdiction?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Èròngbà rẹ̀ ni láti ṣẹ̀dá àwọn ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ti gbogbo ayé  | B) Èròngbà rẹ̀ ni láti dẹ́kun àjọ náà níbi àwọn ìwà ọ̀daràn ilẹ̀ òkèèrè kọ̀ọ̀kan  | C) Èròngbà rẹ̀ ni láti pèsè ìdájọ́ fún gbogbo Ìpínlẹ̀ ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn ìwà ọ̀daràn kan pàtó  | D) Èròngbà rẹ̀ ni láti pèsè ìdájọ́ fún gbogbo Ìpínlẹ̀ ní tó níṣe pẹ̀lú gbogbo ìwà ọ̀daràn ilẹ̀ òkèèrè 
- Options (English): A) Its aim is to establish certain offences as universal | B) Its aim is to deter the commission of certain international crimes | C) Its aim is to provide jurisdiction to all States in respect of particular crimes | D) Its aim is to provide jurisdiction to all States in respect of all international crimes
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Èròngbà rẹ̀ ni láti pèsè ìdájọ́ fún gbogbo Ìpínlẹ̀ ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn ìwà ọ̀daràn kan pàtó 
- Verified Answer (English): C) Its aim is to provide jurisdiction to all States in respect of particular crimes

search_context: Ṣé gbogbo àwọn ìṣesí àwọn ẹ̀ka Ìpínlẹ̀ ló so pọ̀ mọ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ náà lábẹ́ ojúṣe òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè? | Are all acts of State organs attributed to the State under the law international responsibility? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ṣé gbogbo àwọn ìṣesí àwọn ẹ̀ka Ìpínlẹ̀ ló so pọ̀ mọ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ náà lábẹ́ ojúṣe òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè?
- English Question: Are all acts of State organs attributed to the State under the law international responsibility?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìṣesí ẹ̀ka ìṣèjọba kankan ni wọn yóò rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ yẹn, kódà nínú àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ìṣesí yìí ò bá gba àṣẹ tàbí ṣe kọjá agbára rẹ̀ | B) Ìṣesí àwọn onípò gíga nínú ìṣèjọba Ìpínlè nìkan ni wọn yóò sopọ̀ mọ́ ọ  | C) Ìṣesí ẹ̀ka Ìpínlẹ̀ kankan ni wọn yóò rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ yẹn, tó bá jẹ́ wí pé kò ṣe kọjá agbára rẹ̀  | D) Àwọn ìṣesí ẹ̀ka aláṣẹ Ìpínlẹ̀ náà nìkan ni wọn yóò rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ yẹn 
- Options (English): A) The conduct of any State organ shall be considered an act of that State, even in the case that this conduct was unauthorized or ultra vires | B) Only the conduct of the higher echelons of the government of State shall be attributable to it | C) The conduct of any State organs shall be considered an act of that State, provided that it is intra vires | D) Only the conduct of the executive branch of the State shall be considered an act of that State.
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Ìṣesí ẹ̀ka ìṣèjọba kankan ni wọn yóò rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ìṣesí Ìpínlẹ̀ yẹn, kódà nínú àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ìṣesí yìí ò bá gba àṣẹ tàbí ṣe kọjá agbára rẹ̀
- Verified Answer (English): A) The conduct of any State organ shall be considered an act of that State, even in the case that this conduct was unauthorized or ultra vires

pedagogical_answer:

- Yorùbá Question: Kínni 'àdéhùn' gẹ́gẹ́ bíi Àpérò Vienna lórí Òfin Àwọn Àdéhùn (VCLT)?
- English Question: What is a 'treaty' according to the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (VCLT)?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn àdéhùn ni gbogbo àdéhùn tó ti parí láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀, àwọn àjọ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè àti àwọn nǹkan tí kìí ṣe ti Ìpínlẹ̀ (b.a àwọn ilé iṣẹ́) | B) Àwọn àdéhùn jẹ́ àdéhùn tó ti parí láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ní kíkọ tí òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ń ṣàkóso rẹ̀ | C) Àwọn àdéhùn jẹ́ àpapọ àwọn àdéhùn kíkọ àti sísọ láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀  | D) Àwọn àdéhùn ni àwọn àdéhùn tó ti parí láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tó wà ní kíkọ tí òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè tàbí ti abẹ́lé ń ṣàkóso lórí rẹ̀
- Options (English): A) Treaties are all agreements concluded between States, international organizations and non-State entities (e.g. corporations) | B) Treaties are agreements concluded between States in written form and governed by international law | C) Treaties are both the written and oral agreements between States | D) Treaties are agreements concluded between States in written form governed either by international or domestic law
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Àwọn àdéhùn jẹ́ àdéhùn tó ti parí láàrín àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ní kíkọ tí òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ń ṣàkóso rẹ̀
- Verified Answer (English): B) Treaties are agreements concluded between States in written form and governed by international law

search_context: Kínni àbájáde ṣíwájú kí Ilé Ẹjọ́ Yúrópù fún Àwọn Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn nínú ìpẹ̀jọ́ Al-Adsani?  | What was the outcome before the European Court of Human Rights in the Al-Adsani case? | international_law

- Options (English): A) The Court held that the right to a fair trial trumped the privilege of immunity | B) The Court held that immunity trumped the right to a fair trial | C) The Court held that immunities were not in conflict with the right to a fair trial | D) The Court held that human rights considerations prevailed over all other contrary rules of international law, including most immunities

search_context: Báwo ni a ṣe lè ṣe ìtumọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn? | How treaties are to be interpreted? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Báwo ni a ṣe lè ṣe ìtumọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn?
- English Question: How treaties are to be interpreted?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìtúmọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ṣíṣe pẹ̀lú òótọ́ inú ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú ìtumọ̀ lérèfé tí wọn yóò fún àwọn àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ àdéhùn náà ní ọ̀gangan ipò wọn àti ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn ohun èlò àti ìwúlò rẹ̀ | B) Ìtumọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ṣíṣe ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú ìtumọ̀ lérèfé àwọn àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ àdéhùn wọn nìkan  | C) Ìtumọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ṣíṣe ní ìbámu pẹlú èròngbà awon ẹgbẹ́ náà, gẹ́gẹ́ bó ṣe fojú hàn nínú àwọn iṣẹ́ ìgbaradì àdéhùn náà  | D) Ìtumọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ṣíṣe ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú àwọn ohun èlò àti ìwúlò rẹ̀ nìkan 
- Options (English): A) Treaties are to be interpreted in good faith in accordance with the ordinary meaning to be given to the terms of the treaty in their context and in the light of its object and purpose | B) Treaties are to be interpreted only in accordance with the ordinary meaning of their terms | C) Treaties are to be interpreted in accordance with the intention of the parties, as evidenced in the preparatory works of the treaty | D) Treaties are to be interpreted only in light of its object and purpose
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Ìtúmọ̀ àwọn àdéhùn gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ṣíṣe pẹ̀lú òótọ́ inú ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú ìtumọ̀ lérèfé tí wọn yóò fún àwọn àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ àdéhùn náà ní ọ̀gangan ipò wọn àti ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn ohun èlò àti ìwúlò rẹ̀
- Verified Answer (English): A) Treaties are to be interpreted in good faith in accordance with the ordinary meaning to be given to the terms of the treaty in their context and in the light of its object and purpose

search_context: Nígbà wo ni àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ etí omi lè ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ ìwà ọ̀daràn wọn lórí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ní èbúté won?  | When coastal States do enforce their criminal jurisdiction over foreign vessels in their ports? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Nígbà wo ni àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ etí omi lè ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ ìwà ọ̀daràn wọn lórí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ilẹ̀ òkèèrè ní èbúté won? 
- English Question: When coastal States do enforce their criminal jurisdiction over foreign vessels in their ports?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ Èbúté lápapọ̀ ò kí ń ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ ìwà ọ̀daràn wọn lórí àwọn ìwà ọ̀daràn tí kò bá rú àwọn òfin àṣà wọn tàbí da àlàáfíà àti ètò ìlú rú. | B) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ Èbúté máa ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ wọn nínú gbogbo ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ tó ti bàjẹ́ | C) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ Èbúté máa ń ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ wọn ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú ìwà ọ̀daràn tó lágbára nìkan, bíi gbígbé òògùn olóró  | D) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ Èbúté ò ní ànfàní láti ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ wọn lórí ọkọ̀ àjòjì kankan 
- Options (English): A) Port States generally do not enforce their criminal jurisdiction over crimes that do not infringe their customs laws or disrupt peace and public order. | B) Port States enforce their jurisdiction in all cases of delinquent vessels | C) Port States enforce their jurisdiction only in respect of very serious crimes, such as drug trafficking | D) Port States are not entitled to enforce their jurisdiction over any foreign vessel
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ Èbúté lápapọ̀ ò kí ń ṣàmúlò ìdájọ́ ìwà ọ̀daràn wọn lórí àwọn ìwà ọ̀daràn tí kò bá rú àwọn òfin àṣà wọn tàbí da àlàáfíà àti ètò ìlú rú.
- Verified Answer (English): A) Port States generally do not enforce their criminal jurisdiction over crimes that do not infringe their customs laws or disrupt peace and public order.

search_context: Kínni iyì àwọn Ìpinnu Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ UN ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú 'orísun' òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè? | What is the value of the Resolutions of the UN General Assembly in terms as a 'source' of international law? | international_law

[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni iyì àwọn Ìpinnu Ilé Aṣòfin Àpapọ̀ UN ní èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú 'orísun' òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè?
- English Question: What is the value of the Resolutions of the UN General Assembly in terms as a 'source' of international law?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn ìpinnu GA ni wọ́n rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi àfikún orísun fún òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè fún ìdí èyí ó wà lórí àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀  | B) Àwọn ìpinnu GA ṣe déédé pẹ̀lú àwọn àdéhùn  | C) Àwọn ìpinnu GA ṣe àfihàn òfin àṣà ní gbogbo ìgbà  | D) Àwọn ìpinnu GA ni wọ́n rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi orísun ohun èlò, nítorí wí pé wọ́n lè sọ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ òfin àṣà 
- Options (English): A) GA Resolutions are considered as additional sources of international law and thus binding upon States | B) GA Resolutions are equivalent to treaties | C) GA Resolutions reflect always customary law | D) GA Resolutions are considered as material source, in the sense that they may enunciate statements of customary law
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): D) Àwọn ìpinnu GA ni wọ́n rí gẹ́gẹ́ bíi orísun ohun èlò, nítorí wí pé wọ́n lè sọ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ òfin àṣà 
- Verified Answer (English): D) GA Resolutions are considered as material source, in the sense that they may enunciate statements of customary law

search_context: Ṣé àdéhùn máa ń siṣẹ́ lórí àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ò sí nínú àdéhùn, ie àwọn ẹgbẹ́ tí kìí ṣe Ìpínlẹ̀? | Do treaties bind third States, ie non-State parties? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ṣé àdéhùn máa ń siṣẹ́ lórí àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ò sí nínú àdéhùn, ie àwọn ẹgbẹ́ tí kìí ṣe Ìpínlẹ̀?
- English Question: Do treaties bind third States, ie non-State parties?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn àdéhùn lè ṣẹ̀dá ẹ̀tọ́ fún Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí nínú àdéhùn  | B) Àwọn àdéhùn sẹ̀dá àpapọ̀ ojúṣe àti ẹ̀tọ́ fún àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí nínú àdéhùn  | C) Àwọn àdéhùn ò kí ń ṣẹ̀dá ojúṣe àti ẹ̀tọ́ fún Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí nínú àdéhùn láì gba ìyànda wọn | D) Àwọn àdéhùn ò kí ń ṣẹ̀dá ojúṣe àti ẹ̀tọ́ kankan fún Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí nínú àdéhùn, kódà tí ẹni kejì bá yànda.
- Options (English): A) Treaties may create only rights for third States | B) Treaties create both obligations and rights for third States | C) Treaties do no create obligations or rights for third States without their consent | D) Treaties do not create any obligations or rights for third States, even when the latter consent.
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Àwọn àdéhùn ò kí ń ṣẹ̀dá ojúṣe àti ẹ̀tọ́ fún Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí nínú àdéhùn láì gba ìyànda wọn
- Verified Answer (English): C) Treaties do no create obligations or rights for third States without their consent

pedagogical_answer:

- Options (Yorùbá): A) Kò sí lọ́gà lọ́mọṣẹ́ láàrín àwọn orísun elétò òfin ilẹ̀ òkèèrè  | B) Àwọn àdéhùn borí àṣà  | C) Àṣà borí àwọn àdéhùn  | D) Àwọn òpó àpapọ̀ òfin borí àpapọ̀ àṣà àti àwọn àdéhùn

search_context: Kínni ànfàní pàtó tí Ìpinnu UNSC 678 ní lórí àgbáríjọpọ̀ ìṣesí ìdáàbòbò lábẹ́ Abala òfin 51 UN Charter lásìkò Ogun Gulf? | What was the particular advantage of UNSC Resolution 678 over a collective defensive action under Article 51 UN Charter during the Gulf War? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kínni ànfàní pàtó tí Ìpinnu UNSC 678 ní lórí àgbáríjọpọ̀ ìṣesí ìdáàbòbò lábẹ́ Abala òfin 51 UN Charter lásìkò Ogun Gulf?
- English Question: What was the particular advantage of UNSC Resolution 678 over a collective defensive action under Article 51 UN Charter during the Gulf War?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìpinnu 678 fi ààyè gba àwọn olùkù láti kọlu Iraq pẹ̀lú àwọn ohun ìjà ìpanirun àti kẹ́míkà  | B) Ìpinnu 678 ṣe tóóró ju ẹ̀tọ́ sí ìdáàbòbò ara ẹni tó ṣe pàtàkì lábẹ́ Abala òfin 51 UN Charter  | C) Ìpinnu 678 yá láti ṣàmúlò àti láti dunàdúrà. | D) Ìpinnu 678 kẹnú nítorí ó fi ààyè gba lílo ipá lórí èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú èyíkéyìí ọ̀rọ̀ tó ń dúkokò mọ́ àlàáfíà àti ààbò àwọn agbègbè Gulf.
- Options (English): A) Resolution 678 allowed the allies to attack Iraq with nuclear and chemical weapons | B) Resolution 678 is narrower than the inherent right of self-defence under Article 51 UN Charter | C) Resolution 678 was faster to adopt and negotiate. | D) Resolution 678 is broader because it authorised the use of force with respect to any matter threatening the peace and security of the Gulf region.
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): D) Ìpinnu 678 kẹnú nítorí ó fi ààyè gba lílo ipá lórí èyí tó níṣe pẹ̀lú èyíkéyìí ọ̀rọ̀ tó ń dúkokò mọ́ àlàáfíà àti ààbò àwọn agbègbè Gulf.
- Verified Answer (English): D) Resolution 678 is broader because it authorised the use of force with respect to any matter threatening the peace and security of the Gulf region.

search_context: Báwo ni òfin àṣà ṣe lè di lílò nínú àwọn ìpèsè àdéhùn?  | How can customary law be related to treaty provisions? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Báwo ni òfin àṣà ṣe lè di lílò nínú àwọn ìpèsè àdéhùn? 
- English Question: How can customary law be related to treaty provisions?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn àdéhùn lè ṣe àkójọpọ̀ òfin àṣà nìkan.      | B) Òfin àṣà jẹ́ orísun ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ fún àgbáyé àti pé a kò lè ṣe é ṣe nínú àdéhùn.      | C) Àwọn àdéhùn lè 1) ṣe àkójọpọ̀ òfin àṣà, 2) 'crystallise' òfin àṣà , 3) yọrí sí ìfarahàn òfin àṣà      | D) Òfin àṣà lè jáde láti inú àdéhùn ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀.
- Options (English): A) Treaties may only codify customary law | B) Customary law is a different source of international and it cannot be embodied in treaties | C) Treaties may 1) codify customary law, 2) 'crystallise' customary law, 3) lead to the emergence of customary law | D) Customary law can emerge only from few multilateral treaties
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Àwọn àdéhùn lè 1) ṣe àkójọpọ̀ òfin àṣà, 2) 'crystallise' òfin àṣà , 3) yọrí sí ìfarahàn òfin àṣà     
- Verified Answer (English): C) Treaties may 1) codify customary law, 2) 'crystallise' customary law, 3) lead to the emergence of customary law

search_context: Kí ló túmọ̀ sí fún Ìpínlẹ̀ kan láti ní òmìnira?  | What does it mean for a State to be sovereign? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ló túmọ̀ sí fún Ìpínlẹ̀ kan láti ní òmìnira? 
- English Question: What does it mean for a State to be sovereign?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Òmìnira túmọ‌ sí wípé gbogbo àwọn ìpínlẹ‌ yòókù mọ‌ ọ‌.    | B) Òmìnira túmọ‌ sí pé láti lè ṣe àdéhùn kí ó sì darapọ‌ mọ‌ UN.    | C) Òmìnira túmọ‌ sí òmìnira láti pinnu ọ‌rọ‌ ẹni láìsí wípé ará ìta dá síi.    | D) Òmìnira túmọ‌ sí níní ẹ‌tọ‌ láti dáàbò bo ara ẹni.
- Options (English): A) Sovereignty means being recognised by all other States | B) Sovereignty means to be able to enter into treaties and join the UN | C) Sovereignty means freedom to determine one's own affairs without external interference | D) Sovereignty means possessing the right to defend oneself
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Òmìnira túmọ‌ sí òmìnira láti pinnu ọ‌rọ‌ ẹni láìsí wípé ará ìta dá síi.   
- Verified Answer (English): C) Sovereignty means freedom to determine one's own affairs without external interference

- Verified Answer (English): B) The act of State doctrine denotes that the assessment as to the existence of an alleged tort committed by a State belongs to the executive and not the courts

search_context: Báwo ni a ṣe lè ṣe àfihàn ètò àwọn àwùjọ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè?  | How can the structure of the international society be displayed? | international_law

- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ètò àwùjọ àgbáyé tẹ̀lé àwòṣe àwọn àṣẹ òfin tiwantiwa.       | B) Àwùjọ àgbáyé ní àkójọpọ̀ àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ aláṣẹ àti àwọn àjọ àgbáyé mìíràn, èyí tí wọ́n fọ́nká pẹ̀lú àṣẹ onípele kan.       | C) Àwùjọ àgbáyé jẹ́ ìwà ìbàjẹ́ débi pé kò sí ìpele àṣẹ, kì í ṣe òòró tàbí ìwọ̀n.      . | D) Ètò àwùjọ àgbáyé jọ ètò àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè tó lágbára jùlọ ní àgbáyé

- Options (Yorùbá): A) Gẹ‌gẹ‌ bí òfin lis pendens, ilé ẹjọ‌ tí ó gba àríyànjiyàn àkọ‌kọ‌ náà ní àṣẹ l láti ṣe ìdájọ‌ rẹ‌. | B) Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ìdájọ́ Àgbáyé ní àṣẹ lórí ilé ẹjọ́ tàbí ilé ẹjọ́  mìíràn. | C) Níwọ̀n ìgbà tí kò sí òfin lis pendens nínú òfin àgbáyé àti pé gbogbo rẹ̀ dá lórí ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ lórí àríyànjiyàn, kò sí ohun pàtàkì tàbí ìlànà láàárín àwọn ilé ẹjọ́ àgbáyé àti ilé-ẹjọ́. | D) Àwọn ilé ẹjọ́ agbègbè tàbí àkànṣe ní àkọ́kọ́ lórí gbogbo àwọn yòókù ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú ìlànà lex specialis.
- Options (English): A) According to the lis pendens rule, the court or the tribunal that seizes first the dispute has exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate it | B) The International Court of Justice has by definition priority over any other court or tribunal | C) Since there is no lis pendens rule in international law and all depends on the consent of the parties to a dispute, there is no priority or hierarchy among international courts and tribunals | D) Regional or special courts have priority over all others in line of the principle of lex specialis
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Níwọ̀n ìgbà tí kò sí òfin lis pendens nínú òfin àgbáyé àti pé gbogbo rẹ̀ dá lórí ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ lórí àríyànjiyàn, kò sí ohun pàtàkì tàbí ìlànà láàárín àwọn ilé ẹjọ́ àgbáyé àti ilé-ẹjọ́.
- Verified Answer (English): C) Since there is no lis pendens rule in international law and all depends on the consent of the parties to a dispute, there is no priority or hierarchy among international courts and tribunals

- English Question: Do third States enjoy any fishing rights within the Exclusive Economic Zone of another State?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Nígbà tí Ìpínlẹ‌ etíkun kò bá lè kórè 'gbogbo iye tó ṣe é mú', Ìpínlẹ‌ etíkun náà ni láti fún ìpínlẹ‌ mìíràn ní àfààní sí ọ‌pọ‌ náà kó sì jẹ‌ kó ṣe pàtàkì fún àwọn ìpínlẹ‌ tí ó ṣẹ‌ṣẹ‌ ń dàgbà tí ó jé wípé ọ‌gbẹ ilẹ‌ ló yí wọn ká. | B) Àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò sí lábẹ́ EU lè má ní àfààní sí ẹja láàárín EEZ ìpínlẹ̀ mìíràn. | C) Ìpínlẹ̀ etíkun yóò fún àwọn ẹja ní àfààní sí ẹja láàárín EEZ rẹ̀ fún àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ tó wà ní àyíká nìkan. | D) Àwọn Ìpínlẹ̀ ọ̀gbẹ̀rì ní òmìnira láti pẹja láàárín EEZ mìíràn, àyàfi láti àwọn agbègbè kan tí wọ́n yàn.

- Verified Answer (English): A) When the coastal State cannot harvest the 'total allowable catch', the coastal State is to give other State access to that surplus with priority to be given to developing and land-locked States

search_context: Kí ní ojúṣe ìdáàbòbò òmìnira? | What is the purpose of sovereign immunity? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ní ojúṣe ìdáàbòbò òmìnira?
- English Question: What is the purpose of sovereign immunity?

- Options (English): A) The purpose of immunity is to protect foreign Heads of State from embarrassment | B) Immunity protects a State from being invaded by another | C) Immunity shields States from being sued in the courts of other States | D) The purpose of immunity is to offer impunity in respect of all crimes

pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni àṣẹ lórí ẹni àjèjì?
- English Question: What is passive personality jurisdiction?

- Verified Answer (English): C) It is jurisdiction based on the nationality of the victims

search_context: Kí ni àléébù 'ìpínyà' òfin àgbáyé? | What is the problem of 'fragmentation' of international law? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni àléébù 'ìpínyà' òfin àgbáyé?
- English Question: What is the problem of 'fragmentation' of international law?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìpínyà òfin àgbáyé ní í ṣe pẹ‌lú pé ó ṣeéṣe kí àwọn ìjọba ọ‌tọ‌ọ‌tọ‌ lo òfin  òfin àgbáyé kan náà. | B) Ó ṣe é ṣe fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìjọba  (ìyẹn òfin ìdókòwò ilẹ̀ òkèèrè àti òfin ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn) láti wà kí wọ́n sì ṣe ìdàgbàsókè ní ìyàsọ́tọ̀ ara wọn, nígbẹ̀yìn-gbẹ́yìn kí ó parí sí ṣíṣe àwọn òfin ìyàtọ̀ òfin àgbáyé. | C) Ìpínyà ni ìgbà tí àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bá gba ìtumọ̀ ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ nípa òfin àgbáyé kan náà. | D) Ìpínyà ni ìgbà tí àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ kò bá fara mọ́ òfin àgbáyé kan.
- Options (English): A) Fragmentation of international law concerns the possibility of different legal regimes apply the same rules of international law | B) It is possible for several legal regimes (ie foreign investment law and human rights law) to exist and develop in isolation of each other, ultimately culminating in the production of divergent rules of international law | C) Fragmentation is when States assume different interpretations of the same rule of international law | D) Fragmentation is when States disagree to abide by a certain rule of international law
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): B) Ó ṣe é ṣe fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìjọba  (ìyẹn òfin ìdókòwò ilẹ̀ òkèèrè àti òfin ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn) láti wà kí wọ́n sì ṣe ìdàgbàsókè ní ìyàsọ́tọ̀ ara wọn, nígbẹ̀yìn-gbẹ́yìn kí ó parí sí ṣíṣe àwọn òfin ìyàtọ̀ òfin àgbáyé.
- Verified Answer (English): B) It is possible for several legal regimes (ie foreign investment law and human rights law) to exist and develop in isolation of each other, ultimately culminating in the production of divergent rules of international law

search_context: Kí ni ìtumọ‌ àṣẹ tí a ò kọ kalẹ‌? | What is the meaning of implied authorisation? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni ìtumọ‌ àṣẹ tí a ò kọ kalẹ‌?
- English Question: What is the meaning of implied authorisation?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìgbàgbọ‌ ìfọwọ‌sowọ‌pọ‌ Ìgbìmọ‌ Ààbò fún àwọn ọmọ ogun nígbà tí wọ‌n bá ti kìlọ‌ fún ìpínlẹ‌ kan. | B) Àṣẹ tí kò hàn kedere lórí ìpìlẹ̀ iye ìbò pàtó láti ọwọ́ àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ UNSC. | C) Èrò pé gbogbo ìgbógun tí kò bófin mu yóò wà lábẹ́ àṣẹ àwọn ọmọ ogun pẹ̀lú ìpinnu UNSC | D) Fún àwọn ìgbà tí ìgbóguntini tí kò bófin mu léraléra bá ṣẹlẹ̀, UNSC yóò fún àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ tó wà ní àyíká láṣẹ láti gbé ìgbésẹ̀ yòówù tí wọ́n rò pé ó ṣe pàtàkì láti tún ipò náà ṣe.
- Options (English): A) Presumption of Security Council approval of armed force when a State has been forewarned | B) Implicit authorisation on the basis of a specific number of votes by UNSC members | C) Presumption that all unlawful attacks will be subject to armed force by a resolution of the UNSC | D) In cases of repeated unlawful attacks the UNSC shall authorise neighbouring States to take whatever measures they deem necessary to rectify the situation
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Ìgbàgbọ‌ ìfọwọ‌sowọ‌pọ‌ Ìgbìmọ‌ Ààbò fún àwọn ọmọ ogun nígbà tí wọ‌n bá ti kìlọ‌ fún ìpínlẹ‌ kan.
- Verified Answer (English): A) Presumption of Security Council approval of armed force when a State has been forewarned

search_context: Ta ló ní àṣẹ láti fi òǹtẹ‌ lu àdéhùn ní apá ìpínlẹ‌? | Who has the authority to conclude a treaty on the part of States? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:

- Yorùbá Question: Ta ló ní àṣẹ láti fi òǹtẹ‌ lu àdéhùn ní apá ìpínlẹ‌?
- English Question: Who has the authority to conclude a treaty on the part of States?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn aṣojú ìpínlẹ‌ tó kójú òṣùwọ‌n lo máa ń Fọwọ́sí àdéhùn náà. Àwọn olórí orílẹ‌-èdè, olórí ìjọba, àwọn mínísítà fún ọ‌rọ‌ ilẹ‌ òkèèrè àti àwọn olórí àwọn iṣẹ‌ ìjọba ni wọ‌n rò pé wọ‌n ní irú àṣẹ bẹ‌ẹ‌. | B) Àwọn olórí ìpínlẹ̀ àti Àwọn mínísítà fún ọ̀rọ̀ ilẹ̀ òkèèrè lè dúnàádúrà àwọn àdéhùn kí wọ́n sì fi ó te lù ú | C) Àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n ní 'gbogbo agbára' nìkan ni wọ́n ń ṣe ìdúnàádúrà àti pé kò sí ẹni tí wọ́n rò pé ó ní irú àṣẹ bẹ́ẹ̀. | D) Àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìjọba ìpínlẹ̀ nìkan ni wọ́n máa ń fi àṣẹ sí àdéhùn.
- Options (English): A) Treaties are concluded by the competent representatives of States. Heads of States, heads of governments, ministers of foreign affairs and heads of diplomatic missions are presumed to have such authority | B) Treaties may only negotiated and concluded by the heads of State and ministers of foreign affairs | C) Treaties are negotiated and signed only by the persons that bear the necessary 'full powers' and no person is presumed to hold such authority | D) Treaties are concluded only by members of the diplomatic missions of States
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn aṣojú ìpínlẹ‌ tó kójú òṣùwọ‌n lo máa ń Fọwọ́sí àdéhùn náà. Àwọn olórí orílẹ‌-èdè, olórí ìjọba, àwọn mínísítà fún ọ‌rọ‌ ilẹ‌ òkèèrè àti àwọn olórí àwọn iṣẹ‌ ìjọba ni wọ‌n rò pé wọ‌n ní irú àṣẹ bẹ‌ẹ‌.
- Verified Answer (English): A) Treaties are concluded by the competent representatives of States. Heads of States, heads of governments, ministers of foreign affairs and heads of diplomatic missions are presumed to have such authority

search_context: Ta ni 'alátakò ní gbogboògbà'? | Who is a 'persistent objector'? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Ta ni 'alátakò ní gbogboògbà'?
- English Question: Who is a 'persistent objector'?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ìpínlẹ‌ tí ó máa ń tako òfin tí ó wà nínú ìbéèrè lẹ‌yìn ìdásílẹ‌ rẹ‌. | B) Ìpínlẹ̀ tí kò gbà pé òfin náà dè é ní ìbéèrè fún ìgbà díẹ̀. | C) Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ó ń tako ìdásílẹ̀ òfin àṣà láti ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ rẹ̀ àti ní gbangba. | D) Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ó gba ìdásílẹ̀ òfin àṣà ṣùgbọ́n ó ń tako òfin náà.
- Options (English): A) The State which persistently objects to the rule in question after its formation | B) The State which denies to be bound by the rule in question for a short period | C) The State which persistently and publicly objects to the formation of a rule of customary law from its outset | D) The State which accepts the formation of a rule of customary law but it retains objections as to its content
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ó ń tako ìdásílẹ̀ òfin àṣà láti ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ rẹ̀ àti ní gbangba.
- Verified Answer (English): C) The State which persistently and publicly objects to the formation of a rule of customary law from its outset

pedagogical_answer:

- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni ìtumọ‌ ààbò àpapọ‌?

- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ẹ‌tọ‌ láti dáàbò bo ara rẹ‌ láti ọwọ‌ orílẹ‌-èdè tó ju orílẹ‌-èdè kan lọ tí wọ‌n jọ sowọ‌pọ‌ | B) Ẹ̀tọ́ àwọn alájọṣepọ̀ ẹni láti dáàbò bo ìpínlẹ̀ tí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ṣẹlẹ̀ sí. | C) Àṣẹ àwọn ọmọ ogun láti ọwọ́ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ààbò UN | D) Fífi owó sí iṣẹ́ ìtẹ̀síwájú àlàáfíà láti ọwọ́ Ìgbìmọ̀ Gbogbogbò UN

- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) Àṣẹ àwọn ọmọ ogun láti ọwọ́ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ààbò UN

- Verified Answer (English): A) On the one hand, naturalism is based on a set of rules that are of universal and objective scope and on the other hand, positivism is based on a structured and coherent legal system that is created by States in light of their interests and desires

pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ló lè mú kí rírú òfin ẹ‌tọ‌ ọmọnìyàn ní ìta agbègbè tí Ilé Ẹjọ‌ ECHR wà lábẹ‌ Ẹ‌tọ‌ Ọmọnìyàn?
- English Question: Under what circumstances do human rights violations taking place outside the territory of ECHR member States fall within the remit of the ECHR?

- Options (English): A) The ECHR applies outside Europe where human rights are violated by ECHR member States abroad | B) The ECHR applies extraterritorially in circumstances where a member State exercises effective control | C) The ECHR applies extraterritorially where a member State has contributed forces to a UN peacekeeping mission | D) The ECHR applies extraterritorially where human rights violations are taking place in former colonies of member States

pedagogical_answer:

- Options (English): A) Parties to a treaty should be cognizant of its terms and not misinterpret them | B) Parties to a treaty should safeguard the object and purpose of the treaty | C) Parties to a treaty should adhere to its terms in good faith | D) Parties to a treaty should not violate the most important provisions of the treaty

- Verified Answer (English): C) Parties to a treaty should adhere to its terms in good faith

search_context: Kí ni àbájáde àìtẹ‌lé òfin nínú ẹjọ‌ Ìgbìmọ‌ Tin? | What was the consequence from the absence of implementing legislation in the Tin Council case? | international_law

- Verified Answer (English): C) The absence of implementing legislation with respect to the Council's founding treaty meant that individuals did not derive rights and duties from it in the English legal system

- Options (English): A) The Human Rights Act 1998 incorporates the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law | B) The Human Rights Act 1998 allows a court to invalidate primary legislation | C) The Human Rights Act 1998 allows any person with a reasonable case to bring a case before a court | D) The Human Rights Act 1998 incorporates the EU charter of fundamental rights into UK law

- Options (English): A) Reparation may take only the form of pecuniary compensation, including the interest | B) Reparation denotes only the physical restitution of the wrongful act | C) Reparation includes restitution, compensation, and satisfaction, either alone or alongside other forms of reparation | D) The form of reparation is a matter for the responsible State to decide

- Verified Answer (English): C) Reparation includes restitution, compensation, and satisfaction, either alone or alongside other forms of reparation

- English Question: What is 'unilateral acts'?

- Verified Answer (English): B) They are acts creating unilateral legal obligations to the acting State

search_context: Ṣé ìjínigbé ní agbègbè mìíràn jẹ‌ ìdí fún ìkọ‌sílẹ‌ ẹjọ‌ òfin láti ọwọ‌ àwọn ilé ẹjọ‌ Gẹ‌ẹ‌sì? | Is extra-territorial abduction a ground for refusal of otherwise lawful jurisdiction by English courts? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:

- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Irú ìjínigbé bẹ́ẹ̀ jẹ́ ìlòkulò ìlànà ó sì yọrí sí ìdúró ìgbésẹ̀.

search_context: Kí ni ìtumọ‌ tí 'awọn ofin amúgbálẹ‌gbẹ‌ẹ‌' nínú òfin  ti ojúṣe káríayé? | What is the meaning of 'secondary rules' in the law of international responsibility? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:

- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni ìtumọ‌ tí 'awọn ofin amúgbálẹ‌gbẹ‌ẹ‌' nínú òfin  ti ojúṣe káríayé?

- Verified Answer (English): B) Secondary rules are the rules that govern the legal consequences arising from a breach of the primary rules, ie of the international obligations of the States

search_context: Kí ni ẹ‌kọ‌ àkójọpọ‌ sọ nípa àdéhùn? | What does the doctrine of incorporation suggest in respect of treaties? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni ẹ‌kọ‌ àkójọpọ‌ sọ nípa àdéhùn?
- English Question: What does the doctrine of incorporation suggest in respect of treaties?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Ẹ̀kọ́ àkójọpọ̀ nílò kí gbogbo àdéhùn ṣe àyípadà òfin kí wọ́n tó di òfin ìbílẹ̀. | B) The doctrine of incorporation does not require any further action at the domestic level | C) The doctrine of incorporation treats treaties as inferior to domestic law | D) Ẹ‌kọ‌ àkójọpọ‌ fi hàn pé àwọn àdéhùn tí wọ‌n fọwọ‌ sí máa ń wọ inú agbègbè òfin ìbílẹ‌ fúnra rẹ‌.
- Options (English): A) The doctrine of incorporation requires that all treaties undergo legislative transformation before they become domestic law | B) The doctrine of incorporation does not require any further action at the domestic level | C) The doctrine of incorporation treats treaties as inferior to domestic law | D) The doctrine of incorporation suggests that ratified treaties automatically pass into the sphere of domestic law
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): D) Ẹ‌kọ‌ àkójọpọ‌ fi hàn pé àwọn àdéhùn tí wọ‌n fọwọ‌ sí máa ń wọ inú agbègbè òfin ìbílẹ‌ fúnra rẹ‌.
- Verified Answer (English): D) The doctrine of incorporation suggests that ratified treaties automatically pass into the sphere of domestic law

search_context: Ṣé àwọn ìgbésẹ‌ àkọ‌kọ‌ tí ICJ gbé jáde wà fún àwọn ẹgbẹ‌ náà? | Are the provisional measures issued by the ICJ binding upon the parties? | international_law

search_context: Nígbà wo ni àwọn ọ‌nà àtakò kò bófin mu? | When are countermeasures illegal? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Nígbà wo ni àwọn ọ‌nà àtakò kò bófin mu?
- English Question: When are countermeasures illegal?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn ìlànà àtakò jẹ́ ohun tí kò bófin mu nígbà tí inter alia bá jẹ́ àìtọ́ tàbí tí ó rú ìlànà ìdènà òfin àgbáyé (fún àpẹẹrẹ lílo ipá, ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn) | B) Countermeasures are illegal when they are taken in the course of an armed conflict | C) Countermeasures are illegal when they violate bilateral treaties | D) Àwọn ọ‌nà àtakò kò bófin mu nígbà tí ìpínlẹ‌ tó jẹ‌ ojúṣe kò bá gbà wọ‌n.
- Options (English): A) Countermeasures are illegal when inter alia are disproportionate or in violation of a peremptory norm of international law (e.g. the use of force, human rights) | B) Countermeasures are illegal when they are taken in the course of an armed conflict | C) Countermeasures are illegal when they violate bilateral treaties | D) Countermeasures are illegal when the responsible State does not consent to them
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Àwọn ìlànà àtakò jẹ́ ohun tí kò bófin mu nígbà tí inter alia bá jẹ́ àìtọ́ tàbí tí ó rú ìlànà ìdènà òfin àgbáyé (fún àpẹẹrẹ lílo ipá, ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn)
- Verified Answer (English): A) Countermeasures are illegal when inter alia are disproportionate or in violation of a peremptory norm of international law (e.g. the use of force, human rights)

search_context: Kí ni ìyàtọ‌ láàrin ọ‌nà ìṣèlú àti ọ‌nà òfin ni píparí àríyànjiyàn? | What is the difference between political and legal means of dispute settlement? | international_law

[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:

- English Question: What is the difference between political and legal means of dispute settlement?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Àbájáde tí ó wáyé láti inú àwọn ọ̀nà òfin, bíi tàbí ìdájọ́ láti ọwọ́ ICJ, jẹ́ ìkẹyìn àti ìfẹsẹ̀múlẹ̀ lórí àwọn ẹgbẹ́, nígbà tí èyí kò rí bẹ́ẹ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀nà ìjọba. | B) The political methods are pursued upon the consent of then parties to the dispute, whereas the legal methods not | C) The political means lead to a final settlement of the dispute, whereas this is not the case with the legal methods | D) Àwọn ọ‌nà tí òfin ń lépa láti parí ija wà fún tó àwọn ìjà ńlá nìkan, bẹ‌ẹ‌ sì nìyí, àwọn ọ‌nà òṣèlú jẹ‌ èyí tí wọ‌n máa lò nínú gbogbo ìjà.

- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): A) Àbájáde tí ó wáyé láti inú àwọn ọ̀nà òfin, bíi tàbí ìdájọ́ láti ọwọ́ ICJ, jẹ́ ìkẹyìn àti ìfẹsẹ̀múlẹ̀ lórí àwọn ẹgbẹ́, nígbà tí èyí kò rí bẹ́ẹ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀nà ìjọba.
- Verified Answer (English): A) The outcome arising from legal methods, ie arbitration or adjudication by the ICJ, is final and binding upon the parties, whereas this is not the case with diplomatic methods

search_context: Kí ni ìdí fún ìrẹ‌wẹ‌sì àwọn àtúnṣe ìbílẹ‌ nínú ẹ‌tọ‌ ọmọnìyàn àgbáyé? | What is the rationale for the exhaustion of local remedies in international human rights? | international_law
pedagogical_answer:
[Subject: international_law | Academic Bilingue Reference]:
- Yorùbá Question: Kí ni ìdí fún ìrẹ‌wẹ‌sì àwọn àtúnṣe ìbílẹ‌ nínú ẹ‌tọ‌ ọmọnìyàn àgbáyé?
- English Question: What is the rationale for the exhaustion of local remedies in international human rights?
- Options (Yorùbá): A) Òfin àtúnṣe ìbílẹ̀ ní èrògbà láti dá àwọn ilé ẹjọ́ àgbáyé sílẹ̀ láti kojú àwọn ẹjọ́ tó burú jù. | B) The local remedies rule aims to dissuade applicants abusing the system from filing unnecessary petitions | C) The local remedies rule aims on the one hand to restrict the volume of petitions to international tribunals while at the same time building up the capacity of local courts | D) Òfin àtúnṣe ìbílẹ‌ ń ṣe ìrànlọ‌wọ‌ láti fi hàn pé àwọn ilé ẹjọ‌ orílẹ‌-èdè máa ń wà ní ipò tó dára ju àwọn àgbáyé lọ láti kojú ẹjọ‌.
- Options (English): A) The local remedies rule aims to free up international tribunals to deal with the most serious cases | B) The local remedies rule aims to dissuade applicants abusing the system from filing unnecessary petitions | C) The local remedies rule aims on the one hand to restrict the volume of petitions to international tribunals while at the same time building up the capacity of local courts | D) The local remedies rule helps demonstrate that national courts are always better placed than international ones to deal with cases
- Verified Answer (Yorùbá): C) The local remedies rule aims on the one hand to restrict the volume of petitions to international tribunals while at the same time building up the capacity of local courts
- Verified Answer (English): C) The local remedies rule aims on the one hand to restrict the volume of petitions to international tribunals while at the same time building up the capacity of local courts

search_context: Kini idi rẹ ti awọn aworan ori amohunmaworan fi ni ila gige ni ibi awọn ibode wọn? | Why do the images on television have their borders cut?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Òkan lára àwọn ìṣòro tó wọ́pọ̀ nígbà tí ènìyàn ń gbìyànjú láti yí sinima padà sí èrò DVD ni ìṣújù . Ọ̀pọ̀ ẹ̀rọ amóhùnmáwòrán ni wọ́n ṣẹ̀dá láti tẹ́ àwọn ará ìlú lọ́rùn. Fun idi eyi, gbogbo nkan ti o ba n ri lori amohunmaworan ni won ge ala okoe, isale ati egbegbe re kuro. Èyí ni láti ri wípé àwòrán náà bo gbogbo ìbòjú. Òhun ni wọ́n ń pè ní ìṣíjú. Ó ṣeni láàánú pé tí o bá ṣe DVD, eteti rẹ náà ṣe é ṣe kí ó gé kúrò pẹ̀lú, tí fídíò náà bá ní àdàkọ sií èdè mìíràn tí o sì súnmọ́ abẹ́, wọn ò ní hàn dáadáa.
[Reading Passage (English)]: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan. Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public. For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides. This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan. Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Nitori naa awọn aworan yii gba gbogbo oju aṣafihan
[Verified Answer (English)]: So the image fills the entire screen

search_context: Nibo ni ile-ogun Orilẹ-ede Gẹẹsi kan wa? | Where was there a British garrison located?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ètò ìlú Amerika gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé kíkọjú ìjàkadì láti ibi ọ̀tọ̀tọ̀ mẹ́ta. Ọ̀gágun John Cadwalder ma ṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ ìkọlù ìyàtọ̀ tó lòdì sí British garrison ní Bordentown, láti lè dínà fún ìrànlọ́wọ́. Ọ̀gágun James Ewing yóò kó ọmọ ológun ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀rin fo oi tó wà ní Trenton Ferry, gba afárá lórí Odọ̀ Assunpinki, gbégi rénà ikọ̀ ọlọ̀tẹ̀ kí wọ́n má lè sá. Àwọn ikọ̀ ajagun tí okùnrin ẹgbẹ̀rún méjì ó lé irinwó máa la odò máìlì mẹ́san ní apá àríwá Trenton kọjá, wọ́n á sì pín sí ọ̀wọ̣́ méjì; ọ̀kan lábę Greene àti ọ̀kan láẹ́ Sullivan, láti lè se àkọlù kílẹ̀ tó mọ́.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions. General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements. General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping. The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Bordentown
[Verified Answer (English)]: Bordentown

search_context: Ibuwọlu tani o han lori iwe kikọ ti a fi ọwọ kọ? | Whose signature appeared on the handwritten draft?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá yálò ní ọjọ́ Agemo 4 wọn fi atọ́kùnwò rẹ̀ ti Àrẹ Kongresi Johanu Hankoki àti akọ̀we Ṣalsi Tomsini fọwọ́sí ránṣẹ́ sí ilé ìtẹ̀jáde Johanu Dunlapi tí ò jìnà. Bíi ẹ̀dà̀ àádọ́jọ sí igba ni wọ́n se mọ́jú tí a ńpè ní “Dunlap broadsides”. John Niksoni lo ka iwe naa nigba akoko ti won maa ka ni gbanga ni ogba Hoolu Ominira ni Agemo 8. Wọ́n fi ìkan ránṣẹ́ sí George Washington ní ọjọ́ lẹfà oṣù kẹje, tó kàá fún àwọn ikọ̀ rẹ ní New York ní ọja kẹssàn oṣù kẹje. Ẹ̀dà kan dé London ní ọja kẹwàá oṣù kẹjọ. Ìwọ̀n mẹ́ẹ̀dógbọ̀n ìwé fẹ̀rẹ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ti Dunlap èyí tí a mọ̀ wípé ó jẹ́ ẹ̀dà àkọọ́lẹ̀ tó dàgbà jù tó sì wà. Àpilẹkọ̀ ẹ̀dà náà gan-an kò sí mọ́.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "After its adoption by Congress on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by the President of Congress John Hancock and the Secretary Charles Thomson was then sent a few blocks away to the printing shop of John Dunlap. Through the night between 150 and 200 copies were made, now known as ""Dunlap broadsides"". The first public reading of the document was by John Nixon in the yard of Independence Hall on July 8. One was sent to George Washington on July 6, who had it read to his troops in New York on July 9. A copy reached London on August 10. The 25 Dunlap broadsides still known to exist are the oldest surviving copies of the document. The original handwritten copy has not survived."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Charles Thomson

Nigba ti o ti je pe awon akeeko mma n tako ju, onkowe blogi ma n sa gbogbo agbara lati dara si ki o baa le yera fun itako. Blogging, “ti kàn án nípá fáwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ láti fẹ ní ìmọ̀ àti òye kíkún nípa ayé tó yí wọn ká” èròǹgbà àti ìlò láti wo ṣàkun ohun tí àwọn olùgbọ́ ń fẹ́ kí wọn sì ṣe e fún wọn ni ó mú kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ gbọ́n nínú gbọ́n ní ìlta, tí wọ́n si ń ṣe ohun tó móríyá. (Toto, 2004) Búlọ́gìn jẹ́ ohun èlò tó ń ṣe ìwúrí fún àjọṣepọ̀, tí ó sì ń ṣe ìrànwọ́ fún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ láti mú ìmọ̀ ẹ̀kọ́ kọjá ilé ẹ̀kọ́. Lílo ìtàkùn Blog ní ọ̀nà tí ó tọ́ “lè ró àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní agbára láti di ẹni tó ń wo nǹkan ní àwòfín, tí yóò si lè ṣe ọ̀rínkíniwin rẹ̀; látàrí fífèsì tí ó tọ̀nà sí àwọn nǹkan tí ẹnìyàn ń rí lórí ayélujara, akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè sọ nípa ohun tí wọn rò ní pa elọmìíran tàbí sọ èròwọn nípa nǹkan kí nǹkan (Oravec, 2002).
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Blogs can also help improve student writing. While students often begin their blog experience with sloppy grammar and spelling, the presence of an audience generally changes that. Since students are often the most critical audience, the blog writer begins to strive to improve writing to avoid criticism. Also blogging ""forces students to become more savvy about the world around them."" The need to feed the interest of the audience inspires students to be clever and interesting (Toto, 2004). Blogging is a tool that inspires collaboration, and encourages students to extend learning well beyond the traditional school day. Appropriate use of blogs ""can empower students to become more analytical and critical; through actively responding to Internet materials, students can define their positions in the context of others' writings as well as outline their own perspectives on particular issues (Oravec, 2002)."

search_context: Tani o ṣe awari idunpada onfa nukila?  | Who discovered nuclear magnetic resonance?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: MRI dálórí kàyéfì fisiksi ta n pè ní nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), tí Felisi Boṣi (tó n ṣiṣẹ́ ní Ile Iwe Giga Stanfodi) àti Edwodi Pọseli (láti Ile Iwe Giga Hafadi) wárí ní 1930s. Nínú àbájáde yìí, àwọn pápá agbérin àti ìgbì rádíò tó ń fa átọ̀mù tó fún àwọn rádìò kéèkèé ní àfihàn. Ní ọdún 1970, dókítà oníṣègùn òyìnbó àti ìwádìí ìmò sáyẹ́nsì, Raymond Damadian, ṣàwárí lílo ohun òǹfà ìgbohún-pẹ̀lú -àwòrán jáde gẹ́gẹ́ bí ẹ̀rọ fún àyẹ̀wò àwọn ìwádìí àìsàn. Lẹ́yìn ọdún mẹ́rin wọ́n fàṣe sí ẹ̀tọ́ náà, ó jẹ́ ẹ̀tọ́ àkọ́kọ́ tí wọ́n ma fàṣę sí nínú ẹ̀kọ MRI. Ni 1977, Dokita Damadiani pari kiko skana MRI “ti gbogbo ara” to pe ni “Ailesegun”.
[Reading Passage (English)]: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University). In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals. In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis. Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI. In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Bloch ati Purcell
[Verified Answer (English)]: Bloch and Purcell

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àrà ìkọ̀wé Gothic lé téńté ní àkókò séńtúrì kẹwàá sí ikọkànlá àti ikẹrìnlá. Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ àṣà Bisantini ni apá ìlà orùn ni ipá púpọ̀ lórí aṣọ. Àmọ́ṣá, látàrí ìlànà ìbáraẹnisọ̀rọ̀ tó falẹ̀, àwọn àrà lẹ́kùn ìwọ̀ oòrùn le wà lẹ́yìn pẹ̀lú bí i ọdún márùndínlọ́gbọ̀n sí ọgbọ̀n ọdún. ní ìparí Middle ages western Europe bẹ̀rẹ̀ láti ṣàgbéga àrà wọn, ìkan lára ìdàgbàsókè tó tóbi jùlọ látàrí crusades àwọn ènìyàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní lo àwọn bọ́tìnnì láti de aṣọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century. At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east. However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year. towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn Ogun ẹsin
[Verified Answer (English)]: The Crusades

search_context: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí oju ewe náà, èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni a kà sí ojútùú pípẹ́ sí àwọn iṣoro àyíká? | According to the passage, which of the following is considered a viable longterm solution to environmental issues?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: A lè bẹ̀rẹ̀ sih ní gbeh ìgbé ayé to faramọ́ra, bẹ́ẹ̀ sì ni a tún lè jẹ́ ajàjàgbara kí a lè mú àdínkù bá ìyà tí o le. Èyí dàbi wíwo àwọn àmà àìsàn ni ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà. Sùgbón, tí a kọ ba fẹ ojútuu ránpẹ, a nílò làti wá ìdí àwọn ìṣòro náà, ki´ a si yanjú wọn. Ó hàn kedere wípé ayé ti yípadà gidigidi pèlú ìlọsíwájú ìmọ̀-èrọ àti sáyẹ̀nsì láti ọwó ẹ̀dá ènìyàn, àti wípé ìṣòro ti di púpọ̀ nípasè pípọ̀ làpọ̀jù àti ìgbé ayé àsẹjù.
[Reading Passage (English)]: We can start living more friendly to the environment, we can join to the environmental movement, and we can even be activists in order to reduce the future suffering in some degree. This is just like symptomatic treatment in many cases. However, if we do not only want a temporary solution, then we should find the root of the problems, and we should deactivate them. It is obvious enough that the world has changed much because of humankind's scientific and technological advancements, and problems have become greater because of overpopulation and mankind's extravagant lifestyle.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Idamọ idi ti awọn ọran
[Verified Answer (English)]: Identifying the cause of the issues

search_context: Ni orilẹ-ede wo ni ogun akọkọ ni Yuroopu ni iṣoro rẹ gan jẹ ti iwọntunwọnsi agbara ni dipo ti ẹsin? | In which country was the first war in Europe whose central issue was said to relate to the balance of power rather than having a religious context?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìsedédé agbára ni ètò tí ilẹ̀ Europu ń lò láti fi se ìsàkóso ìjẹgàba àpapọ̀ àwọn orílẹ̀ Europu lápapọ. Èróngbà ni pé gbogbo orílẹ̀ èdè Europe níláti wà láti lè dènà orílẹ̀ èdè kan láti má ní agbára, àti pé ìjọba ma ń yí ọ̀rẹ́ wọn kí wọ́n bá lè ní ìwọ̀ntúnwọ̀nsí. Ogun Igbapò ilẹ̀ Spain ni ó jẹ́ alákọ̀ọ́kọ́ tí yóò dá lórí dídọ́gba agbára. Eleyi jẹ apẹẹrẹ ti o ṣe pataki, bi awọn alagbara alawọ funfun ko ṣe ni ma lugọ sẹyin ogun ẹsin mọ. Bẹẹni, Ogun Ọlọgbọn Ọdun naa ni yio jẹ eyi ti o gbẹyin ti a o pẹ ni ogun ẹsin.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states. The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance. The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power. This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Orilẹ-ede Sipeni
[Verified Answer (English)]: Spain

search_context: Èwo nínú àwọn abala tí ijọ Kátólíìkì ní a kò ṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ̀? | Which of the following aspects of the Catholic Church was not being scrutinized?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ni akoko yi ni itan abalaye Yuropi, Ijo Katoliki, to ti di olow ati alagbara, wa labe imojuto fini fini. Fún ẹgbẹgbẹ̀rùn ọdún sẹ́yìn ẹ̀sì krìstíẹ́nì tí so àwọn orílẹ̀ èdè Europe papọ̀ pẹ̀lú èdè àti àṣa wọn tó yàtọ̀. Gbogbo ènìyàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ láti orí ọba lọ sí orí àwọn ará ìlú ni agbara gbogbogbò yíò sèpalára fún. Ọ̀kan lára òpó ẹ̀sìn kìrìsìtíẹ́nì ni pé, ọrọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ lílò láti fi mún ìyà àti ìṣẹ́ tán nílẹ̀ àti wípé àwọn owó ìjọ wà fún ìdí pàtàki náà. Àṣe nlá ìjọ ti wà ní Rómù ó lé ní ęgbẹ̀rún ọdún, ìkójọpọ̀ agbára àti owó yí tí jẹ́kí àwọn èyàn ma ṣèyemẹ́jì pé bóyá a gbọ́ràn sí òfin yí.
[Reading Passage (English)]: During this period of European history, the Catholic Church, which had become rich and powerful, came under scrutiny. For over a thousand years the Christian religion had bound European states together despite differences in language and customs. I Its all-pervading power affected everyone from king to commoner. One of the main Christian tenets is that wealth should be used to alleviate suffering and poverty and that the monetary funds of the church are there specifically for that reason. The central authority of the church had been in Rome for over a thousand years and this concentration of power and money led many to question whether this tenet was being met.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Bi o ba yẹ ki a ṣe atunṣe awọn ilana gboogi ti ẹsin
[Verified Answer (English)]: If the main tenets of the religion should be amended

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, tani wọn pa ni Versailles? | According to the passage, who was murdered at Versailles?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ọba búburú Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette àwọn ọmọ wọn kékèké méjì ( Marie Therese, ọmọ ọdún mọ́kànlá àti Louis-Charles ọmọ ọdún mẹ́rin) àti àbúrò ọba obìnrin Madam Elizabeth, ní ọjọ́ kẹfà, oṣù kẹwa ọdún 1789, ni ọ̀gọọrọ̀ àwọn ìyá ọlọ́jà lé jáde pada sí Paris láti Versailles. Nínu kẹ̀kẹ́ ẹṣin, wọ́n rìrìn àjò padà sí Paris àwọn ènìyàn sí yí wọn kà , wọ́n han, wọ́n sì ń pariwo ìdérùba Ọba àti Aya ọba. Àwọn èèyàn tínú ń bí tí kan ọba àti olorì nípá láti má a ṣí fèrèsé ohun èlò tó ń gbé wọn lọ sílẹ̀. Nígbà tóyá, ọ̀kan lára àwọn èrò ju orí olórí ẹ̀ṣọ́ tí wọ́n sekúpa ni Versaille síwájú ayaba tẹ́rù ti ń bà.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women. In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen. The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open. At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Oluṣọ kan
[Verified Answer (English)]: A guard

search_context: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí kii ṣe àbájáde ogun aiṣedeede ọojú omi ti ilẹ̀ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì? | Which of the following was not a result of Britain’s unconventional naval warfare?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Láìpẹ́ tí ìfúngunmọ́ni bẹ̀rẹ̀, Ilẹ̀ Britian bẹ̀rẹ̀ síní fi ikọ̀ ológun ojú omi dá ilẹ̀ Germany dúró. Ọgbọ́n náà dára, yíyọ àwọn ǹkan èlò tí ológun àti àwọn ènìyàn, ṣùgbọ́n ìdènà yìí kò tọ̀nà fún òfin orílẹ̀èdè tí wọ́n fọwọ́sí tí àwọn tó wà ní òkè òkun fọwọ́sí fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọdún sẹ́yìn. Britain ma ń wa omi òkun tí àwọn ọka ojú omi ma ń gbà kọjá láti má jẹ́ kí èyíkèyí okọ̀ ojú omi wo gbogbo abala òkun náà, tó ma fa ewu fún àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi tí kò mọ ǹkankan. Torí pé èsì sí ìgbésẹ̀ náà ò pọ̀, Jamani retí irú èsì bẹ́ẹ̀ sí ìjàkadì ọkọ̀ abẹ́ omi t’aláìhámọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany. The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries. Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships. Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: A ṣe awọn ayipada si ofin agbaaye
[Verified Answer (English)]: Changes were made to international law
