search_context: Dida lori oju ewe naa, fun tani ayẹwo ti Ọpọ Sclerosis yoo jẹ julọ? | Based on the passage, for whom would a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis be most likely?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Káàkiri orílẹ̀èdè America, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àìsàn ọpọlọ àti ògóró ẹ̀yìn (MS) tí ó tó irinwó ẹgbẹ̀rún, èyí tí ó mún un di àìsàn tó nííse pẹ̀lú ọpọlọ láàrin àwọn ọ̀dọ́ àti àwọn tí ó wà ní agbedeméjì ọjọ́ orí tí ó pọ̀jù lọ ní ìwádìí ti fìdi rẹ̀ múnlẹ̀. MS je aarun ti o ma n se akoba fun aringbungbun eto ainifokanbale ti o niise pelu opolo, ogoro eyin ati opa ofoolo. Ìwádí ti gbé jáde pé obìnrin ní ìlọ́po méjì ma ń sábà ní MS ju okùnrin lọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Across the United States of America, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), leaving it as the leading neurological disease in younger and middle aged adults. MS is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which is made up of the brain, the spinal cord and the optic nerve. Research has found that females are two times more likely to have MS then males.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Arabinrin ọdun 32 kan
[Verified Answer (English)]: A 32 year old female

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, awọn olukopa ninu iṣẹ ṣiṣe deede nilo atilẹyin diẹ sii fun kini? | According to the passage, participants in regular activity required more support for what?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Iṣẹ́ ìwádìí náà fìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ pé ìbànújẹ́, ẹ̀rù àti àjálù má a ń ṣokùnfà ìrora àti àìlera fún àwọn tó má a ń ní ìrora ní ìsàlẹ̀ ẹ̀hìn. Awọn ipa ti ajalu nikan, kiise ibanujẹ tabi ẹru ni o jẹ awọn isẹlẹ gbẹdẹkẹ ọlọsọọsẹ ti akoko PA. Àwọn tó n ṣe ìṣe dédé wọn nílò ìgbèlẹ́yìn sí nípasẹ̀ ojú burúkú tí a fi n rí ẹ̀dùn sí, láti tọ́ka sí ìyàtọ̀ láàrín ẹ̀dùn ti o jẹ́ àìsàn àti ẹ̀dùn tí o wáyé torípé a gbọn ara.

Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions. Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Iwoye odi ti irora
[Verified Answer (English)]: Negative perception of pain

search_context: Dida lori oju ewe naa, kini ihi okuta Muhammad sọ nipa awọn iṣẹ ẹmi ati ihhuwasi rẹ? | Based on the passage, what does Muhammad’s cave say about his spiritual practices or values?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn ohun tó kọjá ayé yìí jẹ Muhammad lógún. Ó má ń lọ síbi ihò kan tí ó di ohun tí wọ́n mọ̀ sí “iHira” lórí òkè “Noor” (ìmọ́lẹ̀) fún àsàrò. ó dé ara rẹ̀ pamọ́, ó sì yè, èyí fún wa ní àwòrán ìfa ọkàn nípa ti ẹ̀mi Mohammad. Ìsinmi lórí ọ̀kan lára àwọn òkè àríwá Mecca, ihò àpáta náà ni a yàsọ́tọ̀ sí ìyókù lágbàáyé. Kódà kò rọrùn láti wárí rárá tí èyàn bá tiẹ̀ mọ̀ pé ó wà. Tóba ti wà ní òkúta àpámọ́, o ma dáwà pátá pátá. Kòsí ǹkan tí a lè rí ju ojú ọ̀run tó rẹwà tó sì mọ́lẹ̀ lókè àti ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn orí òkè tó yiká. Díẹ̀ lára àgbáyé yìí ní a lè rí tàbí gba láti inú ihò.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation. he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations. Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world. In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation. Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: O fẹran alaafia ati iyara-ẹni sọtọ
[Verified Answer (English)]: He values peace and isolation

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, kini wọn kọkọ lo irin fun? | According to the passage, what was iron used for first?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Wọ́n tí kọ́ Wágọ́nwè ní Ìlu Gẹ̀ẹ́sì láti sẹ́ntúrí 16th. Lóòótọ́ àwọn ohun tí wọ́n fi ń wọ́ kẹ̀kẹ́ akẹ́rù ní àwọn pákó pẹlẹbẹ pẹlẹbẹ, wọ́n má ń lo àwọn ẹṣin tó ń wọ́wọn láti lè sáré dáadáa, le fa ẹrù tó pọ̀ láwọn ọ̀nọ̀ tí kò tọ́ dáadáa. Wọ́n tètè sàfihàn àwọn ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ojú ọ̀nà irin láti sàrídájú pé àwọn ipa wà déédé. Ó sàfihàn wípé àwọn ipa yìí yóó múná dóko bíwọ́n bá ní ọ̀pá irin lókè. Eléyìí di ìse, sùgbọ́n irin mún kí àwọn pákó ẹsẹ̀ ọkọ̀ jẹ. Àmọ́ ṣá wọ́n fi wíìli onírin dípo wíìlì onípákó. Ní ọdún 1767 wọ́n gbe réèli onírín láti òkè délẹ̀ àkọ́kó irú rẹ̣̀ jáde.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Wagonways were built in England as early as the 16th Century. Although wagonways merely consisted of parallel planks of wood, they allowed horses pulling them to achieve greater speeds and pull larger loads than on the slightly more rough roads of the day. Crossties were introduced fairly early to hold the tracks in place. Gradually, however, it was realised that tracks would be more efficient if they had a stip of iron on the top. This became common practice, but the iron caused more wear on the wooden wheels of the wagons. Eventually, wooden wheels were replaced by iron wheels. In 1767, the first full-iron rails were introduced.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn irin igbedabu ojurin
[Verified Answer (English)]: Crossties

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, kini o ṣayipada ẹnikọọkan lakoko igbe aye Romanu? | According to the passage, what shaped individuals during the period of Romanticism?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Romantisimi ma n sába dá àṣà láti àwọn akosile awọn akọ̀wé bío Gọẹ́tì, Fíṣtì àti Ṣlegel. Ní ìlànà tí àkójọpọ̀ ẹgbẹ́ oníse, ẹ̀kọ́ nípa ìpìlẹ̀ ayé tún oníkálukú dá, bí ọjọ́ se ń gorí ọjọ́, ìṣe àti àṣà tí ó lọ́ mọ́ àgbéǹde ìpìlẹ̀ ayé, pẹ̀lú bí èyí se wà nísọ̀kan pẹ̀lú ipò àwùjọ èyí tó dára ju àwọn òfi àfipá gbé kalẹ̀.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel. In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ẹkọ nipa ile aye
[Verified Answer (English)]: Geography

search_context: Ewo ninu awọn alaye yii ni ko ṣafihan eronu gbogboogbo ni ti ipinnu imọ ẹrọ?  | Which of the following statements does not reflect a general idea of technological determinism?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìpinnu tí ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ jé asayan ọ̀rọ̀ gbogbogbò fún orísirísi àwọn ìlóyẹ fún ìmúsisé to´ gbòòro, kíkànípá ìmò-ẹ̀rọ tábì pàtàkì ìmò-ẹ̀rọ sí ìwòyẹ tàràtà wípé àwọn àmúyẹ ìwòyẹ tó nísẹ pèlú àwọn òfin ìmọ̀ sayenisi àti ìfarahàn wọn nípa ìmò-ẹ̀rọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí atọ́kùn kádàrá éníyán. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìtunmọ̀ ìpinu ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ pín àbá méjì, pé ìdágbàsóké ìms ẹ̀rọ fún rarẹ̀ fàyègba ọ̀nà tó jù àṣà àti òṣèlù lọ, ìms ẹ̀rọ nà ní “ipa” lóri àwùjọ tí a jogúnbá, jú àwùjọ ìlóniníyè lọ. Fún àpęrę à lè sọ pé ọkọ ló ń sokùnfà àtúnse àwọn ojú ọ̀nà. Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, ojú pópó jákèjádò orílẹ̀-èdè fún àwọn awakọ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́ péréte kò le di síse pẹ̀lú bí ètò ọrọ̀ ajẹ́ sẹ rí, nítorínà àwọn ọ̀nà titun fùn ìselọ́pọ́ tó ń jẹyọ láti dín owó ríra ọkọ̀ kù. Bi opo eyan se ni moto ma n mu ki ijamba oko oju ona po si, iyen naa ma n muu ki aseda awon ona titun ni iwosan ara eyan to ti kolu ijamba.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology. Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has ""effects"" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned. For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads. However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership. Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ipa imọ ẹrọ ni awujọ jẹ awujọ iloniloye
[Verified Answer (English)]: Technology’s effects on society are socially conditioned

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, ewo ni koni fii ṣe pẹlu fifa ohun ifa ọfa? | According to the passage, which of the following is not associated with pulling the bow?
pedagogical_answer:

Òkè túmọ̀ sí wípé kí o bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní etí góńgó kí o sì taari ọrún, àti pé ìsàlẹ̀ túmọ̀ sí pé kí o bẹ̀rẹ̀ nísàlẹ̀ (níbití ọwọ́ rẹ ti di ọrún mún. Orun-oke ma n saba dun kelekele, orun-isale ma n dun ni ohun lile to lase. O ní àǹfànní láti fi gègé kọ àwọn àmì tìrẹ, sùgbọ́n rántí wípé ìlà àtẹ̀jáde tó wà níbẹ̀ wà fún iṣẹ́ orin, nítorínà wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ bíbọ̀wọ̀ fún.

An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive. Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected."

search_context: Awọn fosili fihan wi pe ọwọ se pataki ni lilo lakọkọ fun awọn wọnyi? | Fossils show that hands eventually adapted to be used primarily for which following?
pedagogical_answer:

Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

[Verified Answer (English)]: Manipulation

pedagogical_answer:

Ìrírí wa lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ pélù sísẹsé fúnraeni àti fífi àlàyé síta, àwọn àfihàn amóhùnmáwòrán fún ìkẹ́ẹ́kọ́ sàpèjúwẹ ìtọ́kasí yìí. Opolopo ninu wa ni a ba ara wa ti a n wo ere ori amohunmaworan to sàfihàn iriri tabi isesi ti a o le kopa ninu tabi ya imo re lo lai lai. [Reading Passage (English)]: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn. In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented. Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point. So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge. We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Kosi ọna ikẹkọọ kan to dara ju
[Verified Answer (English)]: There are no absolutes in learning

Eyi je ki o re ara bi eni wipe eniyan nilo lati ma ji iseju ogun si ogbon lera-lera lati wo ero mohunmaworan. Àbájádẹ yìí dálé lórí bí ọpọlọ rẹ se n sakitiyan láti la àlá kẹdẹrẹ ní alẹlẹ́.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting. This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV. The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

[Reading Passage (English)]: Virtual teams are held to the same standards of excellence as conventional teams, but there are subtle differences. Virtual team members often function as the point of contact for their immediate physical group. The presence of a true “invisible team” (Larson and LaFasto, 1989, p109) is also a unique component of a virtual team. The “invisible team” is the management team to which each of the members report. The invisible team sets the standards for each member.

search_context: Ewo ninu awọn atẹle wọnyi ni ko ṣe apejuwe ọna kika fọtoyiya 35mm? | Which of the following does not describe the 35mm photography format?
pedagogical_answer:

Abala ìpín fọ́màtì yìí (pínpín pẹ̀lú méjìlá láti lè ní odidi nọ́ḿbà onípínpín) ni a ma ní ó jẹ́ 3:2. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìgúnrégé (ìgúnrégé ebí APS, fún àpẹrẹ) dọ́gba sí tàbí súmọ ìpín náà.
[Reading Passage (English)]: For example, the most common still image photography format in the world is 35mm, which was the dominant film size at the close of the analog film era. The 35mm format is actually, somewhat confusingly, 36mm in width by 24mm in height. The aspect ratio of this format (dividing by twelve to obtain the simplest whole-number ratio) is therefore said to be 3:2. Many common formats (APS family of formats, for example) are equal to or closely approximate this aspect ratio.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: O ni ipin ti o yatọ ju ọpọlọpọ awọn ọna kika ti o wọpọ lọ
[Verified Answer (English)]: It has a different aspect ratio than many common formats

pedagogical_answer:

Kii se isoro pupo mo nitori pe awon to n se lensi ti n se aseyori ni iselopo lensi. Èyí jẹ́ kí lẹ́nsì tó lè ṣàmùgbòrò láti gbé àwọn ojúlówó àwòrán jáde k;i a fi wé lẹ́nsì tó jé pé kò lè ṣe àmúgbòrò àwòrán. Àléébù mìíràn tí lẹ́ǹsì àwosúnsún nipé bi ihò bà ṣe tóbi sí (bí o ṣe yára sí ) bẹẹni lẹ́ǹsì lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà yíò sì kéré sí . Èyí mún kí àwọn àwo amúnìkangbòòrò nira láti lò níbi tí òòye kò ti pọ̀ láìsí ìtànsán.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses. This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production. This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length. Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower. This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

Wọn pẹ ara wọn ní àwọn ónilé ẹrẹ́kúsú Polynesia àwọn àkùdẹ́ díè bàwọn ní ìgbẹ̀yìn, àwọn ónilé ẹrẹ́kúsú Polynesia di píparẹ́.

However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture. There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand. They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

[Reading Passage (English)]: "Attention Deficit Disorder ""is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy"". Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation. These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they ""engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority"" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods. search_context: Kini awọn ọmọ ogun ori omi Jamani n gbiyanju lati ṣaṣeyọri lakoko WWII? | What was the German navy trying to accomplish during WWII?
pedagogical_answer:

Ìkan lára àpẹrẹ́ má le gbàgbé ti ìkéde North Atlantic ti WWII. Àwọn Amẹ́ríkà ń gbìyànjú láti gbé àwọn ọkùnrin àti àwọn ǹkan èlò kọjá Atlantic Ocean láti ran Britain lọ́wọ́. [Reading Passage (English)]: Using ships to transport goods is by far the most efficient way to move large amounts of people and goods across oceans. The job of navies has traditionally been to ensure that your country maintains the ability to move your people and goods, while at the same time, interfering with your enemy's ability to move his people and goods. One of the most noteworthy recent examples of this was the North Atlantic campaign of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help Britain. At the same time, the German navy, using mainly U-boats, was trying to stop this traffic. Had the Allies failed, Germany probably would have been able to conquer Britain as it had the rest of Europe.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Idilọwọ awọn Briteni lati gba eniyan ati ẹru
[Verified Answer (English)]: Preventing Britain from receiving people and goods

search_context: Igba wo ni Ọba Tutankhamun di onijagidijagan? | When did King Tutankhamun gain notoriety?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Bẹ́ẹ̀ni! Ọba Tutankhamun, ti wọ́n fi ìgbà kan pè ní “King Tut” tàbí “ọba àwọn ọkùnrin”, jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára ọba Egypt àtijọ́ tí ó gbajúmọ̀ ní ayé òdi òní. Bi ìyanilénu, wọn kò ka kún èyàn Pàtàkì ní àyẹ àtijọ́ wọn o dẹ kọ orúkọ rẹ sílè ni púpọ̀ nínú àwọn àkọsílè ọba àtijọ́. Àmọ́ṣá, síse àwárí ibojì rẹ̀ ní 1922 sọ ọ́ di olóòkìkí. Niigbàtí wọ́n ja ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ibojì látẹ̀yìnwá lólè, ibojì yìí nìkan ní wọ́n fi sílẹ̀ láì fọwọ́kàn. Wọ́n ti dá ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ohun èlò tí wọ́n sin pẹ̀lú Tutankhamun sí, lára è ní ẹgbẹ̀lẹ́gbẹ̀ iṣẹ́ ọnà tí wọ́n se pẹ̀lú irin àti òkúta tó ṣọ̀wọ́n.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as ""King Tut"" or ""The Boy King"", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times. Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists. However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed. Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Lakoko isawari iboji rẹ
[Verified Answer (English)]: After the discovery of his tomb

search_context: Awọn ẹgbẹ wo ni yoo fẹ lati jẹun lailo ijoko? | Which group would prefer to dine without chairs?

[Reading Passage (English)]: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals. search_context: Dida lori oju ewe naa, ewo ninu wọnyi ni kole ni ipa lọ titi? | Based on the passage, which of the following is unlikely to have a lasting impact?
pedagogical_answer:

Ọ̀rọ̀ tí à ń pè ní ọ̀làjú wá látí inú èdè ìlú Latin, èyí tó túmọ̀ sí ọ̀làjú ilẹ̀ Latin, civitas túmọ̀ sí ìlú tàbí ìpínlẹp àti pé wọ́n tún fi í se àlàyé bí àwùjọ se tóbi tó. Àwọn ìlú-ìpinle jẹ àwọn ìsáájú fún àwọn orílè-èdè. Àsà tí ọ̀làjù túnmò sí ìfìoyẹ lẹ́lẹ̀ kọjá ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìran, nípasẹ̀ àsà asájú àti ìtànkálẹ̀ ìtẹ̀lẹ́ra. Àwọn àṣà kéèké ma ń pòórá lá ì fi ìtàn kankan sílẹ̀ bí ẹ̀rí, wọn kì í si ri í lò gẹ́gẹ́ bí ohun ìlàjú tó yẹ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society. The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society. City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination. Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.

search_context: Ewo ninu alaye yii nipa Drukgyal Dzong ni kii ṣe otitọ? | Which statement about The Drukgyal Dzong is not true?
pedagogical_answer:

Wọ́n sọ ọ́ di mímọ̀ pé lọ́dun 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel sèdásílẹ̀ odi láti fi sèrántí ìṣẹ́gun rẹ̀ tako ikọ̀ ológun Tibetan-Mongol. Ní ọdún 1951, ìjàm̀bá iná sàkọlù sáwọn ohun atọ́kasí ìtàn tó sẹ́kù ní Drukgyal Dzong, bí i àwòrán Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal. Lẹ́yìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ iná, wọ́n dá ààbò bo àgọ́ náà, bẹ́ẹ̀ni wọ́n pa á mọ́, èyí tó mún un jẹ́ ọ̀kan gbòógì ohun afanimọ́ra ní ìlú Bhutan.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village). It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces. In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal. After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni Ile-iṣẹ Dutch East India koṣe ni akoko wo ni Taiwan? | Which of the following did the Dutch East India Company not do during their time in Taiwan?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ Taiwan ní 15th century níbi tí àwọn awakọ̀ ojú omi Europe gbà kọjà ṣàkọsílẹ̀ orúkọ island na gẹ́gẹ́ bí IIha Formosa, tàbí island tó rẹwà. Ní ọdún 1624, ilé-iṣẹ́ Dutch East ní ilẹ̀ India se àgbékalẹ̀ ibùdó ní gúúsù ìwọ̀ oòrùn Taiwan, èyí tó mún ìyàtọ̀ bá iṣẹ́ ọ̀gbìn àgbàdo tí àwọn ọmọ onílẹ̀ ń se, tí ó sì tún fààyè sílẹ̀ fún gbígba àwọn òsìṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ China láti síṣẹ́ lórí okò ìrẹsì àti ṣúgà. Ní ọdún 1683, àwọn ọmọ ogun ìran Qing (1644-1912) gba àkóso agbègbèTaiwan western àti northern coastal wọ́n sì sọ Taiwan dí ìlú ti Qing Empire ní 1885. Lọ́dún 1895, lẹ́yìn ìparun ogun Sino àti Japan (1894-1895), ìjọba Qing buwọ́lu àjùmọgbà àláfíà Shimonoseki, nínú èyí tí ó ti gbé agbára kọja Taiwan fún Japan, èyí tó ń darí erékùsù títí dí odún 1945.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island. In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations. In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885. In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Mọọmọ jọwọ Taiwan fun ijọba Qing
[Verified Answer (English)]: Willing cede control of Taiwan to the Qing dynasty

[Reading Passage (English)]: "Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa. There are no particular ""rainy"" and ""dry"" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year."

search_context: Awọn aririn-ajo oni iṣuna owo le fẹ lati yẹra fun iru ohun mimu wo? | Budget conscious travelers may want to avoid which type of beverage?
pedagogical_answer:

Omi ẹ̀rọ agbègbè dára láti mu, ṣùgbọ́n omi inú ìgò rọrùn láti rí tí o bá bẹ̀rù. Fún àwọn ara ìlú Australia, àbá coffee “flat white” jẹ́ ti ìlú òkèrè. Àwọn omi éso gbówó lórí, ṣùgbọ́n wọn dára.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "The main local beer is 'Number One', it is not a complex beer, but pleasant and refreshing. The other local beer is called ""Manta"". There are many French wines to be had, but the New Zealand and Australian wines might travel better. The local tap water is perfectly safe to drink, but bottled water is easy to find if you are fearful. For Australians, the idea of 'flat white' coffee is foreign. A short black is 'espresso', cappuccino comes heaped high with cream (not froth), and tea is served without milk. The hot chocolate is up to Belgian standards. Fruit juices are pricey but excellent."

search_context: O pẹ fun awọn ọgọrun ọdun mẹta, ẹgbẹ wo ni o bẹrẹ ijọba amunisin? | Lasting for three centuries, the period of colonization was started by which group?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn ènìyàn Guarani ni wọ́n jẹ́ ènìyàn ìbílẹ̀ tó ń gbé ibi tó jẹ́ ìlà oòrùn Paraguay báyìí, wọ́n ń gbé bí i apwọn ọdẹ tí ó tún siṣẹ́ ohun ọ̀gbìn alárojẹ. Ẹkun ti Chaco jẹ ile fun ọpọlọpọ ẹgbẹ awọn ẹya abinibi bi Guaycurú ati Payaguá, ti o jẹ iṣẹ ọdẹ ṣiṣe ati ẹja pipa ni won yan laayo. Ní sẹ́ntúrì kẹrìndínlógún, Paraguay tí wọ́n pè ní “Agbègbè Nlá tí Indíaì” ni wọ́n bií látàrí láti ìpàdé àwọn aṣẹ́gun ilẹ̀ Spain pẹ̀lú àwọn ęgbẹ́ ìbílẹ̀. Àwọn ará Spain bẹ̀rẹ̀ àkòkò ìsèjọba amúnisìn èyí tó pẹ́ tó sẹ́ńtúrì mẹ́ta. Láti ipile Asensioni ní 1537, Paragueti gbìyànjú láti pa púpọ̀ nínú ìwà àti ìyàtọ̀ rẹ̀ mọ́.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "The Guaraní were the most significant indigenous group inhabiting what is now Eastern Paraguay, living as semi-nomadic hunters who also practised subsistence agriculture. The Chaco region was home to other groups of indigenous tribes such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, who survived by hunting, gathering and fishing. In the 16th century Paraguay, formerly called ""The Giant Province of the Indies"", was born as a result of the encounter of Spanish conquerors with the native indigenous groups. The Spaniards started the colonization period which lasted for three centuries. Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has managed to keep a lot of its indigenous character and identity."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn Spaniṣi naa
[Verified Answer (English)]: The Spaniards

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìrìn afẹ́ ò wọ́n fáwọn èrò tó bá pọ̀, torínà bí o bá ń dábọ̀ tàbí tí o bá wà pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ́ rọ kanṣoṣo, gbìyànjú láti bá àwọn míìràn pàdé kí ẹ sì se àkójọ ẹgbẹ́ eléèyàn mẹ́rin sí mẹ́fà fúnrayín kí ẹ lè rí owó tó mọ níwọ̀n san léèyàn kọ̀ọ̀kan. Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, èyí kò yẹ kó pò ọ́ lọ́fun pọ̀, nítorí ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà ní wọ́n má ń da àwọn arìnrìn àjò afẹ́ papọ̀ sínú àwọn ọkọ̀. Ń se ló dàbí ọ̀nà ati má a tan àwọn ènìyàn jẹ́, kíwọ́n lè gbàgbọ́ wípé wọ́n nílò àti má a sanwó sí i.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate. However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars. It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Wiwa ẹgbẹ mẹrin
[Verified Answer (English)]: Finding a group of four

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, kini o ṣafikun ilu mọọka San Francisco ni agbaaye? | According to the passage, what contributed to San Francisco’s worldwide recognition?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Níwọn ìgbà tí aje San Francisco sopọ mọ bó ṣe jẹ́ ibi ti gbogbo arìnrìnajo àgbáyẹ nífẹsí, ajẹ́ rẹ jẹ́ oníruurú. Àwọn ẹka tó ń gbanisíṣẹ́ jùlọ ní àwọn akọ́ṣẹ́-mọṣẹ́, ìjọba, ìnáwó, ìsòwò àti ìrìn àjò afẹ́. Ìfihàn àwòrán rẹ lóorèkòorẹ́ nínú orin, ẹrẹ́, lítírẹ́sọ̀ àti àsa olókìkí ti ran Ìlu náà áti sọ ámí rẹ di mímọ̀ ní gbogbo àgbáyẹ́. San Francisco ti ka ilé ńlá fún àwọn tó rìnrìn àjò wá sí ìlú yẹn pẹ̀lú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ilé ìtura, ilé óúnjé, àti ibi tí wọ́n ti lè ṣe ìpàdé. San Francisco jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn ibi tó dára jù ní orílẹ̀èdè fún oúnjẹ ilẹ Asia; Korean, Thai, Indian, àti Japan.
[Reading Passage (English)]: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified. The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism. Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world. San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities. San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Wiwa ni oriṣii ibi iṣẹ ọna ati midia
[Verified Answer (English)]: A frequent presence in various forms of art and media

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, irufẹ arinrin-ajo wo ni koni jẹ anfani lilo awọn iṣẹ aṣoju irin-ajo? | According to the passage, which type of traveler is not likely to benefit from using a travel agent’s services?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ríra àyè sílẹ̀ ní inú ọkọ̀ máa ń fún àwọn arìnrìnàjò ní ìbàlẹ̀ ọkàn pé àwọn yóò rí ibi sùn sí tí àwọn bá gúnlẹ̀. Àwọn tó ma n ṣaájò ìrìn àjò ma n ṣòwò pẹ̀lú àwọn ilé ìtura, biotilejepe o ṣeéṣe ki o gba àyè míìn sílẹ̀, bii ọgbà ikapo, nípasẹ̀ àwọn tó ma n ṣaájò ìrìn àjò. Àwọn aṣojú Ilé iṣẹ́ arìnàjò máa ń sábà pèsè àwọn ẹ̀dínwó pẹ̀lú oúnje àárọ̀, àwọn ètò ìrìnà lílọ/pípadà láti pápakọ̀ òfuurufú tàbí àkójọpọ̀ èdínwó fífò ọkọ̀ òfuurufú àti ilé ìtura . Wọ́n tún lè fi ààyè sílẹ̀ fún ọ bí o bá nílò láti ronú lórí ìpèsè tàbí kí o gba àwọn àkọ́ọ̀lẹ̀ mìíran fún ibi tí ò ń lọ (àpẹrẹ. ìwé ìrìnnà). Koko fi awon atunse tabi ibeere kan kan lo osise aajo irin ajo, ki o to fi lo ile itura naa.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Booking in advance gives the traveller peace of mind that they will have somewhere to sleep once they arrive at their destination. Travel agents often have deals with specific hotels, although you may find it possible to book other forms of accommodation, like camping grounds, through a travel agent. Travel agents usually offer packages that include breakfast, transportation arrangements to/from the airport or even combined flight and hotel packages. They can also hold the reservation for you if you need time to think about the offer or procure other documents for your destination (e.g. visa). Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Arinrin-ajo ti o saba maa n ṣe ohun ni pajawiri
[Verified Answer (English)]: A traveler prone to spontaneity

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, kini awọn ohun ti ohun elo ogbufọ atẹjiṣẹ oju akoko kole ṣe? | According to the passage, what are real-time text translator applications not capable of?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Apu komputa to n tumo ede lesekese - awon ero komputa to le da tumo odindi apa eyo oro lati ede kan si omira. Àwọn ìwé ìfisọwọ́ tí ó wà ni àbẹ́ ìsòrí yìí lè sọ ọrọ̀ tí ó wà jí kíkọ sílẹ̀sí èdè ilẹ̀ òkèrè lórí àmì tàbí àwọn nǹkan mìíràn ni ojú ayé nigbàtí ẹni náà bá kọ ojú ẹrọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ìgbàlóde sí àwọn nǹkan náà. Àwọn èrọ atúmò èdè ti dárasi láìsí ánì-àní, pèlú níbàyí o ń fi ìtumọ̀ èdè dárá ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà (àti ìwòmba àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ díẹ̀ tí kò ní ìtumọ̀), sùgbọ́n àwọn àyẹ̀wò díẹ̀ se pàtakì nítorí wọ́n lè gbe gbági. Ọkàn lára àwọn ohun èlò pàtàkì áàpù yí ni atúmọ̀ èdè Google tó fi aàyè gba Ìtùmò láìsí ẹ̀rọ ayélujára lẹ́yìn tí a ti se igbàsílè ẹ̀dà èdè tó wuni.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Real-time text translator apps – applications that are capable of automatically translating whole segments of text from one language into another. Some of the applications in this category can even translate texts in foreign languages on signs or other objects in the real world when the user points the smartphone towards those objects. The translation engines have improved dramatically, and now often give more or less correct translations (and more seldom gibberish), but some care is due, as they still may have gotten it all wrong. One of the most prominent apps in this category is Google Translate, which allows offline translation after downloading the desired language data.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Iṣogbufọ daadaa ni igba ida 100
[Verified Answer (English)]: Translating correctly 100% of the time

search_context: Ewo ninu awọn atẹle yii ni kii ṣe okunfa fun awọn ọpọ yinyin? | Which of the following is not a trigger for avalanches?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Iji yinyin kii se ohun ajeji, oke to ga o le di yinyin pupo ju, eyi to ba koja afara lo ma n wa sile gege bii iji yinyi. Ìṣòro ibẹ̀ ní pé yìnyín náà ma ń lẹ̀, nítorínà ó nílò okùnfà láti jẹ́ kó wálẹ̀, àti pé kí yìnyín ma wálẹ̀ lé fa ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kan fún àwọn ènìyàn. Nígbà míràn ètò tó má ń dùn ún wò ní bí òòrùn se ń yọ́ yìnyín, lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà àwọn yìnyín ma ń se sí i, ìgbàmíran ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àdáyébá, tàbí lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà ti ènìyàn.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Avalanches are not an abnormality; steep slopes can hold only so much slow, and the excess volumes will come down as avalanches. The problem is that snow is sticky, so it needs some triggering to come down, and some snow coming down can be the triggering event for the rest. Sometimes the original trigging event is the sun warming the snow, sometimes some more snowfall, sometimes other natural events, often a human.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Yinyin alẹmọra
[Verified Answer (English)]: Sticky snow

search_context: Kini idi ti a fi nilo yiyi ni ayika awọn oke-nla Transantarctic lati wa sori pẹtẹlẹ naa? | Why is a swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains required to get onto the plateau?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: The South Pole Traverse (tàbí òpópónà) jẹ́ 1600 km láti ibùdó McMurdo lóri Ross Sea sí Pole. Àwọn yìnyín tó ti là níwọn kó jọ, dí fi àwọn àsìá pààlà. Àwọn ohun ìkọlẹ̀ tí wọ́n ti se lọ́tọ̀ nìkan ló lè rìn ín, pẹ̀lú lílo ọkọ̀ fi wọ́ epo rọ̀bì àtàwọn ohun èlò. Oju opo yi ko jafafa to, itopa naa ni lati dojuko ibomiran ni agbegbe ori oke Transantarctic lati wa si petele.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The South Pole Traverse (or Highway) is a 1600 km trail from McMurdo Station on the Ross Sea to the Pole. It's compacted snow with crevasses filled in and marked by flags. It can only be traveled by specialized tractors, hauling sleds with fuel and supplies. These aren't very nimble so the trail has to take a long swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains to come onto the plateau.

search_context: Ewo ninu eyi ni kii ṣe itọkasi Timbuktu? | Which of the following is not an accurate description of Timbuktu?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Pelu pe o soro die lati de be, “Timbuktu” ti di apere ile alailegbe, jinjin. Lónìí ìlú òtòṣì ní Timbuktu, ṣùgbọ́n ó lorúkọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ibi tó ma n fẹjúmọ́ àwọn onirinajo, ó sì ní pápá ọkọ̀ òfurufú. Wọ́n sàfikún rẹ̀ sára àwọn àkọọ́lẹ̀ ibùdó ohun ìní àgbáyé tó wà nínú ewu lọ́dún 1990 látàrí ìdúnkokò àwọn yẹ̀pẹ̀ asálẹ̀. Ó jẹ́ ọ̀kan pàtàkì nínú àwọn ibi tí Henry Louis Gates’ PBS ti dúro nígbà tí ó ń wo àrà tí ó wà ní ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀. Ìlú náà yàtọ̀ gédégbé sí àwọn ìlú orílẹ̀èdè yòókù, nítoríwípé ó fara pẹ́ Áràbù ju àwọn adúláwọ̀ lọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Combined with its relative inaccessibility, ""Timbuktu"" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands. Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport. In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands. It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World. The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African."

[Verified Answer (English)]: It’s inaccessible by plane

search_context: Igba wo ni wọn fi Olimpiki igba ooru si?  | When were the summer Olympics originally scheduled?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìdíje paralympics máa wáyé láti ọjọ́ kẹ́rìndínlógún oṣù kẹjọ sí ojọ́ karùn ún oṣù kẹsàn án ọdún 2021. Oríṣìíríṣìí ibi ni àwọn ètò yóò ti máa wáyé jákèjádò Japan. Tokio màá jẹ́ ìlú Asia kan soso to sàlejo Olimpiki àkókò ọ̀run méjì torí wọ́́n salejo re ní ọdún 1984. Tó bá jẹ́ wípé o ti pè fún ìwé ìrìnnà ojú òfúrufú àti iléègbé fọ́dún 2020 kí wọ́n tó kéde ìsúnsíwájú, o lè wà nípò ẹ̀tàn. Ofin ifagile wa ni otooto, sugbon ni ipari Erena opo ofin ifagile to dale ori aarun Korona o ni sun de Agemo 2020, igba ti won kosile pe won maa se Olimpiki. A ti mọ̀ pé púpọ̀ nínú àwọn tíkẹ́tì fún party ma ń jẹ́ ¥2,500 àti ¥130,000, pẹ̀lú irú tíkẹ́tì kanáà tó jẹ́ ¥7,000.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The Paralympics will take place from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Some events will be held in other locations throughout Japan. Tokyo will be the only Asian city to have hosted two summer Olympics, having hosted the games in 1964. If you booked your flights and accommodation for 2020 before the postponement was announced, you may have a tricky situation. Cancellation policies vary, but as of late March most coronavirus-based cancellation policies don't extend to July 2020, when the Olympics had been scheduled. It's expected that most event tickets will cost between ¥2,500 and ¥130,000, with typical tickets costing around ¥7,000.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Oṣu keje 2020
[Verified Answer (English)]: July 2020

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ni inu ile, nitori wipe a ma n ni ifarakinra pelu opolopo kokoro aifojuri, o seese ki a ti ni ajesara si won. [Reading Passage (English)]: At home, due to this constant exposure to the local germs, odds are very high that you're already immune to them. As with respiratory problems in colder climates, intestinal problems in hot climates are fairly common and in most cases are distinctly annoying but not really dangerous.

search_context: Ewo ninu atẹle yii ni o jẹ anfani ti irin-ajo laarin agbegbe Schengen? | Which of the following is an advantage of traveling within the Schengen zone?

[Reading Passage (English)]: Europe is a continent that is relatively small but with many independent countries. The Schengen zone, however, works somewhat like one country in this respect. As long as you stay in this zone, you can generally cross borders without going through passport control checkpoints again. Similarly, by having a Schengen visa, you do not need to apply for visas to each of the Schengen member countries separately, hence saving time, money and paperwork.

[Verified Answer (English)]: Avoiding multiple passport control checkpoints

search_context: Kini a ko le ri ni iboji Tutankhamun mọ? | What can no longer be found in the tomb of Tutankhamun?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Itẹ́ òkú Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 lè jẹ́ itẹ́ tó gbajúmọ̀ jùlọ ní orí pẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀, àwárí ìran Howard Carter's 192, tó jẹ́ ibi sàárè tó lọ́lá jùlọ fún ọba kékeré. Ní síse àfiwé rẹ̀ sáwọn ibi ìtẹ́ òkú àwọn ọlọ́lá sí, àmọ́ṣà, ìtẹ́ òkú Tutankhamun kò yẹ ní ohun tí à ń sàbẹ̀wò sí, níbí ó se kére jù pẹ̀lú ìdálọ́lá tí kò pọ̀. Ẹni tí ó bá wù láti rí èrí ìpalára sí mummy ni ìgbà tí wọ́n ń gbìyànjú láti yọ ọ́ kúrò ní inú pósí, yóò banújẹ́, nítorí orí àti èjìká ni ó ṣe é rí. Ọrọ̀ ńlá inú ibojì kò sí níbẹ̀ mọ́, sùgbọ́n wọ́n ti gbe lọ sí ilé ìkó iṣẹ́ ọnà sí ni Cairo, ní ilẹ̀ Egypt. Ó ma dáa kí àwọn àlejò tí o ní àkókò púpọ̀ lògbà wọ́n níbò miin.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king. Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration. Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible. The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo. Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn ọrọ
[Verified Answer (English)]: The riches

pedagogical_answer:

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Victoria Falls je ilu ni agbegbe iwo oorun Zimbabwe eyi ti o la enu ibode lati Livingstone, Zambia koja eyi ti o sunmo Botswana. Ìlú náà tẹ̀dó ní kété sí àwọn ìdàwálẹ̀ omi, àti wípẹ́ wọn jẹ ibi ìfamọ́ra pàtàkì, sùgbón ibi ìdúrósí olókìkí fún àwọn arìnrìnàjó yìí pẹ̀sẹ̀ ànfàní lọ́pọ̀lọpọ̀ fùn àwọn arìnrìnàjó ìgbafẹ́ àti ẹ̀rò ìwòran dúró pípẹ́. Ní àsìkò òjò, (oṣù kọkànlá sí oṣù kẹta), ìwọn omi yíó pọ̀ sí tí ìjáwásílẹ̀ yíò sí dàbí àrà. Mo fi dá ọ lójú pé tí o bá fi lè sọdá afárá náà tàbí rìn lẹba ọ̀nà lásìkọ òjò, gbogbo ara rẹ lo máa tutù. Ní ìdàkejì, nítorí bí omi náà se pọ̀tọ́ ní yóò mun nira fún ọ láti rí bí omi se ń dà—pẹ̀lú gbogbo omi.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana. The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay. In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic. You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls. On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Lẹhin saa ojo
[Verified Answer (English)]: Outside of the rainy season

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, ewo ni a ko gba ni imọra bi a ba n lo duroni lati ya fiimu? | According to the passage, which of the following is not recommended when using a drone to film?
pedagogical_answer:

Ti o ba n lo drooni, ṣaridaju nkan ti wọn gba ẹ laye lati yaworan rẹ ati awọn iwe aṣẹ ti o ye ki o gba. Ẹ̀rọ tó ń káwòrán sílẹ̀ lójú òfúrufú tó fò lẹ̀gbẹ́ pápá ọkọ̀ òfurufu tàbi lórí èrò kì n sábà jẹ́ èrò tó dáa, biotilejepe kò lòdì sí òfin ní agbègbè ę.

If just taking a photo of something isn't allowed, then you shouldn't even think of recording a video of it. If using a drone, check well in advance as to what you are allowed to film and what permits or additional licensing are required. Flying a drone near an airport or over a crowd is almost always a bad idea, even if it's not illegal in your area.

search_context: Dida lori oju iwe naa, ewo ninu alaye yii nipa amuyẹ iforukọsilẹ fun ilana iwe irinna ni kii ṣe otitọ? | Based on the passage, which statement regarding the registration requirement for the visa process is not true?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìforúkọsílẹ̀ jẹ́ àfikún tí a nílò fún ìṣètò visa. Ní àwọn orílẹ̀ èdè kànkan, o ní láti forúkọsílẹ̀ fún wíwá rẹ àti àdírẹ́sì ibi tí ò ń gbé fún àwọn tó wà ní ipò àṣẹ sílẹ̀. Ó se é se kí èyí béèrè sísàkọọ́lẹ̀ fọ́ọ̀mù pẹ̀lú olopa agbegbe tabi sàbẹ̀wò sí ọ́fìsì àwọn aṣíkiri. Ni ọpọ orilẹede to ni iru ofin naa, awọn ile itura kekeke ni wọn ma moju to iforukọsilẹ( ri daju pe o bere). Ní ìgbà mìíràn, àwọn tó ń gbé ní ìta ilé ìgbé àwọn-onírìnkiri afẹ́ nílò láti fi orúkọ sílẹ̀. Síbẹ̀, èyí kò jẹ́́ kí òfin náà wà ní gbangba, torí náà kí o wádìí saájú.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Registration is an additional requirement for the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and address where you are staying with the local authorities. This might require filling out a form with the local police or a visit to the immigration offices. In many countries with such a law, local hotels will handle the registration (make sure to ask). In other cases, only those staying outside of tourist accommodations need to register.  However, this makes the law much more obscure, so find out beforehand.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Gbogbo awọn orilẹ-ede nilo iforukọsilẹ pẹlu awọn alaṣẹ agbegbe
[Verified Answer (English)]: All countries require registration with the local authorities

pedagogical_answer:

search_context: Ṣiṣe ewo ninu awọn atẹle yii ni yoo ṣẹdinku iṣelẹ ikọlu ẹranko? | Doing which of the following would decrease the likelihood of an animal attack?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Lóòtọ́, ó ti mọ́ ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ẹranko tó wà nínú ààyè lára láti má a rí àwọn èèyàn, àwọn ohun abẹ̀mí inú igbó jẹ́ tigbó, tí kò si yẹ kí wọ́n má a fún wọn ní oúnjẹ́ tàbí dàwọn láàmùn. Gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn aláṣẹ ibùdó ṣe sọ, jẹ́ kí ó kéré tán ọgọ́rùn ún ọ̀pa ìwọ̀n wà láàárín àgbọ̀nrin àti ìkokò àti ìwọ̀n ọ̀pá márùndínlógún sí àwọn ẹranko ìgbẹ́ tí ó kù! Ko si bi oju won se le rele to, bisoni, elki, moosi, esi ati gbogbo eranko nla le doju ko en. Ní ọdọdún, àwọn àlejo tó tó méjìlá ló ṣèṣe nítorí wọn kò fi àyè sílẹ̀ dáadáa. Àwọn eranko wọ́nyí tóbí, wọ́n sí le gan, wan sí léwu, nítorínà fún wọ́n ní àyè wọn. NÍ àfikún, mọ̀ pé òórùn ma ń fa béárì àti àwọn ęranko inú igbó mìíràn, torínáà yàgò fún gbígbé tàbi síse àwọn oúnjẹ́ tí ó ní òrùn púpọ̀, jẹ́kí ibi ìpàgọ́ rẹ mọ́ tótó nígbàgbogbo.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed. According to park authorities, stay at least 100 yards/meters away from bears and wolves and 25 yards/meters from all other wild animals! No matter how docile they may look, bison, elk, moose, bears, and nearly all large animals can attack. Each year, dozens of visitors are injured because they didn't keep a proper distance. These animals are large, wild, and potentially dangerous, so give them their space. In addition, be aware that odors attract bears and other wildlife, so avoid carrying or cooking odorous foods and keep a clean camp.

[Verified Answer (English)]: Removing trash from a campsite

search_context: Kini Adehun Shimonoseki mu wa? | What did the Treaty of Shimonoseki establish?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ Taiwan ní 15th century níbi tí àwọn awakọ̀ ojú omi Europe gbà kọjà ṣàkọsílẹ̀ orúkọ island na gẹ́gẹ́ bí IIha Formosa, tàbí island tó rẹwà. Ní ọdún 1624, ilé-iṣẹ́ Dutch East ní ilẹ̀ India se àgbékalẹ̀ ibùdó ní gúúsù ìwọ̀ oòrùn Taiwan, èyí tó mún ìyàtọ̀ bá iṣẹ́ ọ̀gbìn àgbàdo tí àwọn ọmọ onílẹ̀ ń se, tí ó sì tún fààyè sílẹ̀ fún gbígba àwọn òsìṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ China láti síṣẹ́ lórí okò ìrẹsì àti ṣúgà. Ní ọdún 1683, àwọn ọmọ ogun ìran Qing (1644-1912) gba àkóso agbègbèTaiwan western àti northern coastal wọ́n sì sọ Taiwan dí ìlú ti Qing Empire ní 1885. Lọ́dún 1895, lẹ́yìn ìparun ogun Sino àti Japan (1894-1895), ìjọba Qing buwọ́lu àjùmọgbà àláfíà Shimonoseki, nínú èyí tí ó ti gbé agbára kọja Taiwan fún Japan, èyí tó ń darí erékùsù títí dí odún 1945.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island. In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations. In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885. In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Aṣẹ Japani lori Taiwan
[Verified Answer (English)]: Japan’s authority over Taiwan

search_context: Bawo ni wọn ṣe n ṣe iwọn ipele pH ninu kẹmika? | How is the pH level of a chemical measured?

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Eléyìí ni à ń pè ní pH apòògùn. O lè se asàmì pẹ̀lú lílo ohun ẹlẹ́rìndòdò pupa ti kábèjì. Omi kabeeji maa paro awo eyi dalelori oye asidi tabi besiki (alkalaini) to wa ninu kemika naa. Átọka ìwọ̀n áásìdì sàfihàn nípasè iyẹ Hydrogen ( H nínú pH) mólẹ́kù nínú kẹ́míkàli tí a sẹ àyẹ̀wò rẹ. Hydrogen ions jẹ́ protons tó ní electron tí wọ́n bọ́ lára wọn (nítoríHydrogen atoms ní proton kan àti electron kan).
[Reading Passage (English)]: This is called a chemical's pH. You can make an indicator using red cabbage juice. The cabbage juice changes color depending on how acidic or basic (alkaline) the chemical is. The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical. Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).

pedagogical_answer:

search_context: Ewo ninu alaye yii ni ko ṣalaye ihuwasi awọn kiniun? | Which of the following statements does not accurately describe the behavior of lions?

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Kìnìún ni ẹranko ológbò tó lajú jù, tí o máa n wà ní agbo ńlá tí a sì máa ń pè ní olólà ijù. Àkójọpọ̀ kínìú jẹ́ akọ métà, pẹ̀lú ọgbọ̀n abo àti àwọn ọmọ wọn. Àwọn obìnrin wọn ma ń súma ara wọn, nítorí wọ́n jẹ́ ẹbí tó tóbi tóní àwọn ọmọ obìnri. Àwọn àkópọ̀ kìnìhún máà wùwà bí àpẹ́jọpọ̀ ìkookò tàbí ajá, ìyanilẹ́nu ló jẹ́ wípẹ́ awon ẹranko bi kìnìhún (àmọ́ tí kì í se àwọn olóńgbò tó tóbi) ní ìhùwàsí, pẹ̀lú pé wọ́n léwu fún àwọn ẹranko ìjẹ..
[Reading Passage (English)]: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides. Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs. The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters. Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ihuwasi wọn jọ ti awọn ologbo nla miiran
[Verified Answer (English)]: Their behavior similarly to other big cats

search_context: Awọn ehoro jẹ ẹran apajẹ fun awọn irufẹ awọn ẹran aṣọdẹ wo? | Rabbits are a common prey for what type of predator?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn olóógbò kéèké tó má ń jẹ àwọn àpajẹ kéèkèé bẹ̀rẹ̀ láti orí ehiri lọ sí ìgalà àti àgbọ̀nrín. NÍgbẹ̀yìn, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn olóógbò kéèké (nínú èyí tí olóógbó igbó wà) ó má ń jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àpajẹ bíi kòkòrò, èkúté, aláǹgbá àti ẹyẹ. Àṣírí àṣeyọrí wọn ní ìmọ̀ nípa níṣì, iṣẹ́ àkànṣe tí ológbò kookan lè ṣe láyì díje pẹ̀lú àwọn míì.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer. Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds. The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn ologbo ti ko tobi ju
[Verified Answer (English)]: Medium-sized cats

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni kii ṣe ọna ti ologbo igbo n gba ṣọsẹ? | Which of the following is not a part of an ocelot’s hunting method?
pedagogical_answer:

Bí i gbogbo ẹranko ti olóńgbo jẹranjẹran fi n ṣe ọdẹ rẹ ni o kẹ́rẹ́ juu lọ. Àwọn onímọ̀ sáyẹnsì gbàgbọ́ pé àwọn Osiloti ma ń fí oorun wá àti tẹ̀lé eranko tí wọn fẹ́ jẹ. Wọ́n ríran dada ní òkùnkùn pẹ̀lú iràn òkùnkùn àti pe wọn ma n yọ́ rìn náà. Àwọn Osiloti ma n pa àwọ̀ da láti bá àyíká rẹ̀ rẹ́ kó ba lè bà léàwọn eranko tí wọ́n ma jẹ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is. Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground. They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Wọn maa n pa awọn ẹran kekeeke jẹ nikan
[Verified Answer (English)]: Only preying on animals of a smaller size

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni a o ni ka si okun amọtẹkun? | Which of the following would not be considered a tiger’s greatest strength?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Eléré ìje tó dá ń tọ́, ẹkùn lè gùn ún (ó lè má tọ̀ọ́ dáadáa)lúwẹ̀ẹ́, fo ibi tó jínna, bẹ́ẹ̀ ló lè fa ohun tí èèyàn tó sángun lè fà fún ìgbà márùn ún. Ẹkùn náà wà nínu ẹgbk kanáà (Genus Panthera) gẹ́gk bí kìnìú, àmọ̀tékù, àti olóngbò ńlá. Àwọn olọ́ngbò mẹrin wọ̀nyí nìkan ló lè dún. [Reading Passage (English)]: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human. The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar. The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Oge gigun
[Verified Answer (English)]: Climbing

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, kini Robert Hooke ṣe ṣaaju awọn onimọ bioloji miiran? | According to the passage, what did Robert Hooke do before other biologists?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Seeli je eya ara (awon) alaye to kere ju to ni itosona ati ise. Seeli wa lati oro Latiini cella to tumo si iyara kekere. Tí ẹ bá wo àwọn nǹkan ẹlẹ́mìí nínú ẹ̀rọ-awòjìji-amóhun-bín-tín-fẹ̀, a máa rí pé láti ara nnkan onígun tàbí nǹkan roboto ni a ti ṣẹ̀dá wọ. Robaati Hooki, Olùmọ̀ bayọ́lọ́jì láti ìlú Gẹ̀ẹ́sì, ri skwia kekeke ninu kooki pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rọ mikroskopi. Wọn jọ iyàrá. Òun ní ẹni àkọ́kọ́ tí ó kọ́ sèwòye òòkú sẹ́ẹ̀lì.
[Reading Passage (English)]: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism. Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room. If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls. Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope. They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

pedagogical_answer:

[Reading Passage (English)]: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move. Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains). Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, ewo ninu awọn apẹẹrẹ wọnyi ni yoo ṣe idiwọ fun ilana itiranyan? | According to the passage, which of the following examples would hinder the process of evolution?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Nígbà tí ẹgbẹ́ kékeré nǹkan abẹ̀mí (tó kéré níye) bá yẹra kúrò lọ́dọ̀ àwọn olùgbé àkọ́kọ́ tíwọ́n ti wá (bí i kí wọ́n kúrò lórí òkè àbí odò tàbí tí wọ́n bá kó lọ sí erékùsù tuntun kí wọ́n má lè padà mọ́) wọ́n yíò ri wípé wọ́n bára wọn ní àyíká tó yàtọ̀ ju ibi tí wọ́n wà tẹ́lẹ̀ lọ. Agbègbè tuntun ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ohun àlùmọ́nì àti àwọn orogún òwò lóríṣìíríṣìí, fún ìdí èyí iye ènìyàn tuntun yóò nílò oríṣìíríṣìí nǹkan láti ní okun tí wọ́n fi lè kọjú àwọn tí wọ́n jọ ń sorogún. Ojúlówó iye kò yípadà rárá, wọ́n túbọ̀ nílò láti ṣe àmúlò ẹ̀da bíí ti àtijọ́. Bí àkókò ṣe ń lọ, bí àwọn olùgbé titun ṣe n yípadà sí àyíká wọn, wọn ò ní fibẹ́ẹ̀ jọ àwọn olùgbé tókù. Láìpẹ́, léyìn egberun tàbi mílíọ́nù ọdún, iye àwọn èèyàn náà ò ní jọra tó jẹ́ pé a ò lè pe wọ́n ní ęgbẹ́ alàyè kán náà. A pè ìṣètò yìí ní ẹ̀yà, èyí tó túms sí pé ẹ̀yà tuntun. Ẹ̀yà jẹ́ àtubọ̀tán tí a kò lè yẹra fún ó sì jẹ́ ǹkan pàtàkì fún ìtànkálẹ̀.
[Reading Passage (English)]: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before. This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before. The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before. Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population. Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species. We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn ẹgbẹ kekere ti wọn kọ lati gbeeru ni ibikan
[Verified Answer (English)]: A small group failing to thrive in a new location

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni o mu ẹni n sare lori yinyin ki o yi? | Which of the following causes a skater to turn?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Abẹ náà lórí síkààtì yìnyín ìgbàlódẹ́ ní igun olújúmẹ́jì pẹ̀lú ihò róbótó láàrin wọn. Àwọn igi méjèèjì fàyègbà láti di yìnyín mu dada, àní nígbàtí ó bá di títẹ̀. Nítorí wípé wọ́n yọgun díẹ̀ sí abẹ́ abẹfẹ́lẹ́, bí abẹfẹ́lẹ́ bá yí sí igun kan tàbí òmíràn, igun èyí tó fatakan yìnyín náà yó yọgun. Èyí fa kí àwọn tó ń fi ǹkan bí táyà rìn yí, tí ǹkan bí táyà náà bá yí sí apá ọ̀tún, ó ma yí sí apá ọ̀tún, tí ó bá yí sí òsì, ǹkan bí táyà náà ma yí sí òsì.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted. Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves. This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Igun kekere labẹ abẹ siketi
[Verified Answer (English)]: The slight curve on the bottom of the skate’s blade

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, ewo ni ilana ti o jẹki atọmu mu ọpọ agbara kuro ninu ina? | According to the passage, what is the process that allows atoms to eliminate excess energy from the light?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Láti padà sí ipò agbára titélè, wọn gbọdọ̀ mú ìfikún agbára èyí tí wọn gba láti ara ìmólẹ̀ kúrò. Bi won se ma n seyi nipe won a ma yo ina kekere ti an pe ni “foton.” Àwọn onímọ̀ sáyẹ́nsì ma n pè ní “stimulated emission of radiation” torí àwọn átọ́mù ma ń fura sí iná tó ràn èyí ṣokùn fa kí fotoni ina maa jáde,iná dẹ̀ jẹ́ irúfẹ́ redieṣọ́ni. Àwòrán tókàn ṣàfihàn atoms tó ń jáde láti photons. Lóòtọ́, ní ojú ayé photons kéré gan jú àwọn tí à ń rí nínu àwòrán. Àwọn ìwọn iná tún kéré ju àwọn n´ kan tó kórajọ di àwọn ìwọn nkan tó gba àyè tó kéré jùlọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light. They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a ""photon"". Scientists call this process ""stimulated emission of radiation"" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation. The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture. Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!"
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ti itujade ti riran
[Verified Answer (English)]: Stimulated emission of radiation

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, ewo lo le fa ti ina bọọbu fi duro iṣẹ? | According to the passage, what will eventually cause a light bulb to stop working?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Lẹ́yìn ọgarun wákàtí ìṣẹ́ ṣíṣe iná gílóbù ná jó kò sí ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́. Gílóòbù tí nílò à ti pààrọ̀. O sé pàtàkì láti kíyè sára bí a bá ń pààrọ̀ gílòbù. Àkọ́kọ́, ibí ti a ti ń tan iná ní láti wà ní pípa tàbí kí a yọ gbogbo wáyà iná náà dàn. Ìdí ni wípé iná tó ń gba ara ihò níbi tí apákan irin tí bọ́ọ̀bù wà le gbé ọ bí o bá fọwọ́ kan inú ihò àbí ti ibùjókòó irin bọ́ọ̀bù nígbàtí apákan rẹ̀ sì wà nínú ihò.
[Reading Passage (English)]: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works. The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb. First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected. This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ina inu bọọbu ti jo
[Verified Answer (English)]: The filament inside the bulb burning out

pedagogical_answer:

Wọ́n ran satalaiti ló sí spéèsì pẹ̀lú rokeeti. Àwọn onimo sayensi ma n lo teliskoopi ni sleesi nitori pe afẹ́fẹ́ ma n kóba ina wa ati nkan to ba ri. [Reading Passage (English)]: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite. The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly. The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view. It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Satalati 
[Verified Answer (English)]: Satellites

search_context: Lakoko wo ninu itan ni Jamani lo agbara igaba aṣa lori Estonia? | At what time in history did Germany exert a strong cultural influence on Estonia?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ní 15th Century, apá Àríwá Estonia ní ipa àṣà ìlú Germany. Awọn ará ilẹ̀ German mú Ọlọ́rún wá súnmọ́ àwọn ẹnìyàn ìbilẹ̀, torí náà wọ́n ṣe àgbékalẹ̀ èdè Estonia. Nitori alfabeeti Jamani ati okan ni won se fi “Õ/õ” kun. Níbí ọjọ́ se ń gorí ọjọ́, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ tí wọ́n yá láti Germany dirapọ̀ di ọ̀kan. Èyí ni ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ìlàlọ́yẹ̀.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany. Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language. It was based on the German alphabet and one character ""Õ/õ"" was added. As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Bi 600 ọdun sẹhin
[Verified Answer (English)]: Around 600 years ago

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, iye awọn olusọ ede Hindi ko ṣe deedee nitori idi wo? | According to the passage, the number of native Hindi speakers fluctuates based on which factor?

Èdè ìperí Hindi àti Urdu jọ ara wọn, ṣùgbọn ìyàtọ̀ wà nínú kíkọ wọn sílẹ̀;Nínú ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ojoojúmọ́, àwọn olùsọ̀ èdè méjèèjì lè gbọ́ ara wọn yé yéké.
[Reading Passage (English)]: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world. The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted. Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language. Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

[Verified Answer (English)]: If dialects very similar to Hindi are being counted

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, awọn ede wo ni Sanskrit nipa lori rẹ? | According to the passage, which languages have been influenced by Sanskrit?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ọ̀pọ̀ ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ nípa bí Sankrit se bẹ̀rẹ̀ ló wà. Ọkàn lára wọn ni ti asíkiri Aryan láti ìwọ̀ oòrùn lọ sí ilẹ̀ India tó mún èdè wọn wá pẹ̀lu wọn. Sanskrit jẹ́ èdè tó ti pẹ́ a sì lè fi wé èdè latin tí wọ́n ma sọ ní Europe. Iwe akọkọ ti a mọ ni agbaye ni wọn kọ pẹlu ede Sanskrit. Lẹyin akojọpọ Upanishads, Sanskrit sadede parẹ nitori eto igbelewon. Ede lile ati aladun ni Sanskriti, o ti wulo gege bi orisun opo ede Indiya igbalode, gege bii ede Latini se je orisun awon ede Yuropi bii Faranse ati Speen.
[Reading Passage (English)]: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them. Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe. The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy. Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn ede India
[Verified Answer (English)]: Indian languages

search_context: Bawo ni wọn ṣe kọ awọn ọrọ ti o wa lẹhin Ikede Ominira? | How are the words on the back of the Declaration of Independence written?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Bí o bá ti wo èré àgbéléwò National Treasure, wà á rò wípé àtọ́ka wúra wà ní kíkọ lẹ́yin ìkéde òmìnira ni. Àmọ́ṣá, èyí kò tọ̀nà. lóòótọ́ ohùn kan wà tí wọ́n kọ sí ẹ̀yìn àkọọ́lẹ̀, kìíse ìtọ́nisọ́nà wúra. Oro ti ako si eyin Ikede Ominira ni “Ojulowo Ikede ti Ominira eyi ti a se ni 4th July 1776”. Oro naa han ni isale iwe naa, ni adorikodo. Nígbàtí kò sí ẹni tí ó mọ pàtó ẹni tí ó kọ ọ́, ohun tí a mọ̀ ni pé ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀pẹ̀ ayé rẹ̀, ìwé àkọọ́lẹ̀ aláwọ ẹran tí ó tóbi (ó wọn tó 29¾ inṣi sí 24½ inṣì) ní wọ́n yí pamọ́. Torina o seese pe won fi akosile naa se lebeeli lasan.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence. However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map. Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words ""Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776"". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down. While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage. So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label."

[Verified Answer (English)]: Upside down

search_context: Iṣẹ Sealion ni wọn kogunja ni orilẹ-ede wo? | Operation Sealion was an invasion of which country?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Bí ogun ilẹ̀ Faransé tí ṣe parí, Germany bẹ̀rẹ̀ si ní gbaradì láti gbógun ti erékùsù ilẹ̀ Britain. Jẹmaní pẹ ìnajíjẹ́ àwọn ìkolù náà ní “Isẹ́ Sealion”. Ọmọ ogun IÌú Gẹ̀ẹ́si ti pàdánù ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ohun ìjà àti ìpẹ̀sẹ̀ ikan ogun rẹ nígbàtí o kójádẹo kúrò ní Dunkirk, fún ìdí èyí, ikọ̀ ọmọ ogun náà ti di alàílágbára. Ṣùgbọ́n ikọ̀ ológun orí omi Royal ṣì ní agbára ju ikọ̀ ológun orí omi ti Germany lọ (“Kriegsmarine”) Wọ́n sì le borí ìgbógun kí ìgbógun tí ẹkùn Gẹ̀ẹ́sì ìbá gbé wá. Amọ́ṣá, ìwọ̀nba àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ọlọ́ba ló wà lẹ́gbẹ̀ẹ́ ọ̀nà àkọlù níbí ẹ̀rù se ń ba àwọn ọ̀gágun pé àkọlù ojú òfúrufú ilẹ̀ Germany yíó bo àwọn mọ́lẹ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain. Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak. But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel. However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Orilẹ-ede Biriteni
[Verified Answer (English)]: Britain

search_context: Ewo ni a ko mẹnuba bii igbesẹ dandan ninu ipinnu Itali lati gba awọn orilẹ-ede Afirika? | What is not mentioned as a necessary step in Italy’s plan to capture African countries?
pedagogical_answer:

Lóòọ́tọ́ wọ́n sẹ̀sẹ̀ kọ́ àọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi tuntun mẹ́rin sáájú kí ogun tó bẹ̀rẹ̀, ó ní ikọ̀ ológun tí kò lágbára àti àwọn ikọ̀ ológun ojú omi tí kò ra jaja. Gbogbo aleba Itili je awon ilu Afirika. Lati ka awon ilu naa mo, won maa nilati ni ibi ti awon ajagun ti le gba lo ja, ki eon lr gba oju Osa Meditereniani lati lo kogun ja Afirika. Torí náà, wọ́n ni láti pa ibùdó àt ọkọ̀ ojú omi tí ilẹ̀ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì tó wà ní́ Egypt run . Yàtọ̀ sí àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ wọ̀nyí, kò yẹ́ kí ìjagun ojú omi ilẹ̀ Italy seohunkóhun. Nisin fun Japani, orileede irekusu ni Japani je, gege bii Briteeni.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the ""little brother"" of Germany and Japan. It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war. Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa. For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else. Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Kikọ awọn ọkọ si
[Verified Answer (English)]: Building additional ships

search_context: Tani o ṣagbekalẹ ibadọrẹ pẹlu awọn ajalulogun? | Who established friendly relations with invaders?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìfibalè ọjọ́ nla náà àti àwọn ogun tó tèle e lọ fún apá Àríwá ìlú Faransé ní òmìnira, súgbọn apá Gúúsù ò tìí di òmìnira. “Vichy” French ló ṣe adarí rẹ̀. Àwọn ará French niwọ́n tó fẹ́ àláfíà pẹ̀lú àwọn ará ìlú Germany ní 1940 tí wọ́n sì ṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú àwọn tó wá dabẹ̀ rú tí wọ́n kò pè dípò kí wọ́n bá wọn jà lọ. Ní ọjọ́ karùndínlógún oṣù kẹjọ ọdún 1940, Àwọn tó jẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́ wọnú ìlú southern France, wọ́n sí pé ìkọlù náà ní “Operation Dragon”. Ní ọ̀sẹ̀ méjì péré ikọ̀ ológun ilẹ̀ Americans àti Free France ti dóòlà ẹkùn gúúsù ilẹ̀ France, wọ́n sì ń padà sí ilẹ̀ Germany.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free. It was ruled by the ""Vichy"" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them. On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called ""Operation Dragoon"". In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Vichy Faranse
[Verified Answer (English)]: The Vichy French

search_context: Idagbasoke ti imọ-ẹrọ wo ni o fa awọn ọkọ inu-omi lati bẹrẹ irin-ajo labẹ omi? | The development of what technology caused submarines to start traveling under water?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: ọkọ̀ abẹ́ omi ni àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omí tí wọn ṣe láti máa rìn ní abẹ́ omi, kí wọ́n sì tún wà ní abẹ́ omí fún ìgbà púpọ̀. Wọ́n lo àwọn ọkọ̀ ìjagun ojú omi nínú ogun àgbáyé àkọ́kọ́ àti ogun àgbáyé kejì. Nígbà náà, wọ́n má ń lọ́ra gan won kò sì le yìnbọn níbi tí ó jìnnà. Níbẹ̀rẹ̀ ogun wọn sábà rín àjò lọ sí òkè òkun ṣùgbọ́n bí wọn ṣe n ṣẹ̀dá rédà tí ó pé si àwọn ọkọ̀ abẹ́ omi níláti jìn sínú omí kí wọ́n ma baà rí wọn. Àwọn ọkọ̀ ìjagun ojú omi ilẹ̀ Germany ni wọ́n ń pè ní U-Boats. Ilẹ̀ Germany dára púpọ̀ nínú à ń tukọ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ ìjagun ojú omi. Nítorí àṣeyọrí wọ́n pẹ̀lú àwọn ọkọ̀ inú omi kékèké, lẹ́yìn tí a kò gbọ́kànlé àwọn ọmọ ogun Germany láti ní púpọ̀ wọn.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time. Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range. In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen. German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines. Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Iwokiri
[Verified Answer (English)]: Radar

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn agbófinro ni Ohio sọ pé, Oníṣègùn tó ṣiṣẹ́ ni ilé ìwòsàn àwọn ọmọdé tí ó wà ní Pittsburgh, ni Pennsylvania ni wọn yóò fi ẹ̀sùn ìpànìyàn kàn lẹ́yìn tí wọn bá òkú ìyá rẹ̀ lẹ́yìn ọkọ̀ rẹ̀ ní ọjọ́rú. [Reading Passage (English)]: A doctor who worked at Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania will be charged with aggravated murder after her mother was found dead in the trunk of her car Wednesday, authorities in Ohio say. Dr. Malar Balasubramanian, 29, was found in Blue Ash, Ohio, a suburb approximately 15 miles north of Cincinnati lying on the ground beside the road in a T-shirt and underwear in an apparently heavily medicated state. She directed officers to her black Oldsmobile Intrigue which was 500 feet away. There, they found the body of Saroja Balasubramanian, 53, covered with blood-stained blankets. Police said that the body appeared to have been there for about a day.

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni kii ṣe ilana idibo Faranse? | Which of the following is not a part of France’s voting process?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ní ilẹ̀ Faranse, ètò ìdìbò ti di ìrírí tó kéré, àwọn olùdìbò ma ń yara wan sọ́tọ̀ nínú akoto, fi ìwé tó ń sàfihàn olùdíje dunpò wọn sínú àpò ìwé. Lẹ́yìn tí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ti ṣàrídájú olùdìbò, olùdìbò a fi ẹnfílópì sínú apoti ìbò a dẹ̀ fọwọ́ sí iwé ìbò. Òfin ìdìbò ilẹ́ Faranse se àgbéjáde ìlànà òfin lóní danda. Lati ọdun 1988, apoti idibo gbọdọ jẹ eyi ti o seeri fun awọn oludibo ati awọn oluworan lati ri wipe ko si apo iwe kankan ninu apoti ki idibo to bẹrẹ ati wipe ko si afikun apo iwe kankan yatọsi ti awọn oludibo ti a lu lonte. Àwọn olùkópa lè fi aṣojú wọ́n ránṣẹ́ láti jẹ́rìsí gbogbo ètò náà. Ní alẹ́, àwọ́n tó fi ara wọ́n sílẹ̀ ka àwọn ìbò pẹ̀lú àbójútó tó le, tó sì tẹ̀lé àwọn ìlànà kan pàtó.
[Reading Passage (English)]: In France, voting has traditionally been a low-tech experience: voters isolate themselves in a booth, put a pre-printed sheet of paper indicating their candidate of choice into an envelope. After officials verify the voter's identity, the voter drops the envelope into the ballot box and signs the voting roll. French electoral law rather strictly codifies the proceedings. Since 1988, ballot boxes must be transparent so that voters and observers can witness that no envelopes are present at the start of the vote and that no envelopes are added except those of the duly counted and authorized voters. Candidates can send representatives to witness every part of the process. In the evening, votes are counted by volunteers under heavy supervision, following specific procedures.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn ibi ti awọn aṣoju oludije ka
[Verified Answer (English)]: Votes counted by candidate representatives

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ní ilẹ̀ Faranse, ètò ìdìbò ti di ìrírí tó kéré, àwọn olùdìbò ma ń yara wan sọ́tọ̀ nínú akoto, fi ìwé tó ń sàfihàn olùdíje dunpò wọn sínú àpò ìwé. Lati ọdun 1988, apoti idibo gbọdọ jẹ eyi ti o seeri fun awọn oludibo ati awọn oluworan lati ri wipe ko si apo iwe kankan ninu apoti ki idibo to bẹrẹ ati wipe ko si afikun apo iwe kankan yatọsi ti awọn oludibo ti a lu lonte. Àwọn olùkópa lè fi aṣojú wọ́n ránṣẹ́ láti jẹ́rìsí gbogbo ètò náà. Ní alẹ́, àwọ́n tó fi ara wọ́n sílẹ̀ ka àwọn ìbò pẹ̀lú àbójútó tó le, tó sì tẹ̀lé àwọn ìlànà kan pàtó.
[Reading Passage (English)]: In France, voting has traditionally been a low-tech experience: voters isolate themselves in a booth, put a pre-printed sheet of paper indicating their candidate of choice into an envelope. After officials verify the voter's identity, the voter drops the envelope into the ballot box and signs the voting roll. French electoral law rather strictly codifies the proceedings. Since 1988, ballot boxes must be transparent so that voters and observers can witness that no envelopes are present at the start of the vote and that no envelopes are added except those of the duly counted and authorized voters. Candidates can send representatives to witness every part of the process. In the evening, votes are counted by volunteers under heavy supervision, following specific procedures.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Lori pepa ti wọn tẹ
[Verified Answer (English)]: On a pre-printed sheet of paper

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi Dr. Moll, kini o kan XDR-TB gbọngbọn? | According to Dr. Moll, what is most concerning about XDR-TB?
pedagogical_answer:

Ninu iforoworo kan, o wi pe irufe titun naa o n “danilamu pupo o de n fa ijaya nitoripe osuwon iku ti o le sokun fa, o ga.” Dokita Moli ro wipe awon alaisan kan leti fara ko kokoro naa ni ile-iwosan,ati wipe meji lara won je osise eleto ile-iwosan naa. Bí yíò bá fi di ọdún kan sí àkókò yìí, ènìyàn kan tó ní ààrùn lè kó o ran ẹni mẹ́wàá sí márùndínlógún mííràn tó bá ní ìfarakínra. Àmọ́ṣa, ìda XDR-TB nínú gbogbo àwọn èèyà tó ní ikọ́ àwúgbẹ sì kéré níye: ẹgbẹ̀rún mẹ́fà nínú èèyàn ọ̀jì lé lọ́ọ̀dúnrún ó dín mẹ́wàá ni ó ní lákòókò kan nílẹ̀ South Africa.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Dr. Tony Moll discovered the Extremely Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB) in the South African region KwaZulu-Natal. In an interview, he said the new variant was ""very highly troubling and alarming because of the very high fatality rate."" Some patients might have contracted the bug in the hospital, Dr. Moll thinks, and at least two were hospital health workers. In one year's time, an infected person may infect 10 to 15 close contacts. However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa."

pedagogical_answer:

Kí àwọn ológun tó dé, ìlú Haiti kò ì tí kojú ìsòro tí ó jọ́ mọ́ ààrùn yìí láti ọdun 1800. Ilẹ́-ẹ̀kọ́ fún òdodo àti ìjọba tiwantiwan ti Haiti ti tọ́ka sí àwọn ìwádìí olómìnira tí ó dá àbá pẹ́ ikọ́ ọmọ ogun ti Nepal fún àlàáfíà ní UN pẹ̀lú àìmọ̀ kó àrùn náà wọ Haiti. Danielle Lantagne, tí oh jẹ́ ògbóntarìgì fún UN lórí àìsàn, sọ pé àwọn onílàjà ni ó ṣe e ṣe kí wọn fa àjàkálẹ̀ ná.
[Reading Passage (English)]: UN peacekeepers, whom arrived in Haiti after the 2010 earthquake, are being blamed for the spread of the disease which started near the troop's encampment. According to the lawsuit, waste from the UN camp was not properly sanitized, causing bacteria to enter the tributary of the Artibonite River, one of Haiti's largest. Prior to the arrival of troops, Haiti had not encountered problems related to the disease since the 1800s. The Haitian Institute for Justice and Democracy has referenced independent studies that suggest the Nepalese UN peacekeeping battalion unknowingly brought the disease to Haiti. Danielle Lantagne, a UN expert on the disease, stated the outbreak was likely caused by the peacekeepers.
