search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, tani o yẹ ko gba beeli awọn ti wọn mu? | According to the passage, whose job is it to set bail for arrestees?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Láàrin oṣù mẹ́ta tó kọjá, àwọn bí i ọgọ́rin tí wọ́n fi páńpẹ́ òfin gbé ni wọ́n ti dásílẹ̀ kúrò ní ọgbà Central Booking láláì fojú balé ẹjọ́. Nínú osù kẹrin ọdún yí adájó Glynn pa àṣę ìkánilọ́wọ́kò onígbàkanná pé kí ilé iṣẹ́ náà tú àwọn tí wọ́n tí dè mọ́lẹ̀ fún wákàtí mẹ́rìnlélógún sílẹ̀ lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n gbà wọ́n sọ́dọ̀ tí wọn ò dę rí ìdájọ́ gbà láti ọ̀dọ̀ kọmíṣọ́nà kọ́ọ̀tú. Kọmíṣíọ́nà se àgbékalẹ̀ owó ìtanràn, tí ó bá bọ́ si, tí ó sì fì ẹ̀sùn tí agbófinró fi kàn múnlẹ̀. Ẹ̀sùn náà ni ó gbé wọnú ẹ̀rọ ayárabíàsá ìpínlẹ̀ tíwọ́n ti ń taná wádìí ẹ̀sùn náà. Ìgbẹ́jọ́ náa sàmí ẹ̀tọ́ afurasí sí ṣíṣe ęjọ́ ní kíá kíá.
[Reading Passage (English)]: In the last 3 months, over 80 arrestees were released from the Central Booking facility without being formally charged. In April this year, a temporary restaining order was issued by Judge Glynn against the facility to enforce the release of those held more than 24 hours after their intake who did not receive a hearing by a court commissioner. The commissioner sets bail, if granted, and formalizes the charges filed by the arresting officer. The charges are then entered into the state's computer system where the case is tracked. The hearing also marks the date for the suspect’s right to a speedy trial.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Kọmiṣọna ile ẹjọ naa
[Verified Answer (English)]: The court commissioner

search_context: Aami ẹyẹ wo ni wọn yan Emma Stone fun? | Which award was Emma Stone nominated for?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Fíìmú tó sàfihàn Ryan Gosling àti Emma Stone gba yíyàn nì gbogbo éka pàtàkì. Goslini àti Okuta yege fún ìbò Eléré Ọkùnrin àti Eléré Obinrin ní kọ̀kan wọn. Awọn ìsọ̀rí mìíràn ni, Àwòrán tó dára jù, Olùdarí, Àyàwòrán, Aṣaralóge, Asàtúntò-Fíìmù, Aṣàtúntò ohùn, Apohùnpọ̀, àti Akọ̀tà. Orin méjì látinú àgbéléwò, ìdánwò (Àwọn òmùgọ̀ tó ń lá àlá) àti ìlú àwọn ìràwọ̀ ni wọ́n mún fún orin ojúlówó tó dára jù. ilé ìsiṣẹ́ Lionsgate ló gba ìyànsípò mẹ́rìndínlọ́gbọ̀n — jú àwọn ilé ìsiṣẹ̀ mìíràn lọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The movie, featuring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone, received nominations in all major categories. Gosling and Stone received nominations for Best Actor and Actress respectively. The other nominations include Best Picture, Director, Cinematography, Costume Design, Film-editing, Original Score, Production Design, Sound Editing, Sound Mixing and Original Screenplay. Two songs from the movie, Audition (The Fools Who Dream) and City of Stars, received nominations for best original song. Lionsgate studio received 26 nominations — more than any other studio.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Oṣere ti o dara julọ
[Verified Answer (English)]: Best Actress

Hokuriku electric power co. jábọ̀ pé kò sí ipa kankan látara ilẹ̀ rírì àti pé àwọn ìsesí kìnní àti ìkejì sí ilé iṣẹ̀ tó ń pèsè agbára apanirun Shika ni wọ́n ti gbé tìpa. A gba pé àwọm ilé tó tó 9400 ní agbègbè náà wà láìsí omo àti pé àwọn tó tó 100 wà láìsí iná. Àwọn ọ̀nà kán ti bàjẹ́ wón to dá reluwé dúró níbi tó kàn Papa Ọkọ̀ Ofurufu Noto ní Iṣikawa wà ní títì.

It is reported that some 9400 homes in the region are without water and approximately 100 without electricity. Some roads have been damaged, railway service interrupted in the affected areas, and the Noto Airport in Ishikawa prefecture remains closed.

Another secondary containment area below the tanks capable of holding 104,500 barrels was not yet filled to capacity.

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àìsàn Red tide ma ń wáyé bí̀ Karenia brevis bá wọ́pọ̀ ju bí ó se yẹ lọ, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àdéyébá tí wọ́n pè ní kòkòrò inú omi. Àwọn ohun àdáyébá lè kórajọ láti pèsè ààyè tó dára, èyí tí yíó fún àwọn ewé yìí láàyè àti pọ̀ níye dáradára. Àwọn ewé ń pèsè oró tó lè sèpalára sọ́fun àwọn èèyàn àti ẹja. Eja maa n saba ku nitori awon oro to ropo ninu omi. Àwọn omi tí kò dára tí atẹ́gùn àti ìjì ti gbé lọ sínu afẹ́fẹ́ lè ṣe ìpalára fénìyàn tí ó bá fà á símú.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Red tide is caused by a higher than normal concentration of Karenia brevis, a naturally-occurring single-celled marine organism. Natural factors can intersect to produce ideal conditions, allowing this algae to increase in number dramatically. The algae produces a neurotoxin that can disable nerves in both humans and fish. Fish often die because of the high concentrations of the toxin in the waters. Humans can be affected by breathing affected water taken into the air by wind and waves.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Maa pọsi niye labẹ ipokipo
[Verified Answer (English)]: Increase rapidly in number under any condition

Ìyókù rẹ̀ má dàbí òjò ní island, ṣùgbọ́n kòsí omiyalé tí a ti gbọ́. Ìwọ́n ojò rírọ̀ náà, tó dé 6.34 ní Oahu, ní wọ́n ṣàpèjúwè gẹ́gẹ́ bí èyí tóní “àǹfàn.” Mọ̀nàmọ́ná tí ó ṣe dédé àti àrá ní ó tẹ̀lé díẹ̀ nínu òjò tí ó rọ̀.

The precipitation, reaching 6.34 inches at a gauge on Oahu, was described as ""beneficial"". Some of the rainfall was accompanied by thunderstorms and frequent lightning."

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Nínú àwọn ènìyàn egbèje tí wọ́n rí saájú ètò ìdìbò àpapọ̀ ọdún 2010, àwọn tí ó takoìdi orílẹ̀ olómìnira ilẹ̀ Australia láti ọdún 2008 fi ìdá mẹ́jọ pọ̀ si. Aladari ijoba fi’di he Julia Gillard so nigba ipolongo eto idibo ijoba apapo odun 2010 wipe oun gbagbo pe Autralia yio ni ominira ni opin isejoba Oba’binrin Elizabeth II. Ìdá mẹ́rìnlélọ́gbọ̀n àwọn tó wà níbi ìdìbò ló ní ìwòye yìí, pé kí Queen Elizabeth II jẹ́ orí adé ilẹ̀ Australia tó kẹ́yìn. Ní apá kan ní idìbo ìdámẹ́wa 29 ló wà àwọn ìwádí gbagbo wipe Ọstrelia mato di ripobiliki n gẹ́lẹ́ ti o ṢeéṢe idamewa 31 wipe kí Ostrelia ma di ripobiliki rara.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Out of 1,400 people polled prior to the 2010 federal election, those who oppose Australia becoming a republic grew by 8 per cent since 2008. Caretaker Prime Minister Julia Gillard claimed during the campaign of the 2010 federal election that she believed Australia should become a republic at the end of Queen Elizabeth II's reign. 34 per cent of those in the poll share this view, wanting Queen Elizabeth II to be Australia's last monarch. At the extremes of the poll, 29 per cent of those surveyed believe Australia should become a republic as soon as possible, while 31 per cent believe Australia should never become a republic.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Lẹhin iṣejọba Ọbabinrin Elisabẹti
[Verified Answer (English)]: After Queen Elizabeth II’s reign

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Sááju Ètò Ojoojúmọ́ àtì Àbábọ̀ Colbert, Heck àti Johnson ti ma ń wòye àgbéjáde tí yíó fara jọ ìròyìn—àti ìjábọ̀ ìròyìn—nígbàtí wọ́n jẹ́ akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ní UW ní 1988. Al Gore áti ọ̀gágun Tommy Franks láìfọtápè ka àwọn àkọlẹ́ ti´ oníkàlùkùn fẹ́ràn (Ti Gore jé ìgbà tí Onion sọ ìròyìn wípẹ́ òhun áti Tipper n ní ìbálòpọ̀ tó dàra jùlo ní ayé wọn lẹ́yìn ìjákulẹ̀ nínú ìdìbò fún ààrẹ áti igbá kẹji ti 2000). [Reading Passage (English)]: Long before The Daily Show and The Colbert Report, Heck and Johnson envisioned a publication that would parody the news—and news reporting—when they were students at UW in 1988. Since its inception, The Onion has become a veritable news parody empire, with a print edition, a website that drew 5,000,000 unique visitors in the month of October, personal ads, a 24 hour news network, podcasts, and a recently launched world atlas called Our Dumb World. Al Gore and General Tommy Franks casually rattle off their favorite headlines (Gore's was when The Onion reported he and Tipper were having the best sex of their lives after his 2000 Electoral College defeat). Many of their writers have gone on to wield great influence on Jon Stewart and Stephen Colbert's news parody shows.

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Wọ́n ti ti gbajúgbajà amòfin ilẹ Greek, Sakis Kechagioglou àti George Nikolakopoulos mọ́ àhámọ́ ọgbà ẹ̀wọ̀n Korydallus ti Athens, níbí wọ́n se ní wọ́n jẹ̀bi ẹ̀sùn ìwà jẹgúdújẹrá àti àjẹbánu. Fún ìdí èyí,wọ́n ti se àgbéga ìbanilórúkọjẹ́ ńlá tó wáyé láàrin ìlú Greek látara ìlàlójú sáwọn ìwà tí kò bófin mun táwọn adájọ́, agbẹ́jọ́rò, alágbàwí, àtàwọn amòfin ti hù láwọn ọdún tó ti kọjá sẹ́yìn. Ní ọ̀sẹ̀ díè sẹ́yìn, lẹyìn ìròyìn tí akọròyìn Makis Triantafylopoulos sẹ àtèjádẹ rẹ nínú gbajúgbajà àfihàn tẹlifísàn “Zoungla” ní Alpha TV, ọmọ ẹgbé ilẹ́ ìgbimọ̀ asòfin àti agbẹjórò, Petros Mantouvalos gba ìdáláre bi àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ míràn nínú ofiisi rẹ se lọ́wọ́ nínú ìwà ìbàjẹ́ àti ìlòdì sófin. Síwájú si, adájọ́ gíga Kalousis ti wà lẹ́wòn nítorí o jẹ̀bi èsùn íwá ájẹbánu àti íwá ìbàjẹ́.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "The famous Greek lawyers, Sakis Kechagioglou and George Nikolakopoulos have been imprisoned in the Athens' jail of Korydallus, as they were found guilty of graft and corruption. As a result of this, a big scandal within the Greek legal community has been raised through the exposure of illegal actions that judges, lawyers, solicitors and attorneys have done during the previous years. A few weeks ago, after the information published by the journalist Makis Triantafylopoulos in his popular Television show ""Zoungla"" in Alpha TV, the member of Parliament and lawyer, Petros Mantouvalos was abdicated as members of his office had been involved in illegal graft and corruption. Moreover, top judge Evangelos Kalousis is imprisoned as he found guilty of corruption and degenerate behaviour."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn akọroyin
[Verified Answer (English)]: Journalists

search_context: Ninu ipo wo ni o ṣee ṣe ki oluwa ọkọ ofurufu ti o ni aniyan ni anfani lati ni oye awọn iṣẹ inu ti ọkọ ofurufu? | In which situation would an anxious flyer be likely to benefit from understanding the inner workings of an aircraft?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ìriìn àjò nínú ọkọ̀ òfuruufú lẹ jẹ ìrírí ìjayà fún èyàn lóórẹkóórẹ, pàápàá júlọ tó bá jẹ pé wọn kò tìí fò télè tàbí wọn ti ní ìrírí tó banilérù. Kìi ṣe nkan ojútíti: kò yàtọ̀ sí àwọn ẹ̀rù bíbà àti ìkórira tí àwọn èyàn púpọ̀ ma n ní. Fún àwọn kan ẹ̀kọ nípa bí àwọn ọkọ̀ ofurufu kan ṣe má n ṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú nkan tó ma n ṣẹ́lẹ̀ nígbàtí ó n fò, lè bá wọn ṣẹ́gun ẹ̀rù bíbà tí ìpilẹ̀ rẹ̀ jẹ́ nkan àìmọ̀ tàbi àìlèṣàkóso.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Travelling by plane can be a scary experience for people of all ages and backgrounds, particularly if they've not flown before or have experienced a traumatic event. It is not something to be ashamed of: it is no different from the personal fears and dislikes of other things that very many people have. For some, understanding something about how aircraft work and what happens during a flight may help to overcome a fear which is based on the unknown or on not being in control.

Nígbà míràn, ìrìn-ajò ọkọ̀ òfuurufú kan náà lè ní àwọn ìdíyẹlẹ́ tó yàtọ̀ nípa onírúurú àkópapọ ìnáwó àti wípẹ́ o sànfàní láti se àfiwé àwọn èsì ìwádìí àti wíwọ ojú òpó ààyè ayélujára ilé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú òfúrufú kí ènìyà tó ra ààyè ìjókòó.

search_context: Nigba wo ni a nilo ẹlẹgbẹ lati tẹle ifijiṣẹ kan? | When is a companion required to accompany a delivery?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ tó ń fi ọjà/ẹrù ránṣẹ́ maha ń pa owó iyebíye láti fi nǹkan ránṣẹ́ ní kíakía. Lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà àsìkò ṣe pàtàkì púpọ̀ pẹ́lù àwọn ìwé ìdókowò, ọjà tàbí àwọn ẹ̀yà ara tí wọ́n fi tún nǹkan ṣe ní kíákíá. Ní àwọn òpópónà kan, àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ńlánlá ní ọkọ̀ ojú òfurufú wọn, ṣùgbọ́n ní àwọn òpópónà míràn àti ní àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ kékèké, wàhálà wà. Tí wọ́n bá fi ǹkan ránṣẹ́ nípa lílo ọkọ̀ òfurufú, ní àwọn ọ̀nà kan o lè gbà ọjọ́ díẹ̀ láti gbà ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ọlọ́pàá ojú ọ̀nà ìrìn àjò. Ona kan soso ti a le fi tete gbe wa ni ki a firanse gege bii eru ti won ti yewo. Awon ofin oko ofurufu o ni je ka fi eru ranse lai si onirinajo, ibe ni iwo ti ma buy.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Courier companies are well paid for delivering things quickly. Frequently, time is very important with business documents, merchandise or spare parts for an urgent repair. On some routes, the larger companies have their own planes, but for other routes and smaller firms there was a problem. If they sent things by air freight, on some routes it may have taken days to get through unloading and customs. The only way to get it through faster was to send it as checked luggage. Airline regulations will not allow them to send luggage without a passenger, which is where you come in.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Nigba ti wọn ba fohun kan ranṣẹ gẹgẹ bi ẹru ti a yẹwo
[Verified Answer (English)]: When things are being sent as checked luggage

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn páfuj Jamani dáa àti ní Baferia, wọ́n ki wọ́n dẹ̀ pe oríṣi , bíi tí Ostria tó wà lẹ́gbẹ́ wọn ní apá guusu. Èso apple ni wọ́n má ń fi se àfúnpọ̀ èso júlọ yípo ọdún, nígbà tí wọ́n má ń lo èso ṣẹrí àti púlọ̀mù lákòókò ooru. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ọjà German ni almonds, lpà, àti àwọn ẹ̀pa orí igi wà nínú rẹ̀. Àwọn àkàrà òyìnbó tí a mọ̀ dáadáa ní a lè jẹ́ pẹ̀lú ife coffee. Tí o bá fẹ́ àwọn ǹkan dídùn tó sì kún fún èròjà, gbìyànjú rẹ̀ wò ṣùgbọ́n ó dá lórí agbègbè bí Berliner, Pfannkuchen tàbí Krapfen.
[Reading Passage (English)]: German pastries are quite good, and in Bavaria, are quite rich and varied, similar to those of their southern neighbor, Austria. Fruit pastries are common, with apples cooked into pastries year round, and cherries and plums making their appearances during the summer. Many German baked goods also feature almonds, hazelnuts, and other tree nuts. Popular cakes often pair particularly well with a cup of strong coffee. If you want some small though rich pastries, try what depending on region are called Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Awọn Pulọmu
[Verified Answer (English)]: Plums

[Reading Passage (English)]: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that. Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter. For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel. The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.

search_context: Ẹwo ninu atẹle yii ni ko ṣalaye daadaa iwakọ laarin Point Marion ati Fairmont? | Which of the following statements does not accurately describe the drive between Point Marion and Fairmont?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ààyè tí ó wà láàrin Point Marion àti Fairmont se àfihàn àwọn ìpènijà àwọn awakọ̀ ní ojú ọ̀nà márosẹ̀ Buffalo-Pittsburgh, ní gbogbo igbà tí wọ́n bá gba àwọn ojú òpó tó dáwà kọjá. Tí wíwa ọks kò bá ma ẹ lára ní òpópónà , má sọ̀rọ̀ nípa ǹkan tí o lè ṣe. àwọn ọ̀nà tó lọ sókè tó tun lọ sílẹ̀, àwọn ọ̀nà tóró, àti ọ̀nà tó tẹ̀ borí. Òsùwọ̀n eré sísá tí a má ń kà sáàba má n kéré ju tàwọn agbọn àtẹ̀yìnwá lọ- lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà ó ma ń jẹ́ láàrin máìlì márùndínlógójì sí ogóji wákàtí kan (56mẹ́rìndínlọ́gọta-mẹ́rìnlélọ́gọ́ta kìlómítà wákàtí) - ati pe igboran pípe sí i se pàtàkì ju àìgbọ́ràn lọ. Ìyàlẹ́nu ló jẹ́ ná pé iṣẹ́ ẹrọ alágbèéká ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa ní ibíyìí ju ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn agbègbẹ̀ mìíràn lọ, bíi Aginjù Pennsylvania.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The stretch between Point Marion and Fairmont presents the most challenging driving conditions on the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Highway, passing frequently through isolated backwoods terrain. If you're not used to driving on country roads, keep your wits about you: steep grades, narrow lanes, and sharp curves predominate. Posted speed limits are noticeably lower than in previous and subsequent sections — commonly 35-40 mph (56-64 km/h) — and strict obedience to them is even more important than otherwise. Curiously, though, mobile phone service is much stronger here than along many other stretches of the route, e.g. the Pennsylvania Wilds.

pedagogical_answer:

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, kini o le ṣe iranwọ fun ẹni ti o n pinnu lati pagọ ninu ọkọ rẹ? | According to the passage, what would be helpful for someone planning to camp in their car?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Wíwọ ọkọ̀ rẹ, pẹ̀lú lílọ sí ọ̀nà jínjìn ní àyò abínibí ní ọ̀nà tó rọrùn . Yàtò sí àwọn ọkọ̀ ńlá, o seése kí o tí ní ìmọ̀lára ọkọ̀ rẹ , kí o sì mọ àwọn ìdiwọ̀n rẹ̀ . Síse àgbékalẹ̀ àgọ́ sórí ohun ìní ọlọ́danni tàbí ní ìlú le fa àfojúsí tí a kò fẹ́. Má fàá gùn lilo mọ́́tò ara eni dara fún irin ajo oju ona ṣùgbọ́́n fún ara re kii se ona lati fi “se ibud.” Ibudo inuoko seese ti o ba ni oko nla mnifaani, SUV abi Station Wagon to ni ijoko ti o le sun sile.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity. Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations. Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention. In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to ""camp"". Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ọkọ ti o gba fifa silẹ awọn ijoko
[Verified Answer (English)]: A vehicle that allows the seats to lay down

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju ewe naa, tabi o tun Casablanca kọ ni ẹkeji? | According to the passage, who rebuilt Casablanca the second time?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Apẹja Berber ní sẹ́ńtúrì kẹwàá ló sèdásílẹ̀ ìlú ìgbàlódé Casablanca, àwọn Phoenicians, Romans àtàwọn Merenidi ló sì lòó gẹ́gẹ́ bí i èbúté tí wọ́n pè ní Anfa. Àwọn ara ìlú Portugali parun wọn si tún sẹ àtúnkọ́ rè pélù orúkọ Casa Brance, kó tó di pé wọn tún sẹ àtúnkọ lẹ́yìn ìsẹ̀lẹ̀ ìwárìrì-ilè ní 1755. Sootani tún ìlú náà kọ gẹ̀gẹ̀ bi Daru I-Badya, àwọn ọlọ́jà ara Speeni to dá ọjà sílè níbẹ̀, sì fún ún ní orùkọ Kasablanka. Casablanca je okan lara awon ibi ti o kere ni ife lati raja ni gbogbo orile ede Morocco. Ní àyíká Medina àtijọ́, ó rọrùn láti rí àwọn ibi tí wọ́n ti ń ta àwọn ọjà ìbílẹ̀, gẹgé bi tangines, àmọkòkò. awọ hookah, àwọn onírúurú òdòdó, àmó, gbogbo rẹ̀ jẹ́ fún àwọn arìrìn-àjò..
[Reading Passage (English)]: The modern city of Casablanca was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and the Merenids as a strategic port called Anfa. The Portuguese destroyed it and rebuilt it under the name Casa Branca, only to abandon it after an earthquake in 1755. The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city as Daru l-Badya and it was given the name Casablanca by Spanish traders who established trading bases there. Casablanca is one of the least interesting places to shop in all of Morocco. Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.

search_context: Bawo ni awọn eniyan yoo ṣe de awọn ilu abule ni ẹkun Liguria? | How can people reach the remote villages in the region of Liguria?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Cinque Terre, èyí to túmọ́ sí Ilẹ́ Márùn, jẹ àkójọpọ̀ àwọn abúlé étíkun márùn ti Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernaxxa àti Monterosson tó wà nií agbẹ̀gbẹ̀ Liguria ti orílè-èdè Italy. Wo koruko won sile lori Iwe Ohun-Ini Agbaye UNESC. Ní ọarun ọdún sẹ́yìn, àwọn ènìyàn ti kọ́ ilé sí ibi tó lọlẹ́ tí wọ́n tẹ́ dé òké tó súmọ́ òkun. Lára àwọn ohun tó yáyì lára rẹ̀ ni pé kò sí ìdàgbàsókè kan tí ó ṣe rí. Ipa ọ̀nà, ọkọ̀ ojú irin, àti ọkọ orí omi ni ó lọ láti abúlé náà sí àwọn ìú mìíràn, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ọkọ̀ kò lè dé ọ̀dọ̀ wọn láti ìta.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Cinque Terre, which means Five Lands, comprises the five small coastal villages of Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza and Monterosso located in the Italian region of Liguria. They are listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Over the centuries, people have carefully built terraces on the rugged, steep landscape right up to the cliffs that overlook the sea. Part of its charm is the lack of visible corporate development. Paths, trains and boats connect the villages, and cars cannot reach them from the outside.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Lilo ọkọ oju irin tabi ọkọ oju omi
[Verified Answer (English)]: By train or boat

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, irufẹ buutu wiwọ wo ni o da fun ilẹ yiyọ lakoko igba otutu? | According to the passage, which type of boot is suitable for potentially slippery winter conditions?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Nkan to ma n saba sokunfa ijamba ni akoko otutu ni yiyo titi oloda, pepele (eba ona) ati paapa julo ona igbese. Ó kéré tán, o nílò bàtà tó ni ìtẹ̀lẹ̀ tó dára. Àwọn bàtà àkókò ooru ma ń yọ̀ lórí yìnyìn, kódà àwọn búùtù òtútù mìíràn kò daátó. Bátáni náà yẹ kí ó jìn tó mìlímítà márùn ún (ínṣì 1/5) tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ, bákan náà ni irúfẹ́ aṣọ náà dára fún ìgbà òtútù. Awon bata igbabolu kookan ni botini ni abebeeni awon botini alafikun wa fun awon ile ti o n yo, eyi ti o ba opolopo bata ati bata booti mu, fun abe ese tabi eyin ese ati abe bata. Ó yẹ́ kí gìgísẹ̀ lọlẹ̀, kó sì fẹ̀. Wọn a máa da iyanrìn, òkúta wẹ́wẹ́ tàbí iyọ̀ (calcium chloride) sí ojú ọnà tàbí ipa ẹsẹ̀ ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà láti jẹ́ kí ó dùn ún rì.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The most common cause for accidents in winter is slippery roads, pavements (sidewalks) and especially steps. At a minimum, you need footwear with suitable soles. Summer shoes are usually very slippery on ice and snow, even some winter boots are deficient. The pattern should be deep enough, 5 mm (1/5 inch) or more, and the material soft enough in cold temperatures. Some boots have studs and there is studded add-on equipment for slippery conditions, suitable for most shoes and boots, for the heels or heels and sole. Heels should be low and wide. Sand, gravel or salt (calcium chloride) is often scattered on roads or paths to improve traction.

[Verified Answer (English)]: Boots with studded equipment

search_context: Ewo ninu wọnyi ni ijọra deedee laarin Hawaii ati Awọn Erekuṣu Cook? | Which of the following is an accurate similarity between Hawaii and the Cook Islands?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Cook Island jẹ island orílẹ́ èdè tó wà ní ẹgbẹ́ ọ̀fẹ́ pẹ̀lú ìlú New Zealand, tó wà ní Polynesia, ní àárín South Pacific Ocean. O je asipelago to ni irekusu 15 kaakiri osa fun km2 mimionu 2.. Pẹ̀lú lílo àkókò kanáà pẹ̀lú Hawaii, àwọn erékùsù ma ń ro Hawaii gẹ́gẹ́ bí “Hawaii tó wà lábẹ́”. Bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́pẹ́ o kéré́, o se ìrántí fún àwọn àlẹjò àtijọ́ ilẹ̀ Hawaii kí a tó sọ di ìpínlẹ,̀ láìsí gbogbo àwọn ilẹ́ ìtura nlanla arìnrìn àjò ìgbafẹ́ àti àwọn ìdàgbàsókè míràn. Kò sí ìlú Kankan ní erékùsù Cook ṣùgbọn erékùsù mẹ́ẹ̀ẹ́dógún ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ ni ó ní. Awọn tí wọ́n ṣe pàtàkì jùlọ ni Rarotonga àti Aitutaki.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean. It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean. With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as ""Hawaii down under"". Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development. The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki."

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn erekùsù ìlà oòrùn adúláwọ̀ wà ní òkun India ní ìlà oòrùn adúláwọ̀. Ní ti àwọ̀n ẹranko, Madagáskà ló tóbi jù lo tó sì jẹ́ kọ́ntínẹ́ntì tí ó dá wà fún ara rẹ̀. Ilù olómìnira ní púpọ̀ nínú àwọn erekusu kékèké tàbí kí wọ́n níṣe pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Faranse, tí a tún mọ̀ wọ́n gẹ́gẹ́ bí risọ́tì etí òkun onígbádùn. Ìmúnisìn àti ipa àwọn ilẹ̀ Europe bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní sẹ́ńtùrì karùndínlógún, níbi ilẹ̀ Portuga se rin ìlú Vasco da Gama tí wọ́n rí ní Cape Route káàkiri láti Europe lọ sí India.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The East African Islands are in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa. Madagascar is by far the biggest, and a continent on its own when it comes to wildlife. Most of the smaller islands are independent nations, or associated with France, and known as luxury beach resorts. The Arabs also brought Islam to the lands, and it took in a big way in the Comoros and Mayotte. European influence and colonialism began in the 15th century, as Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama found the Cape Route from Europe to India.

[Verified Answer (English)]: A reputation for wildlife

pedagogical_answer:

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ecuador fẹ́ kí àwọn ará ìlú Cuban gba lẹ́tà ìpeni ṣáájú wíwọlé sí Ecuador ní ibùdókọ̀ ọkọ̀ òfurufú tàbí ibí ìgbaniwọlé. Iléeṣẹ́ tó ń rí sọ́rọ̀ ilẹ̀ okèrè ilẹ̀ Ecuadorian, kí wọ́n sì tẹ̀lé àwọn àlàkalẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan. Àwọn ohun tí a fẹ́ wọ̀nyí ni a gbé kalẹ̀ láti jẹ́ kí ìbáṣepọ̀ tí ó dá mọ́nrán wà láàárin orílẹ̀èdè méjèèj. Àwọn ọmọ orìlé-èdè Cuban tí wọ́n ní káàdì ìgbéèlú ní láti sàbẹ̀wò sí ọ́fíìsì asojú orìlé-èdè Ecuador láti gba ìyònda fún ètò ìmúlò yí. Ìwé ìrìnnà rẹ gbodò wà ní ìbámu o kéré tan osu mẹfa si àwọn ọjọ́ rínrin ìrin-àjò rẹ. Ìwé ìwọlé tọ péyẹ jẹ lílò làti sẹ èrí dídúró rẹ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points. This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements. These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries. Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Kaadi alawọ ewe Amẹrika
[Verified Answer (English)]: A US green card

search_context: Nipa lilo owo ni Falkland, ewo ninu awọn alaye wọnyi ni o jẹ otitọ? | Regarding the use of currency in the Falklands, which of the following statements is true?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Owó Falklands ni pọ́ùn Falklandtí (FKP) èyí tí iye rẹ̀ jẹ́ ìkan pẹ̀lú iye pọ́ùn ilẹ̀ Britain (GBP). Ilé ìfowópamọ́sí tó wà ní erékùsù ní Stanley káàkiri ibi ìtajà ìwọ̀ oòrùn FIC nìkan ni o ti lè pààrọ̀ owó. Ní gbogbo apa irekusu naa, wọ́n ma n gba Pọ́n ìlú Ọba pẹ̀lú ní ibi tí káàdì àwìn àti Dola Ìlú Amerika. Wọn lẹ má gba káàdì àwìn ní àwọn ìrékùsù tó wa ní pípépe, àmọ wọn lẹ gba àwọn owó ìlú Ọba àti ìlú Amèrìká, kọ́kọ́ sẹ àyèwo pèlú àwọn to ni ibè làti mọ nkan tí wọn lẹ gba gẹ́gẹ́ bii ìlànà ìsanwó. O fee je nkan ti o seese lati paro owo Falklandi nita awon irekusu naa, tori naa paro owo ki o to kuro ni awon irekusu naa.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The official Falklands currency is the Falkland pound (FKP) whose value is set equivalent to that of one British pound (GBP). Money can be exchanged at the only bank in the islands which is located in Stanley across from the FIC West store. British pounds will generally be accepted anywhere in the islands and within Stanley credit cards and United States dollars are also often accepted. On the outlying islands credit cards will probably not be accepted, although British and United States currency may be taken; check with the owners in advance to determine what is an acceptable payment method. It is nearly impossible to exchange Falklands currency outside of the islands, so exchange money prior to leaving the islands.

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ọ̀nà tí ó hànde jù láti gbé ọkọ̀ ojú òfúrufú fò ní kílàsì àkọ́kọ́ tàbí to ní olókoòwò ni láti mún owó tó jọjú jáde fún àǹfàní náà (tàbí èyí tí ó dára jù ni kí ó jẹ́ kí ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ kó bá a se). Síbèsíbè, èyí kò jẹ olówó póókú: gẹ́gẹ́ bí òfin oríowó, ní ìrètí làti san tó ìlọ́pó mẹrin ówó ìrinàjò mèúnù fún ti onísòwò, áti ìlọ́po mọ́kànlá fún ìpín kínní. Lákòótán, kòsí ǹkankan nínu wíwá ẹ̀dínwó fún òwò tàbí ìjókòó olówó ńlá ní ọkọ̀ òfurufù tó ń lọ tààrà láti A sí B. Àwọn ilẹ́ isẹ́ ọkọ̀ òfurufú mọ̀ dájú wípẹ́ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ arìnrìn àjò òfurufú tí wọ́n setán láti san ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ owó dọ́là fún ànfànì láti dẹ ibikíbi ní kíákíá àti pèlú ìrọ̀rùn, wọn si máà n gba ìdẹ́yẹlẹ́ tó bójúmu.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The obvious way of flying in first or business class is to fork out a thick wad of money for the privilege (or, better yet, get your company to do it for you). However, this does not come cheap: as rough rules of thumb, you can expect to pay up to four times the normal economy fare for business, and eleven times for first class! Generally speaking, there is no point in even looking for discounts for business or first-class seats on direct flights from A to B. Airlines know well that there is a certain core group of flyers who are willing to pay top dollar for the privilege of getting somewhere fast and in comfort, and charge accordingly.

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Awon ile ise oko oju ofurufu bi Emirates, Etihad Airways, Qatar Airways ati Turkish Airlines ti se afikun awon eto won si ile Adulawo, won ni eto irinajo losi opolopo ilu ti o gbaju-gbaja ni ile adulawo ni owo ti o din si ti awon akegbe won ni Europe. Ọkọ̀ ojú òfúrufú Turkey ma ń fò lọ sí ibùdó mọ́kàndínlọ́gbọ̀n àwọn orílẹ̀èdè ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀ ọgbọ̀n ní bí i ọdún 2014. Tí o bá ní àkókò díẹ̀ si, ṣàyẹ̀wò àpapọ̀ iye owó ọkọ̀ rẹ sí ti ilẹ̀ Africa pẹ̀lú owó ọkọ̀ ìrìn àjò káàkiri àgbáyé. Má gbàgbé làti se àfikún owó ìlé fún àfikún ìwẹ́ ìwọ̀lú, owó orí ìjádẹ nìlú, ìrìnnà lórí ilè, àti bẹ́ẹ̀bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ fún àwọn agbègbè tó kọjá ilẹ̀ Áfríká.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Airlines such as Emirates, Etihad Airways, Qatar Airways & Turkish Airlines have greatly expanded their services to Africa, and offer connections to many major African cities at competitive rates than other European airlines. Turkish Airlines flies to 39 destinations in 30 African countries as of 2014. If you have additional travel time, check to see how your total fare quote to Africa compares with a round-the-world fare. Don't forget to add in the extra costs of additional visas, departure taxes, ground transportation, etc. for all those places outside of Africa.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Iye owo iwe iwọlu Afirika kan
[Verified Answer (English)]: Cost of an African visa

Àwọn ọjà ǹkan orsiríṣi ní abala ti àwọn óúnjẹ tí wọ́n ti sè sílẹ̀ púpọ̀ si. Àwọn kan ti ẹ̀ pèsè ẹ̀rọ tó má mú óúnjẹ gbọ́ná tàbí ọ̀nà míràn tí o lè mú óúnjẹ gbóná. Láwọn oríléèdè kan, ó kéré tán ilé oúnjẹ orí ìtàkùn ayélujára yóó wà ju àwọn tìbílẹ̀ tó jẹ́ olówó tí kò gunpá lọ.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food. Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food. In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

search_context: Ewo ninu awọn atẹle ni o le ma ye awọn ara Belijiomu Faranse ati Swiss? | Which of the following might not be understood by French-speaking Belgians and Swiss?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Oríṣiríṣi èdè french tí wọ́n sọ ní ilé Belgium àti ilú Switzerland yàtọ̀ díẹ̀ sí èdè French tí wọ́n sọ ní France, ṣùgbọ́n wọ jọra. Ni pataki julo, eto sise onka ni apa to n so ede faranse ni Belgium ati Switzerland ni awon adayato kan to yato gedegede si ede faranse ti won n so ni orile ede Faranse, ati wipe iro opo ninu awon oro won yato si ara won. Àmọ́sá, gbogbo àwọn tó ń sọ faransé bí i àwọn ilẹ̀ Belgian and Swiss ni yí ò kọ́ ìlànà ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ilẹ̀ faransé, kí wọ́n lè gbọ́ ọ yé kódà bí o bá lo ìlànà òǹkà ilẹ̀ faransé.
[Reading Passage (English)]: The varieties of French which are spoken in Belgium and Switzerland differ slightly from the French spoken in France, though they are similar enough to be mutually intelligible. In particular, the numbering system in French-speaking Belgium and Switzerland has some slight peculiarities that are different from the French spoken in France, and the pronunciation of some words is slightly different. Nevertheless, all French-speaking Belgians and Swiss would have learned standard French in school, so they would be able to understand you even if you used the standard French numbering system.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ọna ipede ọrọ Faranse kan

pedagogical_answer:

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, kini idaniloju pe a so ọ mọ ọkọ oju omi ti o dara? | According to the passage, how can you guarantee you are matched with a suitable ship?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Fífi ọkọ̀ ojú omi wo ààyè àti awọn abẹ̀mí inú igbó Galapagos ló dára jùlọ, bí Charles Darwin se se ní ọdún 1835. Àwọn ọkọ̀ orí omi tó ń rin odò Galapagos – wà láti ìwọ̀n elérò mẹ́jọ sí ọgọ́rùn-ún. Ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn ló ma ń gbààyè sílẹ̀ saájú (torí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ti ma ń kún fọ́fọ́ láwọn àkókò tó ga). Mọ̀ dájú pé aṣojú tí o kọ sínú ìwé pàtàkì Galapagos pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ kíkún lórí ọ̀kanòjọ̀kan ọkọ̀ ojú omi. Eleyii yio ri daju pe awon ohun pato ti o ni ife si ati/tabi idiwo bamu pelu oko oju omi tio dara siwon jul.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835. Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers. Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season). Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships. This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Isanwo pẹlu ileṣẹ aṣoju ti o nimọ pẹlu irin-ajo Galapagos
[Verified Answer (English)]: Booking with an agent who specializes in Galapagos travel

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, ewo ni a kii lo gẹgẹ bi ọna lati mu ki awọn alejo ma ba ma ronu yiyan? | According to the passage, which of the following is not used as a tactic to keep guests gambling?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Àwọn ibi ìta tẹ́tẹ́ máa ń gbìyànjú láti ri dájú pé àlékún àsìkò àti owó tí àwọn àlejò wọn ń ná́. Fèrèsé àti ago kìí fi gbogbo ìgbà wà ní ibẹ̀, a sì máa nira láti rí ọnà tí ó jáde sí ìta. Ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà ni wọ́n máa ń ni oúnjẹ, omi àti ìdánilárayá pàtàkì tí ó yàtọ̀ kí àwọn alejò wọn lè máa dunnu kí wọn si fẹ́ lá ti wà ní sàkáni wọn. Awo ibo min ma n funyan ni oti mimu lofe. Sugbon, oti amuju ma n dinwo ogbon, ati pe awon to je ogbologbo ninu tete moo pe o se pataki lati ma mu oti.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Casinos typically make many efforts to maximize time and money spent by guests. Windows and clocks are usually absent, and exits can be hard to find. They usually have special food, drink and entertainment offers, to keep guests in a good mood, and keep them at the premise. Some venues offer alcoholic beverages on the house. However, drunkenness impairs judgement, and all good gamblers know the importance of staying sober.

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, ewo ninu ọrọ ni a n lo lẹta nla fun laarin gbolohun? | According to the passage, which part of speech is capitalized in the middle of a sentence?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Gbogbo ọ́rọ́ orúkọ pèlú ọ́rọ́ Sie fun ọ, nígbogbo ìgbà bẹ̀rẹ̀ pèlú lẹ́ta ńla, kò baa sẹ ní ààrin gbólohùn. search_context: "Ni awọn agbegbe igberiko ti Malaysia, iṣẹwọ wo ni o tumọ si ""wá""?" | In rural parts of Malaysia, which gesture means “come over”?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Láwọn agbègbè àgbáyé, jíjuwọ́ jẹ́ àfihan ìbánidọ́ọ̀rẹ́, tó sàfihàn “Bóon.” Síbẹ̀, ní Malaysia, pàápàá láàárin àwọn ará Malaysia tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko, ó túnmọ̀ sí “máa bọ̀” ó fi ara pẹ́ títẹ ọmọ ìka kèejì sọ́dọ̀ ara ẹni, iyi ara tí a sábà máa ń lò ní àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè ìwò-oòrùn kọ̀ọ̀kan, tí a sì gbọdọ̀ lò fún ìdí náà nìkan ṣoṣọ. Bee naa ni arinrin ajo ara ilu Geesi ni Speeni la sesi juwo pe odigba ki o koju owo re si ara re (dipo ki o koju owo re si eni ti o n juwo si) gege bi ifarajuwe lati pada wa.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "In many parts of the world, waving is a friendly gesture, indicating ""hello."" However, in Malaysia, at least among the Malays in rural areas, it means ""come over,"" similar to the index finger bent toward the body, a gesture which is used in certain Western countries, and should be used only for that purpose. Similarly, a British traveller in Spain may mistake a wave goodbye involving the palm facing the waver (rather than the person being waved at) as a gesture to come back."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ijuwọ
[Verified Answer (English)]: Waving

[Reading Passage (English)]: "In many parts of the world, waving is a friendly gesture, indicating ""hello."" However, in Malaysia, at least among the Malays in rural areas, it means ""come over,"" similar to the index finger bent toward the body, a gesture which is used in certain Western countries, and should be used only for that purpose. Similarly, a British traveller in Spain may mistake a wave goodbye involving the palm facing the waver (rather than the person being waved at) as a gesture to come back."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Ijuwọ ti atẹlẹwọ dojukọ ni
[Verified Answer (English)]: Waving with the palm facing inward

search_context: Dida lori oju iwe naa, awọn arinrin-ajo gbọdọ ṣọra gidi ni lilọ si awọn ibo? | Based on the passage, travelers should take additional precautions before visiting which location?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Goma jẹ́ ìlú ìrìn ajo nínú Olominira Kongo ní etí apá ìlà orùn lẹ́gbẹ́ Ruwanda. Ni 2002 Goma parun nitori lafa folkeno Nyiragongo tó ri púpọ̀ nínu títí ìlú pàpà jùlọ ilé ìjọ-ìlú. Nígbàtí Goma wà ní àbò, èyíkèyí àbẹ̀wò ní ìta Goma ní láti ní ìwádìí kíkún láti ní òye ìjà lemọ́lemọ́ ní agbègbè North Kivu. Ìlú náà ló tún jẹ́ ibùdó fún gígun ilẹ̀ ríru Nyiragongo pẹ̀lú ìtọpa Oríòkè Gorilla tó dínwó jùlọ nílẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. O lè lo boda boda (tákisí ọks alùpùpù) láti rìn kiri Goma. Iye rẹ̀ gangan ni 500 Congolese France fún ìrìn àjò kékeré náà.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda. In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre. While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province. The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa. You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Agbegbe yika Goma
[Verified Answer (English)]: Areas surrounding Goma

Wọn tí fi díè nínún áwọn ìwé àse pamó fún àwọn tó ba rìn wá sẹ bẹ̀rẹ̀r; o wà nílè fún ẹnikéni tó bá kọ́kọ́ wá.

Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month. Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan. Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations. There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

search_context: Gẹgẹ bi oju iwe naa, kini awọn arinrin-ajo ti o n lọ si Greenland gbọdọ yẹra fun? | According to the passage, what should be avoided by travelers visiting Greenland?

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Ọpẹlopé àsopọ̀ okùn fibre lábẹ́ òkun tsi Yuropi ati boolu gbohungbohun satelaiti, Greenland ní àsopọ̀ dada pẹ̀lú 93% àwọn èrò tó ráyè lo íńtánẹ̀ẹ̀tì. Agbàlejò tàbí ilé ìtura rẹ (tí o bá ń wà ní ilé ìgbàlejò tàbí ilé ẹnìkan) lè ní wifi tàbí íntánẹ́ẹ̀tì tí wọ́n sopọ̀ mọ́ ẹ̀rọ kọ́mpútà, àti pé gbogbo ilé ìgbàlejò lóní ìyàrá íntánẹ́ẹ̀tì tàbí ibi tóní wifi fún gbogbogbò. Bi a se daruko loke, biotilejepe ni ilu Amerika won gba ilo “Eskimo”, o si je eebu leti awon ti o ki n se ara Amerika - awon ara Atiki paa pa julo ni Kanada. O lè ma gbọ́ pé áwọn ará Grinlandikí se n ló oro náà, o yẹ kí àwọn àjèjì má a sọ́ra fún un. Àwọn ará ìlú Greenland ma ń pera wọ́n ní Inuit ní Canada àti Kalaalleq (ọ̀pọ̀ Kalaallit Greenlander ní Greenland. ọ̀ràn, àti èrò ibi sí àlejò, jẹ ohun tí wọn kò mọ̀ ni Greenland. Kódà ní ìlú náàm kò sí “agbègbè tó rí jákujàk.” Ojú ọjọ́ to tutù sẹésẹ́ ko jé ẹwu kan sọsọ tí aláìmúrasílè ma dojú kọ. To ba bẹ Grinlandi wo ni igba otutu (bi o ṣe n sumọ apa ariwa, o n tutu si i) o ṣe dandan fun ẹ lati mu aṣọ otutu to peye wa. Awon ojo to gun ju ni igba ooru le muu ki o soro lati ri orun to peye sun ati awon ailera bee. Ní àsìkò ooru, fojúsílẹ̀ pẹ̀lú fún àwọn ẹ̀fọn alárìnká. Bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé wọ́n kì ń tan àrùn ká, wọ́n a má a rìnyànláyà.
[Reading Passage (English)]: "Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access. Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi. As mentioned above, though the word ""Eskimo"" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada. While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners. The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland. Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no ""rough areas."" Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face. If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing. The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues. During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating."
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Itọkasi ọmọ ilu Greenland gẹgẹ bi “Eskimo”
[Verified Answer (English)]: Referring to a native of Greenland as an “Eskimo”

search_context: Dida lori oju iwe naa, ewo ninu awọn alaye atẹle yii ni kiiṣe otitọ nipa irin yinyin oojọ? | Based on the passage, which of the following statements about day hiking would be considered inaccurate?

[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Hiking jẹ́ eré ìta gbangba, tí ènìyàn máa ń ṣe, nípa rínrìn lórí ìlà rẹ̀. Ìrìn lójúmọmọ nííṣe pẹ̀lú rínrin ìrìn tí kò jìnnà ju máìlì kan lọ sí ààyè tí ó lè rìn lọ́jọ́ kan ṣoṣo. Fún rínrín ìrìnàjò lọ́nà ìtọpa tó rọrùn ìmúra díẹ̀ lo níló, àti wípé ẹnikẹ́ni tó dápé ní ìwọ̀ntuwọ̀nsì lẹ jẹ́ ìgbádùn wọn. [Reading Passage (English)]: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often on hiking trails. Day hiking involves distances of less than a mile up to longer distances that can be covered in a single day. For a day hike along an easy trail little preparations are needed, and any moderately fit person can enjoy them. Families with small children may need more preparations, but a day outdoors is easily possible even with babies and pre-school children.

search_context: Ibudo wo ni yoo dara loju arinrin-ajo ti o nifẹ si awọn itan amunisin erekusu? | Which location would appeal to a tourist interested in the island’s colonial history?
pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Irekusu Hon Kongi fun agbegbe Hon Kongi ni oruko re o de je ibi ti abewo pupo ma n dojuko ju. Àwọn àfihàn àwọn ilé tó mún kí ojú òpó Hong Kong rẹwà ni ati fi wé àtẹ tí ó ń dán èyí tó tàn nípa omi Victoria Harbour tó wà nílẹ̀. Láti lè rí Hong Kong dáadáa, fi island sílẹ̀ kí o sì lọ sí ibi omi Kowlon. Ọ̀pọ̀ nínú ìdàgbàsókè tí ó wáyé ní ìgboro erékùsù Hong Kong ni ó wọ́pọ̀ láwọn ilẹ̀ tí ó wà ní àríwá etí òku. Ibi tí àwọn amúnisin mú gẹ́gẹ́ bi tiwọn ni èyí, fún ìdí èyí, tí o bá ń wa ẹ̀rí nípa ìmúnisìn ní àtijọ́, ibi yìí ni ó dára láti bẹ̀rẹ̀.
[Reading Passage (English)]: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus. The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour. To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite. The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore. This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
[Verified Answer (Yorùbá)]: Eti odo Ariwa
[Verified Answer (English)]: The Northern shore

pedagogical_answer:
[Reading Passage (Yorùbá)]: Stirrups wa láti pèsè ìrànwọ́ fún èýkéyìí ẹsẹ̀ ẹni tí o ń wa kẹ̀kẹ́. Wọ́n sàgbékalẹ̀ ìdúró tó ga fún àwọn awakọ̀ àmọ́ wọ́n lè ní ààbò látarí pé ó se é se fáwọn awakọ̀ láti há sínú wọn. Bí wọ́n bá ju ẹni tó ń gun eṣin láti oríirẹ̀, à mó tí o fi ẹṣẹ̀ walẹ̀, wọ́n lè wọ́ tuurutu bí ẹṣin bá sálọ. Láti lè mún àdínkù bá ewu, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìlànà ààbò ni wọ́n lè gbé. Lákòókò ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn agunkèké máà n wọ bàtà gíga pèlú ìtèlè bàtà tọ dan tọ si tínrín. [Reading Passage (English)]: Stirrups are supports for the rider's feet that hang down on either side of the saddle. They provide greater stability for the rider but can have safety concerns due to the potential for a rider's feet to get stuck in them. If a rider is thrown from a horse but has a foot caught in the stirrup, they could be dragged if the horse runs away. To minimize this risk, a number of safety precautions can be taken. First, most riders wear riding boots with a heel and a smooth, quite narrow, sole. Next, some saddles, particularly English saddles, have safety bars that allow a stirrup leather to fall off the saddle if pulled backwards by a falling rider.

- English Sentence: Representatives of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Korea inside the Constitutional Court moments before the Court’s decision.

search_context: Iye àwọn tí orílẹ̀-èdè South Korea ń fi sẹ́wọ̀n lọ́dọọdún torí pé wọn ò ṣiṣẹ́ ológun nítorí ẹ̀rí ọkàn wọn ju àpapọ̀ àwọn tó ń lọ sẹ́wọ̀n ní gbogbo orílẹ̀-èdè yòókù torí pé ẹ̀rí ọkàn ò jẹ́ kí wọ́n ṣiṣẹ́ ológun. | South Korea has annually imprisoned more conscientious objectors than all other countries combined.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:

pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Ìgbà kan wà tó jẹ́ pé nǹkan bí ọgọ́rùn-ún márùn-ún (500) sí ọgọ́rùn-ún mẹ́fà (600) àwọn arákùnrin wa ló ń ṣẹ̀wọ̀n lọ́dọọdún.
- English Sentence: At one point, an average of 500 to 600 of our brothers went to prison every year.

search_context: Tí wọ́n bá sì dá wọn sílẹ̀ lẹ́wọ̀n, gbogbo wọn ni wọ́n máa ń níṣòro láwùjọ torí ẹ̀sùn ọ̀daràn tó ti wà lọ́rùn wọn, tí kò sì lè pa rẹ́. | Upon their release, all conscientious objectors carried with them a lifelong stigma due to their criminal record, which among other challenges limited their employment opportunities.

- English Sentence: Upon their release, all conscientious objectors carried with them a lifelong stigma due to their criminal record, which among other challenges limited their employment opportunities.

search_context: Ara ohun tó sì máa ń yọrí sí ni pé kìí jẹ́ kí wọ́n ríṣẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀. | Starting in 2011, however, some brothers filed complaints with the Constitutional Court because the law provided no option other than imprisonment for their stand of conscience.

search_context: Ni wọ́n bá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í gbé ẹjọ́ wọn lọ sí Ilé Ẹjọ́ Tó Ń Rí Sọ́ràn Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn, kí ilé ẹjọ́ náà lè tún Ìlànà Iṣẹ́ Ológun gbé yẹ̀ wò. | After having twice ruled (in 2004 and 2011) to uphold the Military Service Act, the Constitutional Court has finally agreed that change is needed.

- English Sentence: After having twice ruled (in 2004 and 2011) to uphold the Military Service Act, the Constitutional Court has finally agreed that change is needed.

search_context: Wọ́n ń fọ̀rọ̀ wá Hong Dae-il, tó jẹ́ agbẹnusọ fáwọn Ẹlẹ́rìí Jèhófà ní Korea lẹ́nu wò níwájú ìta ilé ẹjọ́ náà lẹ́yìn tí ilé ẹjọ́ ṣèpinnu Iṣẹ́ Ilé Ẹjọ́ Tó Ń Rí Sọ́ràn Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ni kí wọ́n máa wò ó bóyá òfin kan bá Òfin Ilẹ̀ Korea mu àbí ó ta kò ó. search_context: Àmọ́ ní báyìí, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ti Ilẹ̀ Yúróòpù ti dá àwọn arákùnrin wa láre. | Thus, the ECHR unanimously ruled in favor of the brothers.

- English Sentence: Thus, the ECHR unanimously ruled in favor of the brothers.

pedagogical_answer:

- English Sentence: Thankfully, Armenia’s position on conscientious objection has vastly improved since 2013.

search_context: Wọn ò fi àwọn arákùnrin wa sẹ́wọ̀n mọ́, kò sì sí àkọsílẹ̀ mọ́ pé wọ́n jẹ́ ọ̀daràn nítorí wọn ò dá sí tọ̀tún-tòsì. | Our brothers are no longer imprisoned or saddled with criminal records for their neutral stand.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Wọn ò fi àwọn arákùnrin wa sẹ́wọ̀n mọ́, kò sì sí àkọsílẹ̀ mọ́ pé wọ́n jẹ́ ọ̀daràn nítorí wọn ò dá sí tọ̀tún-tòsì.
- English Sentence: Our brothers are no longer imprisoned or saddled with criminal records for their neutral stand.

pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Láti bí ọdún méje sẹ́yìn, orílẹ̀-èdè Armenia ti ṣètò iṣẹ́ míì tí àwọn tí ẹ̀rí ọkàn wọn ò jẹ́ kí wọ́n ṣiṣẹ́ ológun lè ṣe, tí kò sì sí lábẹ́ ìdarí àwọn ológun rárá.
- English Sentence: For the past seven years, Armenia’s truly civilian ACS has been a model for other nations to adopt.

search_context: Àmọ́ ṣá o, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ti Ilẹ̀ Yúróòpù dá orílẹ̀-èdè Armenia lẹ́bi ní December 5 pé wọn ò tẹ̀ lé òfin àgbáyé ti ọdún 2012. | However, the ECHR’s December 5 judgment holds Armenia accountable for its failure to comply with international law in 2012.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Àmọ́ ṣá o, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ti Ilẹ̀ Yúróòpù dá orílẹ̀-èdè Armenia lẹ́bi ní December 5 pé wọn ò tẹ̀ lé òfin àgbáyé ti ọdún 2012.
- English Sentence: However, the ECHR’s December 5 judgment holds Armenia accountable for its failure to comply with international law in 2012.

search_context: Pẹ̀lú ìdájọ́ yìí, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ti Ilẹ̀ Yúróòpù ń sọ fún gbogbo ayé pé òun máa fìyà tó tó ìyà jẹ orílẹ̀-èdè èyíkéyìí tó bá tẹ òfin ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn àgbáyé lójú. | With this decision, the ECHR sends a clear message that it is willing to heavily penalize a country for violating international human rights laws.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Pẹ̀lú ìdájọ́ yìí, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Ẹ̀tọ́ Ọmọnìyàn ti Ilẹ̀ Yúróòpù ń sọ fún gbogbo ayé pé òun máa fìyà tó tó ìyà jẹ orílẹ̀-èdè èyíkéyìí tó bá tẹ òfin ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn àgbáyé lójú.
- English Sentence: With this decision, the ECHR sends a clear message that it is willing to heavily penalize a country for violating international human rights laws.

search_context: A dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ Jèhófà pé ó fún àwọn arákùnrin wa tó wà lórílẹ̀-èdè Armenia ní ìdáláre tó ṣàrà ọ̀tọ̀ yìí. | We thank Jehovah for granting our brothers in Armenia this extraordinary legal victory.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: A dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ Jèhófà pé ó fún àwọn arákùnrin wa tó wà lórílẹ̀-èdè Armenia ní ìdáláre tó ṣàrà ọ̀tọ̀ yìí.
- English Sentence: We thank Jehovah for granting our brothers in Armenia this extraordinary legal victory.

search_context: A gbàdúrà kí Jèhófà ṣí ọ̀nà sílẹ̀ fún àwọn arákùnrin wa lórílẹ̀-èdè míì láti má ṣe lọ́wọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ ológun tó jẹ́ dandan, kí wọ́n sì lè ní àǹfààní láti ṣe iṣẹ́ míì dípò iṣẹ́ ológun ní àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè tí kò tíì sí, bí Azerbaijan, South Korea, Turkey àti Turkmenistan. | We pray that it opens the way for our brothers in other lands to conscientiously object to compulsory military service and to have the option for alternative civilian service where it is not yet available, such as in Azerbaijan, South Korea, Turkey, and Turkmenistan.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: A gbàdúrà kí Jèhófà ṣí ọ̀nà sílẹ̀ fún àwọn arákùnrin wa lórílẹ̀-èdè míì láti má ṣe lọ́wọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ ológun tó jẹ́ dandan, kí wọ́n sì lè ní àǹfààní láti ṣe iṣẹ́ míì dípò iṣẹ́ ológun ní àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè tí kò tíì sí, bí Azerbaijan, South Korea, Turkey àti Turkmenistan.
- English Sentence: We pray that it opens the way for our brothers in other lands to conscientiously object to compulsory military service and to have the option for alternative civilian service where it is not yet available, such as in Azerbaijan, South Korea, Turkey, and Turkmenistan.

search_context: Ní July 6, 2018, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Barda lórílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan fìyà jẹ ọ̀kan lára àwọn arákùnrin wa tó ń jẹ́ Emil Mehdiyev, wọ́n sì fún un láwọn òfin tó gbọ́dọ̀ máa tẹ̀ lé fún ọdún kan gbáko tí kò bá fẹ́ ṣẹ̀wọ̀n. | On July 6, 2018, the Barda District Court of Azerbaijan ordered a one-year conditional sentence for one of our brothers, Emil Mehdiyev.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Ní July 6, 2018, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Barda lórílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan fìyà jẹ ọ̀kan lára àwọn arákùnrin wa tó ń jẹ́ Emil Mehdiyev, wọ́n sì fún un láwọn òfin tó gbọ́dọ̀ máa tẹ̀ lé fún ọdún kan gbáko tí kò bá fẹ́ ṣẹ̀wọ̀n.
- English Sentence: On July 6, 2018, the Barda District Court of Azerbaijan ordered a one-year conditional sentence for one of our brothers, Emil Mehdiyev.

search_context: Ilé ẹjọ́ sọ pé ọmọ ọlọ́dún méjìdínlógún (18) tó ń jẹ́ Emil yìí jẹ̀bi torí pé ó lóun ò wọṣẹ́ ológun, àmọ́ wọn ò rán an lọ sẹ́wọ̀n. | The court found 18-year-old Emil guilty of evading military service, but did not impose a prison sentence.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Ilé ẹjọ́ sọ pé ọmọ ọlọ́dún méjìdínlógún (18) tó ń jẹ́ Emil yìí jẹ̀bi torí pé ó lóun ò wọṣẹ́ ológun, àmọ́ wọn ò rán an lọ sẹ́wọ̀n.
- English Sentence: The court found 18-year-old Emil guilty of evading military service, but did not impose a prison sentence.

search_context: Ní báyìí, kò lè kó kúrò níbi tó ń gbé láìsọ fáwọn aláṣẹ, wọn ò sì jẹ́ kó kúrò lórílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan. | However, he cannot change his permanent address without notifying the authorities, and he is not allowed to leave Azerbaijan.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Ní báyìí, kò lè kó kúrò níbi tó ń gbé láìsọ fáwọn aláṣẹ, wọn ò sì jẹ́ kó kúrò lórílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan.
- English Sentence: However, he cannot change his permanent address without notifying the authorities, and he is not allowed to leave Azerbaijan.

search_context: Ní December 2017, wọ́n ránṣẹ́ pe Arákùnrin Mehdiyev ní Ẹ̀ka Tó Ń Gbani Síṣẹ́, Tó sì Ń Fani Wọṣẹ́ ní Agbègbè Barda. | In December 2017, Brother Mehdiyev reported to the Barda District Department of the State Service for Mobilization and Conscription.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Ní December 2017, wọ́n ránṣẹ́ pe Arákùnrin Mehdiyev ní Ẹ̀ka Tó Ń Gbani Síṣẹ́, Tó sì Ń Fani Wọṣẹ́ ní Agbègbè Barda.
- English Sentence: In December 2017, Brother Mehdiyev reported to the Barda District Department of the State Service for Mobilization and Conscription.

search_context: Àmọ́ ó kọ̀ láti tọwọ́ bọ̀wé ìwọṣẹ́ ológun, torí ẹ̀rí ọkàn rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kó ṣiṣẹ́ ológun. | He refused to sign the draft notice, as his conscience would not permit him to perform military service.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Àmọ́ ó kọ̀ láti tọwọ́ bọ̀wé ìwọṣẹ́ ológun, torí ẹ̀rí ọkàn rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kó ṣiṣẹ́ ológun.
- English Sentence: He refused to sign the draft notice, as his conscience would not permit him to perform military service.

search_context: Nígbà tí wọ́n tún ránṣẹ́ sí i, ó pa dà lọ ṣàlàyé fún wọn pé ẹ̀rí ọkàn òun ò ní jẹ́ kóun ṣiṣẹ́ ológun, ó sì ní kí wọ́n jẹ́ kóun ṣiṣẹ́ àṣesìnlú míì dípò iṣẹ́ ológun. | In response to a summons, he returned to explain his conscientious stand and requested alternative civilian service in lieu of military service.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Nígbà tí wọ́n tún ránṣẹ́ sí i, ó pa dà lọ ṣàlàyé fún wọn pé ẹ̀rí ọkàn òun ò ní jẹ́ kóun ṣiṣẹ́ ológun, ó sì ní kí wọ́n jẹ́ kóun ṣiṣẹ́ àṣesìnlú míì dípò iṣẹ́ ológun.
- English Sentence: In response to a summons, he returned to explain his conscientious stand and requested alternative civilian service in lieu of military service.

search_context: Wọ́n sọ fún un pé kò sírú iṣẹ́ yẹn, wọ́n sì sọ pé àwọn máa gbé ọ̀rọ̀ ẹ̀ lọ sí ọ́fíìsì olùpẹ̀jọ́ ìjọba ní Àgbègbè Barda. | He was told that this option was not available and that his case would be sent to the Barda District prosecutor’s office.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Wọ́n sọ fún un pé kò sírú iṣẹ́ yẹn, wọ́n sì sọ pé àwọn máa gbé ọ̀rọ̀ ẹ̀ lọ sí ọ́fíìsì olùpẹ̀jọ́ ìjọba ní Àgbègbè Barda.
- English Sentence: He was told that this option was not available and that his case would be sent to the Barda District prosecutor’s office.

search_context: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀pọ̀ atótónu nílé ẹjọ́ àti àìmọye sísún ẹjọ́ náà síwájú, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Barda dá a lẹ́bi, wọ́n sì fòfin dè é láwọn ọ̀nà kan. | After numerous hearings and adjournments, the Barda District Court convicted him and ordered the conditional arrangement.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀pọ̀ atótónu nílé ẹjọ́ àti àìmọye sísún ẹjọ́ náà síwájú, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Barda dá a lẹ́bi, wọ́n sì fòfin dè é láwọn ọ̀nà kan.
- English Sentence: After numerous hearings and adjournments, the Barda District Court convicted him and ordered the conditional arrangement.

search_context: Bó tiẹ̀ jẹ́ pé ilé ẹjọ́ ò rán Emil lọ sẹ́wọ̀n, ojú ọ̀daràn làwọn èèyàn á máa fi wò ó, kò sì rọ́gbọ́n dá sí i, torí pé ìjọba Azerbaijan ò tíì ṣètò iṣẹ́ àṣesìnlú títí di báyìí, bó tiẹ̀ jẹ́ pé tipẹ́tipẹ́ ni wọ́n ti ṣèlérí pé àwọn máa ṣe é. | Although the court did not sentence Emil to prison, he has no other recourse but to be viewed as a criminal because the government of Azerbaijan has still not instituted an alternative civilian service program, as it has long promised to do.
pedagogical_answer:
[Verified Translation (Yorùbá -> English)]:
- Yorùbá Sentence: Bó tiẹ̀ jẹ́ pé ilé ẹjọ́ ò rán Emil lọ sẹ́wọ̀n, ojú ọ̀daràn làwọn èèyàn á máa fi wò ó, kò sì rọ́gbọ́n dá sí i, torí pé ìjọba Azerbaijan ò tíì ṣètò iṣẹ́ àṣesìnlú títí di báyìí, bó tiẹ̀ jẹ́ pé tipẹ́tipẹ́ ni wọ́n ti ṣèlérí pé àwọn máa ṣe é.
- English Sentence: Although the court did not sentence Emil to prison, he has no other recourse but to be viewed as a criminal because the government of Azerbaijan has still not instituted an alternative civilian service program, as it has long promised to do.

- Yorùbá Sentence: Ní November 8, 2018, Àjọ Tó Ń Rí sí Ọ̀rọ̀ Iṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú Àwọn Ẹlẹ́sìn ní orílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan fọwọ́ sí i káwọn Ẹlẹ́rìí Jèhófà forúkọ ẹ̀sìn wọn sílẹ̀ lábẹ́ òfin délẹ̀délẹ̀ nílùú Baku, tó jẹ́ olú-ìlú Azerbaijan.
- English Sentence: On November 8, 2018, Azerbaijan’s State Committee for Work with Religious Associations granted Jehovah’s Witnesses full legal registration in Baku, the capital city of Azerbaijan.

search_context: Àwọn ará wa ti wá ní ẹ̀rí tó lẹ́sẹ̀ nílẹ̀ lábẹ́ òfin láti máa jọ́sìn ní gbangba, kí wọ́n sì máa wàásù fàlàlà ní ìlú náà. | Our brothers now enjoy a stronger legal basis to openly worship and preach in the city.

- English Sentence: Our brothers now enjoy a stronger legal basis to openly worship and preach in the city.

- English Sentence: We are thankful to Jehovah that favorable government officials have legally established our worship in Baku.—Philippians 1:7.

search_context: Ní October 31, 2018, Ilé Ẹjọ́ Kòtẹ́milọ́rùn nílùú Ganja lórílẹ̀-èdè Azerbaijan fọwọ́ sí ẹjọ́ tí ilé ẹjọ́ kan ti dá tẹ́lẹ̀ pé Arákùnrin Vahid Abilov, tó jẹ́ ọmọ ọdún mọ́kàndínlógún (19) jẹ̀bi torí pé ẹ̀rí ọkàn ò jẹ́ kó wọṣẹ́ ológun. | On October 31, 2018, the Ganja Court of Appeal in Azerbaijan upheld a lower court ruling to convict Brother Vahid Abilov, 19, for conscientious objection.

- English Sentence: In the opinion, the rights experts also denounce the courtroom tactics used to try our brothers.

- English Sentence: For example, during their pretrial detention extension hearings, two of the sisters were kept in cages in the courtrooms.

search_context: Nínú àlàyé táwọn onímọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ náà ṣe, wọ́n ní òfin àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè jẹ́ ká mọ̀ pé ẹ̀tọ́ ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ni “pé kí wọ́n fojú aláìmọwọ́mẹsẹ̀ wò ó, títí wọ́n á fi rí i dájú pé onítọ̀hún jẹ̀bi ẹsùn tí wọ́n fi kàn án.” | As the Working Group explains, international law recognizes the right of all persons “to be presumed innocent until proven guilty in accordance with the law.”
pedagogical_answer:

- English Sentence: For that reason, our sisters should not have been “shackled or kept in cages during trials or otherwise presented to the court in a manner indicating that they may be dangerous criminals.”
